From the Ekāmraka forest up to the shore of the southern ocean,

Jaimini said:
Then Brahmā went swiftly to where the Blessed Lord was present in person.
Just as he had seen the Lord at the conclusion of his hymn of praise, so he beheld him then.
Delighted by recognition upon beholding that Supreme Lord,
he became a treasure of the most wonderful knowledge, O best of brahmins.
As he began to praise him, his eyes blossoming with joy,
just then an excellent crow arrived from somewhere.
Plunging into that pool filled with water of mercy,
and beholding Mādhava, whose radiance is that of a blue sapphire, the treasure-house of compassion,
it cast off its crow body, rolling repeatedly upon the ground,
and, with conch, discus, and mace in hand, took its place at his side.
Seeing that destiny of a beast, which is very hard for lords of yogins to attain,
he thought, O sages: "Creation will gradually come to an end."
A doubt arose regarding the Vedānta teaching that liberation belongs to human beings alone:
"Indeed, nothing is difficult to attain here for a devotee of Viṣṇu.
He became visible, O best of brahmins, when the ancient Puruṣa appeared,

2.2.m: By You the world is sustained, by You it was created, and by You it is nourished. 17
In the form of the moon, the sun, and the rest, You constantly illumine the universe.
The Lord of the Universe, the source of the world, the abode of the universe, the teacher of the world, 18

Salutations to the ocean filled with the water of supreme compassion, 19
whose power transcends both higher and lower, who is the origin of the universe, 20
the sun to the frost of worldly misery, the friend of the wretched,
who produced the entire existence through His own māyā, the rope of the guṇas! 21
Salutations to Him whose pure yellow garment is like the filament of a lotus,
the discus-wielder whose discus cuts the shoulders of enemies in great battle, 22

Salutations to the Sacrificial Boar, whose eyes are the moon, sun, and fire, 23

by the mere play of whose side-glance creation, maintenance, and dissolution take place; 24

To that one, radiant like a dark cloud, whose body is of sapphire gem, 25

Salutations to You, whose eyes are refined by union with the side-glances of Kamalā,
whose broad chest captivates the mind, shining with the Śrīvatsa and the Kaustubha! 27-28

2.2.m: Then she was instructed by me: 'O auspicious one, fulfill my wish:

2.2.m: Maṅgalā at the root of the banyan tree, and Vimalā in the west;
Sarvamaṅgalā is situated at the back of the conch;
likewise, Ardhāṃśinī and Lambā are situated in the direction of Kubera;
Kālarātri in the south, and Marīcikā in the east;
and behind Kālarātri stands Caṇḍarūpā.
Protected by these fiercely-formed powers,
this place is very difficult to attain for a person of little merit.
From the darśana and the praise of these eight powers,
all sins are destroyed, and one obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
Seeing the eightfold division of Rudrāṇī, Rudra, who is Śaṃkara,
dividing himself into eight, worshipped the supreme Lord.
Having propitiated Viṣṇu through austerity, he asked for the supreme boon:

2.2.s: yatra tvaṃ deva tatrāhaṃ vaseyaṃ hi yathāsukham .. 48 ..

2.2.m: 'Wherever you are, O Lord, let me dwell there comfortably.

and Vaṭeśa at the root of the banyan tree—these eight liṅgas of the Great Lord,

2.2.m: “And over those who die in this sacred field, Yama has no power;
therefore accomplish elsewhere that purpose for which you have come.” // 54
Even so, that Lord of the Universe who surrenders himself to his devotee,
the Lord who removes the distress of the surrendered, was pleased with Yama by his devotion. // 55
By means of the Sudarśana discus he will veil his divine power
in this supreme sacred field that must never be abandoned, covered with golden sand. // 56

2.2.s: taṃ yamaṃ vaṃcayitvā tu prasthāpayya yamālayam ..

2.2.m: “In the Kṛta age there will be a king named Indradyumna,
a devotee of Viṣṇu, a performer of all sacrifices, and skilled in the sacred treatises. // 58
Having come here, the best of kings will show great devotion;
to please the Lord, a thousand horse-sacrifices // 59

arising from a single log of wood, he will manifest fourfold. // 2.2.4.60

and you, propitiated by Indradyumna, will indeed consecrate them. // 61
O Grandfather, the fashioning and consecration

2.2.s: tadrūpakā pratiṣṭhā hi ghaṭanā ca bhaviṣyati .. 62 ..

2.2.m: remembering again and again that majesty of the sacred field,
their bodies bristling with horripilation out of wonder and delight. // 64
Now, O sages, in that place, pleased by Indradyumna,
the glorious Lord bearing the conch and discus, resembling a dark raincloud, // 65
dwelling within the cave of Nīlācala, assuming a wooden body,
resides for the welfare of the world together with Bala and Subhadrā, // 66
accompanied by the Sudarśana discus fashioned of wood,
he who destroys the afflictions of those bowed in homage, an ocean of compassion. // 67
Upon seeing him, one is freed from the very firm bondage of sin;
the fruition of a multitude of good deeds arrives all at once. // 68
Behold, O best of sages, the treasure-trove of nectar for the three afflictions!
Many indeed are the divine and human descents of Viṣṇu, // 69
his exceedingly wonderful deeds and his majesty have been described;
yet because of familiarity, even the gods do not esteem humans. // 2.2.4.70
O brahmins, upon that wooden Hari,
the minds of gods, asuras, humans, gandharvas, serpents, and rākṣasas, // 71
and even of beasts, dwell—he who is the Self of all, bringing all happiness.
They live on the bliss of him whose nature is non-different [from the Self]; // 72
for Vedic speech says of Brahman: 'it is experienced right here.'
He destroys the sufferings of worldly existence and bestows imperishable bliss; // 73
therefore, Brahman made of wood is sung of in the Upaniṣads.

2.2.s: na hi kāṣṭhamayī mokṣaṃ dadāti pratimā kvacit .. 74 ..
2.2.d: न हि काष्ठमयी मोक्षं ददाति प्रतिमा क्वचित् .. 74 ..
2.2.m: An image made of mere wood never gives liberation anywhere; // 74
O brahmins, uncreated reality is never attained through that which is created.
How could uncreated liberation come from created wood? // 75
Without a physical substrate, the sovereign power of Brahman is not perceived;
this supreme secret is the unexcelled abode of Viṣṇu. // 76
That extraordinary image was manifested as ordinary.

2.2.s: kutra śrutā vā dṛṣṭā vā pratimā vyāharediti .. 77 ..
2.2.d: कुत्र श्रुता वा दृष्टा वा प्रतिमा व्याहरेदिति .. 77 ..
2.2.m: Where has an image ever been heard or seen to speak? // 77
He who possessed a wooden body then granted a boon to Indradyumna—
he who is the sole refuge of the poor and helpless, a crossing over the ocean of existence, // 78
whose feet are ever to be adored by all moving and unmoving beings, the supreme recourse.
[Take refuge in] Nārāyaṇa, the womb of the universe, the cause of creation and destruction,
the releaser from all sins, the shatterer of all calamities,
the dispenser of glories, the choice of all yogins,
the sustainer of all beings, the bearer even of the worlds,
the speaker of all languages, the rebuker of all evildoers,
the drier of all mud, Hari who has his refuge on the Blue Mountain (Nīlādri).
O sages, go for refuge indeed to that all-pervading Lord, who has no other refuge [above him]!
Though motionless and having a wooden body, he displays divine pastimes;
even by a slight devotion he forgives a hundred offenses of men.
Here I will tell you a story that destroys sin,
concerning the sport of the Supreme Self with a wooden body, O sages.
Born in Kurukṣetra, both a brahmin and a kṣatriya,
became companions and went about in affection, taking their food and amusements together.
Fallen from proper conduct, collectors of forbidden things, utterly deluded,
devoid of Vedic recitation and the vaṣaṭ call, abandoned by the svadhā and svāhā utterances,
unworthy vessels for virtue, corrupted by great sins,
eating wine, dwelling together with courtesans, filled with lust,
thought for the next world never occurred to them even in a dream.
Living in this manner, they passed half of their lifespan.
Once, as they wandered, they came upon a sacrificial enclosure,
hearing from afar enchanting hymns and the sound of the scriptures.

Remembering their own castes, the two, Puṇḍarīka and Ambarīṣa,

“How shall we two cross over the terrible ocean of misdeeds
accumulated intentionally in this very life, never decaying?

2.2.s: na tacchāstraṃ hi jānāti yadāvābhyāṃ ca duṣkṛtam ...
2.2.d: न तच्छास्त्रं हि जानाति यदावाभ्यां च दुष्कृतम् ...
2.2.m: Indeed, no scripture knows what misdeed we two have committed;
an expiation for such dread [sin] as we have heaped up is very hard to find.
Nevertheless, approaching these brahmins gathered in the assembly, most devoted to Brahman,
having resorted to them with prostrations, let us ask here for an expiation.”
Having so decided, the two saluted the brahmins and questioned them,
duly confessing each their own impurities again and again.
Hearing their words, those excellent brahmins closed their eyes;
they did not speak anything, looking at one another with astonished faces:
“Ah, most terrible deeds have been amassed by these two wicked souls,

2.2.s: yeṣu śāstraṃ padaṃ dātuṃ prāyaścittāya na hyalam .. 97 ..
2.2.d: येषु शास्त्रं पदं दातुं प्रायश्चित्ताय न ह्यलम् .. 97 ..
2.2.m: in which scripture is not competent to lay down a step for expiation!
Therefore, we are not able to provide an expiation for these two.”
In their midst was an eminent leader of the assembly, an eminent Vaiṣṇava,
whose impurities had been completely destroyed by the greatness of devotion to the Blessed Lord.
Smiling, that best of those who know speech spoke this word to them:
The Vaiṣṇava said:
“O brahmin, and O scion of the kṣatriyas, from this very dreadful heap of sin
if you two desire liberation, go swiftly to Puruṣottama,
the best of sacred fields, where Puruṣottama abides made of wood,
the all-pervading Lord who bestows grace through the devotion of the royal seer Indradyumna.
Having worshipped that Jagannātha, who holds the conch, discus, and mace,

2.2.s: pāpakṣayaṃ vā muktiṃ vā svecchayā prāpsyatha dhuvam .. 102 ..
2.2.d: पापक्षयं वा मुक्तिं वा स्वेच्छया प्राप्स्यथ धुवम् .. 102 ..
2.2.m: you will surely attain the destruction of sin or liberation according to your wish.
He is indeed like a forest fire to a mass of cotton made of dreadful misdeeds;

2.2.s: tapase tatkṣayaṃ netuṃ na śakyaṃ janmakoṭibhiḥ .. 103 ..
2.2.d: तपसे तत्क्षयं नेतुं न शक्यं जन्मकोटिभिः .. 103 ..
2.2.m: by austerity it is not possible to bring about its destruction even in ten million births.
Upon seeing him, all evil goes to destruction simultaneously.

2.2.s: tanmā vilaṃbaṃ kurutaṃ prayātaṃ tatra satvaraṃ .. 104 ..
2.2.d: तन्मा विलंबं कुरुतं प्रयातं तत्र सत्वरं .. 104 ..
2.2.m: Therefore do not delay; go there quickly!
In the exceedingly holy land of Utkala, situated on the shore of the southern ocean,
go for refuge to the all-pervading Lord whose abode is on the peak of the Blue Mountain.
That God, a treasure of compassion, will grant you your desired attainment.”
Thus instructed, the brahmin and the kṣatriya, filled with joy,
departed by that very path to Puruṣottama, O brahmins.

2.2.m:
Jaimini said:
With hearts dispassionate, the two, having abandoned the company of courtesans and the like, / meditating on Viṣṇu with their minds, both observing the vow of pure food, / 1
reached in a short time the abode of Hari on the Blue Mountain. / Having bathed in the waters of the king of sacred fords as prescribed by rule, / 2
standing at the temple gateway and bowing down with all eight limbs, / looking for the Lord, O brahmins, they did not see [him] then. / 3
With pale faces, not seeing the God, distressed with anxiety, / they undertook a fast until they should receive darśana of the Lord. / 4
Praising the sin-destroying name of the Lord, / in the third watch of the night they saw a single light. / 5
Then the two of them, steadfast, fasted for three more days; / in the middle of the seventh night, they saw the Lord. / 6
Hearing the praises of the gods, they acquired divine knowledge; / their slough of sins cast off, they saw the God face to face, / 7
holding conch, discus, and mace in hand, adorned with divine ornaments, / with lotus feet placed on the back of jewel-encrusted sandals, / 8
with eyes like blooming white lotuses, a serene countenance, all-pervading, / embracing with his left arm Lakṣmī who stood at his left side, / 9
taking the prepared betel leaf offered by Śrī. / Some [maidens] held jewelled canes in their hands, others had chowries in hand; / 10
some, rich in youth and well adorned, held with their own hands / lamps of fragrant oil and small lamps with jewelled wicks; / 11
behind [him], a radiant [maiden] held an umbrella made of jewels; / another, holding near his face an incense burner well-perfumed with black aloe, / mocked Pramlocā with the beauty of her form. / Bestowing grace with his playful, curly-haired glance upon the gods before him / 13
who, with hands folded in reverent salutation and necks bowed, praised him individually; / and with a smile upon the divine hosts of perfected ones and sages, Sanaka and the rest; / 14
and upon Nārada and other gandharvas enchanting with divine songs, / lending his ear in listening, compassionate in mere sport; / 15
and upon the foremost Vaiṣṇavas such as Prahlāda meditating upon his true form before him, / absorbing their minds in his own form; / 16
manifesting his universal cosmic form by means of the gods and others / reflected in the Kaustubha jewel gleaming on his chest; / 17
standing beneath a shower of divine flowers raining down from above; / beholding the multitude of apsarases, whose beauty had faded in the presence of Śrī, / 18
[performing] various, ever-alluring movements of the limbs; / having seen him of divine playful sports, the two, the brahmin and the kṣatriya, / 19
became in an instant masters of all branches of learning, O brahmins. / Having circumambulated the Lord of gods three times, both with folded hands, / bowing with prostration of all eight limbs, they praised him, filled with joy. / 20
Puṇḍarīka said:
Salutations to you, support of the universe, cause of creation, maintenance, and destruction! / O Nārāyaṇa, salutations to you, Supreme Self, supreme refuge! / 21
You alone are the ultimate reality, free from arising and passing away; / those endowed with the eye of meditation know you to be the embodiment of eternal bliss. / 22
You are pure consciousness, Lord of the worlds, the foundation, higher than the highest; / how indeed can those of foolish heart know you, the utterly pure? / 23
Their minds bewildered by the craving for desires and wealth, intensely miserable, / weary on the path of coming and going—when do they ever partake of happiness? / 24
Take pity on me, O Lord, who am wretched, who have sought refuge, / foolish, a performer of evil deeds, fallen into the ocean of worldly existence. / 25
What other kinsman like you exists in the cosmic egg, O Lord, / who, regardless of his own obligations, is compassionate toward the wretched and shelterless? / 26
Save [me], O ocean of mercy, who am continually caused / to experience suffering due to wandering through high and low, like a bucket on a waterwheel! / 27
Those fools who worship you with an eye to acquisition and preservation, / though you bestow effortless liberation, are utterly deluded by your māyā. / 28

2.2.m:
Your name, 'Nārāyaṇa', even if chanted casually,
is greater than yourself, O Lord of the universe, as the sole means to the four goals of life. / 29
You grant those various perfections through those various individual sacrifices,
[yet] you alone, O Lord, are the refuge of those fallen into the ocean of worldly existence. / 30
Having boarded the boat of knowledge, with the oar of compassion in hand,
you alone are able, O Lord, to lead the unconscious one to the farther shore of the ocean of saṃsāra,
when meditated upon with undivided devotion.
Those other gods who bestow liberation, established in the scriptures, / 32
truly lead [one] to devotion to you, which is an Agastya to the ocean of suffering. / 33
Therefore be pleased with me, O Blessed One; grant firm devotion to your lotus feet, O Lord,
by which I may cross this terrible and very impassable ocean of existence, even though devoid of the exertion born of eight-limbed yoga. / 34

2.2.m:
I have no need of these heaps of righteousness, wealth, and desire, grasped by the foolish, which are trivial and yield little happiness. / Command, O Worshipful One, through the contemplation of your two lotus feet, my immersion in an ocean of dense and ever-increasing bliss! / 35
Having thus praised [him], the brahmin, near the lotus feet of the Lord of the universe,
fell down, saying, 'Save me, O Kṛṣṇa!' with a voice choked with tears.
Rising again, he stood with folded hands, praising [him]. / 36
Ambarīṣa said:
Be pleased, O God, the Self of all, of countless heads and arms!
O one of countless noses, eyes, hands, and feet, salutations to you! / 37
You transcend the thirty-six principles; you are free from phenomenal existence, yet the cause of phenomenal existence.
O abode of the fourfold universe, O cosmic-formed one, salutations to you! / 38
Having one foot, and having three feet, having sacred waters at your feet, stepping through intermediate space,
from whose foot the Gaṅgā arose and purifies the three worlds; / 39
whose name indeed, when recited, cleanses sins such as the murder of a brahmin
and bestows all auspiciousness—salutations to him of auspicious nature! / 40
O God, even through the praise of your name all perfections arise.

2.2.m:
Out of eager wonder indeed do the wise, endowed with intellect, seek you. / 41
O Lord, the water of your feet removes torment through taking refuge [in it];
for me, who am overcome by the threefold suffering, make devotion firm here. / 42
For me, who have no other master, there is nothing else to be prayed for today.
Bowing down, O Jagannātha, I pray to you a thousandfold:
The seed of all human goals lies in your lotus feet.
As long as I maintain my breath, may my devotion remain steadfast.
Through that devotion by which the Grandfather fashioned this creation,
and Rudra dissolves the universe, and Lakṣmī bestows sovereignty—
O compassionate one to the wretched, with an undivided mind I pray for that devotion.
In this exceedingly firm mire of beginningless ignorance, extremely hard to cross,
for one submerged, O Jagannātha, unsupported and perishing,
there is no other refuge than devotion to you, possessing great majesty.
The conflicting paths of Śruti, Smṛti, and the rest are causes of confusion;
without devotion to you, these are incapable of functioning effectively.

wearing divine yellow garments, adorned with divine garlands and perfumes;

by whose great strength the Lord sustains the cosmic egg—
that Bala, the king of serpents, adorned with seven hoods,

the dwelling place of all beauty, bowed down to by all the gods,

2.2.m:
Lakṣmī, who abides in the lotus heart of the Lord of Lakṣmī, standing separately,
the goddess holding a boon-bestowing lotus, adorned with divine attire and ornaments,
a wish-fulfilling creeper for the surrendered, destroying all sins,
rescuing those submerged in the ocean of worldly existence, the savior of the gods.
On the left side of Viṣṇu, they saw the excellent discus,
fashioned from the end of the log, O brahmins, blazing with golden portions.
Having seen Viṣṇu manifested in a fourfold form, the two—the brahmin and the kṣatriya—
at the time of sunrise, deemed their toil to have borne fruit.
Remembering that dream-like divine play, they were then filled with wonder:
"This is not a wooden image; it is the absolute Brahman manifested in person!"
And the two placed their faith in the words of the brahmins who had assembled:
"Where are we two, great sinners, destined to undergo hellish torments?
And where is this vision of Viṣṇu, surrounded by gods?
Though we were foolish, proficiency in the eighteen sciences [has arisen in us];
therefore, there is no delusion: the knowledge declared by them is true.

2.2.m:
What they said—that the wooden Brahman situated on the shore of the king of sacred fords,
shining at the root of the banyan tree, upon being seen liberates a living being—
that indeed is this Jagannātha, manifested in four forms!
Whenever he descends to earth, he manifests in fourfold form."
"Then, keeping ourselves alive, both of us shall stay in his presence;
turning our backs on trivial desires, we shall not go anywhere else." 74
Having resolved thus, O sages, devoted to Viṣṇu,
constantly chanting the name of Nārāyaṇa, they both attained liberation. 75
Jaimini said:
In this context has indeed been told this secret that destroys sins.
Those who hear the account of Puṇḍarīka and Ambarīṣa, 76
and constantly recite it filled with supreme joy,
go to the abode of Viṣṇu, filled with supreme joy.
With their impurities washed away, they too go to the abode of Viṣṇu. 77

2.2.m: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the dialogue between the sage Jaimini [and the sages], in the Praise of Puruṣottamakṣetra, in the second Vaiṣṇava Section, in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses. 5
The sages said:
In what country, O best of brahmins, is that sacred field of Puruṣottama,
where Nārāyaṇa visibly shines forth in the form of wood? 1
Jaimini said:
There is a country named Utkala, famous and supremely purifying,
where there are many sacred fords and holy sanctuaries. 2
That country is situated on the shore of the southern ocean,
wherein the people residing are models of righteous conduct. 3
There the brahmins are endowed with good conduct and study, performers of sacrifices,
promoters of sacrifices, Vedas, and Vedic scriptures as at the beginning of creation. 4
It is celebrated as a repository of the eighteen branches of learning;
Lakṣmī dwells in every house by the command of Nārāyaṇa. 5
The people are modest, humble, free from mental and physical diseases,
devoted to their father and mother, truthful, and worshippers of Viṣṇu. 6
Neither does any non-Vaiṣṇava live there, nor any atheist;

2.2.s: sarve parahitāstatra na lubdhā na śaṭhāḥ khalāḥ .. 7 ..
2.2.d: सर्वे परहितास्तत्र न लुब्धा न शठाः खलाः .. 7 ..
2.2.m: all there are benevolent towards others, not greedy, not deceitful, and not wicked. 7
The people there are long-lived, and the women regard their husbands as deities,
well-behaved, righteous in character, adorned with modesty and good conduct, 8
abounding in the pride of beauty and youth, adorned with all ornaments,
renowned for conduct appropriate to their lineage, character, age, and behavior. 9
Engaged in their own duties there, consecrated to the protection of the subjects,
the kṣatriyas are champions in generosity, proficient in weapons and treatises. 10
All perform sacrifices constantly with copious sacrificial gifts;
their sacrificial altars shine, and their sacrificial posts are adorned with gold. 11
In their homes, guests are honored beyond their expectations;
and the vaiśyas abide by the occupations of agriculture, trade, and cattle-rearing. 12
With devotion and also with wealth, they gratify the gods, preceptors, and brahmins;
a petitioner who has gone to the door of one does not have to go to another's house. 13
Proficient in songs, poetry, arts, and crafts, speaking kindly,
and the śūdras there are righteous, devoted to the acts of bathing and giving; 14
in deed, thought, speech, and wealth, they are servers of brahmins.
Those others who are born of mixed castes are established in their own duties. 15

2.2.s: na viparyaṃti ṛtavo nākāle varṣate ghanaḥ ..
2.2.d: न विपर्यंति ऋतवो नाकाले वर्षते घनः ..
2.2.m: The seasons do not reverse; clouds do not rain out of season;
there is no loss of crops; nor does wind or hunger afflict the subjects. 16
No famine, epidemic, or ruin of the realm occurs here;
there is no object existing on earth that is unobtainable there. 17
Thus endowed with all virtues, crowded with various trees and creepers:
with arjuna, aśoka, punnāga, tāla, hintāla, and śāla trees; 18
with prācīnāmalaka, lodhra, bakula, and nāgakeśara trees;
with coconuts, priyālas, saralas, and devadārus; 19
with dhavas, khadiras, bilvas, jackfruits, and kapitākas;
with campakas, karṇikāras, kovidāras, and pāṭalas; 20
with kadamba, nimba, nicula, mango, and āmalaka trees;
with oranges, jambīras, nīpas, and mātuluṅgas; 21
with mandāras, pārijātas, banyans, agallochum, and sandaltrees;
with dates, hog-plums, siddhas, mucukundas, and kiṃśukas; 22
with tindukas, saptaparṇas, sacred figs, and vibhītakas;
and strewn with various other exceedingly charming trees; 23
and with mālatī, kunda, bāṇa, and karavīras of white and other colors.
and with groves of ketakī thickets, with atimukta and kubjaka plants,
with cardamoms, cloves, kaṅkolas, pomegranates, and citrons,
surrounded by hundreds of gardens and rows of areca-nut groves.
Teeming with various trees and creepers, surrounded by mountains and rivers,
this excellent country, O best of the twice-born, is called Utkala.
Extending to the Ṛṣikulyā which flows to the southern ocean,
the country is situated between the two great rivers, [the Ṛṣikulyā] and the Svarṇarekhā.
In this sacred dwelling place there are very many sacred fields,
which were described by me to you previously during the pilgrimage, O twice-born.
And now this Puruṣottama, a heaven on earth, has been described.

In which country was his city, and how did he go to Puruṣottama

Jaimini said:
Excellent, excellent, O best of the twice-born, that you ask about the ancient
auspicious history that removes all sins, is holy, and grants enjoyment and liberation!

2.2.d: चरितं तस्य वक्ष्यामि तथावृत्तं कृते युगे ..
2.2.m: I shall relate his life as it happened in the Kṛtayuga.
Listen, all you sages, attentive and with senses subdued.
In the Kṛtayuga, O brahmins, there was a great king named Indradyumna,
born in the solar dynasty, righteous, the fifth descendant of the Creator.
He spoke the truth, had good conduct, was pure, foremost among the virtuous;

2.2.s: nyāyātsadā pālayati prajāḥ svā iva sa prajāḥ .. 7 ..
2.2.d: न्यायात्सदा पालयति प्रजाः स्वा इव स प्रजाः .. 7 ..
2.2.m: he always protected his subjects justly, like his own offspring.
A knower of the supreme Self, expert in knowledge, heroic, victorious in battle,
ever active, always a worshipper of brahmins, devoted to his ancestors,
like another Bṛhaspati in the eighteen branches of learning,
a ruler of gods in majesty, and Kubera in the accumulation of treasure;
handsome, fortunate, well-mannered, generous, an enjoyer, speaking kindly,
a performer of all sacrifices, devoted to the brahmins, true to his word,
dear to men and women like the moon on the full-moon night,
dazzling like the sun, difficult to gaze upon, causing the destruction of enemy ranks,
a Vaiṣṇava, endowed with truth, having conquered anger and controlled the senses.
He sacrificed with the Rājasūya, the best of rites, and a thousand horse-sacrifices,
the supreme, glorious [king], desiring liberation, intent upon righteousness.
Thus endowed with all virtues, that king protecting the earth

You transform [into food]; homage to You who make the world live!
Living on a portion of whom, whose nature is bliss, the worlds subsist,
homage to that Brahman-Self, devoid of all impurities!
To the spotless one, whose form is auspicious, the wielder of māyā,
devoid of all attachment, homage to You, the witness of the universe!
To the one with many feet, eyes, heads, mouths, and arms, victorious over all,
whose essence is all living beings, homage to You who possess all forms!
Homage to You, beloved of Kamalā! Homage to You who sit on a lotus!
Homage, O lotus-petal-eyed one! Protect me, O Puruṣottama!
Afflicted by roaming in worthless worldly existence, truly by diseases and grief,
deliver me from this mass of worldly sorrow, who have taken refuge at Your lotus feet!"

When the brahmin had returned, then, at evening time, thronged by the gods,
at the time of worshiping Mādhava, a wind of violent speed blew. (1)
And it scattered golden sand everywhere.
Their eyes obscured by it, the gods were unable to see. (2)
O brahmins, they then meditated on Puruṣottama, the beloved of Śrī.
While those heaven-dwellers had their gaze fixed in meditation for an hour, (3)
at the end of their meditation they saw a heap of sand, not Mādhava,
nor the Rauhiṇa pool; their senses were thrown into distress. (4)
They fell into great anxiety and wept bitterly, crying ‘Alas! Alas!’:
“What is this misfortune of ours that has suddenly befallen all at once? (5)
The Lord of Śrī, who gladdened our eyes, is no longer found in an instant!
What fault of ours has been seen, O Puruṣottama, (6)
that leaving all Your servants at once, You are no longer seen?
For whose sake, O Jagannātha, You assumed a body, (7)
leaving them helpless in the forest, why do You forsake them?
Abandoning us, the manifestations of Your own body, O lotus-eyed Lord, (8)
why do You unexpectedly reduce the heaven-dwellers to a mere memory?
Sacrificers sacrifice indeed unto all of us who are Your parts, (9)
for Your pleasure, O Yajñapuruṣa, [to us] who grant fruits ordained by You.
Having bodies born of Your ego-sense, living only by Your grace, (10)
whither can we go, fleeing in fear, neglected by You now?

2.2.m: “Today my life has become fruitful through the deeds of my birth,

I bow to the garland from Mukunda’s head, whose charming fragrance, gained from incomparable bliss, surpasses the heavenly tree,
which blinds the swarms of bees, and whose scent, carried by the breeze, destroys the impurities of the world. 36
Through contact with the dust falling from his lotus feet, Brahmā and others attained supreme prosperity;
I bow to this garland, an abode of flowers clinging to the unguents illuminating the body of that Viṣṇu! 37
It laughs, with its blossoming lovely flowers, at its co-wife Padmā,
who dwells in the heart-lotus and is proud of resting on Viṣṇu’s lap. 38

Speaking thus with a voice choked with tears,

That brahmin Vidyāpati too, with all his sins destroyed,
possessing a divine body, stood before the king meditating on Mādhava, 42
the wise man washing away the sins of all the worlds with his splendor.
"May the Lord whose dwelling is on the peak of Nīlādri bless you.
This command of the Lord of Śrī has been revealed to you in the form of a garland,
that you may go to behold His very self, the giver of liberation, who resides in the supreme sacred field."
Speaking thus, he placed the garland around the king's neck.
Then the king arose, and looking upon the garland hanging upon his chest,
he felt as though the beloved of Śrī had entered directly into his heart.
Placing his hands upon his head, his eyes half-closed,
his face bathed in tears of joy, he praised Hari:
Indradyumna said:
"Victory, O Creator whose art is the creation, maintenance, and destruction of all the worlds,
O bearer of the burden of cosmic eggs as numerous as the hairs on Your playfully assumed universal body!
O inner ruler of all, O Lord who removes the distress of those who bow before You,
whose lotus feet are variegated by the diadems of Brahmā, Indra, and Rudra!
O You who are solely intent on ever protecting the wretched, the helpless, and the distressed,
O ocean of unfeigned waters of compassion, higher than the highest!
Pitiable, having no other refuge than You, weighed down by beginningless delusion,
protect me, O Lord of the universe, You who constantly cherish Your devotees!"
Praising Him thus, the king sat down upon his throne,
surrounded by householders, celibate students, ascetics, and forest hermits,
by twice-born sacrificers skilled in the eighteen sciences,
along with leading citizens, elder servants, and ministers at their head.

2.2.m: On the mountain’s summit stands an exceedingly tall, vast banyan tree lasting until the end of the kalpa,
a krośa wide, devoid of flowers and fruits, yet radiant with tender shoots.
Even as the sun moves across, its shade does not depart.
Behind it lies a pool named Rohiṇa;
from its spring of water it is adorned with steps of sapphire stone,
surrounded on all four sides by outer crystal platforms,
charming, filled with waters that remove masses of sin.
In the middle of its eastern platform, cooled by the shade of the banyan,
resides the God made of sapphire, bearing the discus and mace,
measuring eighty-one aṅgulas, standing upon a golden lotus.
His forehead surpasses the beauty of a crescent moon of the eighth lunar day;
his eyes seem intent on disdaining the splendour of a pair of smiling blue lotuses.
The rising nectar-moon of his face releases one from the three afflictions;
he is made lovely by the sesamum flower shone upon by his two nostrils.
Though his body is of stone, his lower lip is bathed in a gentle smile;
charming are his chin and jaw, with cheeks blossoming in laughter;
the two corners of his mouth are truly fashioned like no others before.
Bearing auspicious lower lip, cheeks, chin, and corners of the mouth recessed in laughter,
the God serves as a model for artisans like Viśvakarman and others.
With his pair of ears adorned with ear-ornaments shaped like makara mouths,
he derides the full moon between Jupiter and Venus;
by the region of his neck producing the beauty of a necklace for onlookers,
he causes suspicion that the pearl originated from a right-coiled conch.
He has a pair of stout, broad shoulders, and four arms reaching down to his knees;
the all-pervading Lord's chest is adorned with a pure, clear necklace.
He bears the divine Kaustubha reflecting the fourteen worlds;
he is charming with the fine line of body-hair entering the deep pool of his navel,
and the necklace descending through the three folds [of his belly], appearing motionless.
With a girdle-band of fine gems and a string of tinkling pearls,
the God's hips shine as vessels of the world’s loveliness.
Adorned with yellow garments and a long-hanging pearl garland around his waist,
his two pillar-like shanks serve as an auspicious gateway to liberation.
With rounded, symmetrical knees, a garland reaching to the forefeet,
and two anklets rich in gems, the feet of the Lord shine resplendent.
Adorned with necklaces, bracelets, armlets, crowns, and other ornaments,
Keśava, who embodies knowledge, self-hood, sovereignty, and the Sound-Brahman,
bears these very principles transformed into his discus, lotus, mace, and conch.
The god illuminating all quarters stands atop the blue mountain (Nīlādri),

2.2.m: Then, with his draft animals weary, the king proceeded swiftly

renowned as Dhātukandara, he encamped his army,
intent on performing his afternoon rites as part of his daily observance.
He entered the river at a bathing place, accompanied by his family priest,
which had been inspected beforehand by wise men and cleared of poison and thorns.
Having bathed and offered libations to the gods and ancestors, the lord of the people,
having worshipped Viṣṇu according to rule, then honoured the kings and the subjects
with quarters, seats, and the like.
Then the glorious king, entering the inner apartments along with Nārada,
enjoyed food that tasted like nectar, his mind delighted.
Then, when the sun had gone to the western mountain, the lord of the people
quickly completed his evening rite; and when the cool-rayed moon had risen,
the lord of his dependents and subjects sat down in the midst of the assembly.
There in that assembly, the king, endowed with the marks of universal sovereignty, shone
like the full-orbed autumn moon among the stars.
Poets composed verses praising his fame, pure as nectar,
and singers with melodious, sweet voices sang well-composed songs.
Then courtesans, proud of their beauty, youth, and charm,
danced before him with pure rhythms, melodies, and graceful gestures.
And bards praised him, who possessed an extraordinary and auspicious form,
with diverse clusters of words in prose and verse compositions.
Then the king honoured the foremost Vaiṣṇavas among the courtiers
with highly agreeable and exceedingly splendid perfumes, garlands, and betel leaves.
And the hundreds of kings seated there comfortably by the king's command,
he honoured appropriately with royal presents.
Then, with great respect, he questioned the excellent sage Nārada, dear to the Lord,
who was comfortably seated on a throne,
wishing to hear the deeds of the Lord, which dispel all sins:
Indradyumna said:
O venerable one, treasure of the Vedas and auxiliary sciences, beloved of the Lord!
You alone know the deeds of Viṣṇu by the eye of knowledge.
With the nectar of Hari’s deeds, [my mind] is soiled with hardened mire—
Wash within me, O sage, if you have compassion for me. (14)

O Nārāyaṇa, supreme abode, supreme Self, higher than the highest!
O you whose sovereign power is existence, consciousness, and bliss, taintless one, homage be to you!

2.2.m: hidden by your own māyā, self-luminous one, homage be to you!
Not inside, yet outside; outside, yet inside; situated far off, yet near at hand;
heavy, light, firm, more subtle, and grosser—homage be to you!
O peerless one, millions of Brahmā’s [lifespans] and half an instant of mine
arise from the play of your glance: homage to that embodiment of Time!
Surrounded by hosts of universes held in each single hair,
whose body is beyond measure: homage to that universal Self!
Homage be to you who measure the dissolution and birth of the Creator by his own measure of time,
and the arrangement of manvantaras and the like!
I was created from tamas, O Lord, ignorant of your majesty.
Therefore forgive my offense; protect me who have approached for refuge!
While the burner of Tripura was making this hymn of praise,
Adhokṣaja, relinquishing the form of the discus, manifested himself,
gracious of countenance, glorious, bearing conch, discus, and mace,
seated on Garuḍa upon a lotus throne, adorned with a garland of forest flowers,
radiant with necklaces, earrings, armlets, diadem, and other ornaments,
holding Lakṣmī on his left lap and having Satyā on his right side,
an ocean of compassion possessing a charming body like a dark raincloud.
As if possessed by anger, he spoke to the trembling lord of Girijā:
The Blessed Lord said:
O Śambhu, after so much time, how has this bad judgment come upon you,
that for the sake of a king who is a mere insect you have stood up to fight with me?

Formerly you were strengthened by numerous austerities as [part of] my body;

there is a sacred field renowned on earth by my name, the glorious Puruṣottama-kṣetra,
on the shore of the southern ocean, adorned by the Nīlācala mountain,
ten yojanas in extent, reaching as far as the Viraja-maṇḍala.
Progressively purifying is that sacred field as far as the Citrotpalā river;
from there onwards, whatever region reaches up to the southern ocean,
step by step most excellent, is the Nīlādri, which bestows liberation,
where indeed I abide in four forms, made of sapphire.
To the north of it is the renowned forest named Ekāmraka;
dwell there with Pārvatī without fear, O destroyer of Tripura!
By the self-manifest [Brahmā] creating all the worlds at my command,
you shall be anointed as king even there over ten million liṅgas.
And this sacred ford which is Maṇikarṇikā consists of all sacred fords;
abandoning your egoism here, go there with your retinue.

O Lord of the world, obeying your command is the cause of the highest good for me.

Then at noon, O twice-born, the sage and the king,
together with their army, reached the sacred field called the Ekāmra forest.
The king, bathing in the Bindutīrtha and worshiping

Having properly sipped its water, he, for his [the Lord’s] pleasure, gave many

to the twice-born, the king being established in sattvic duty.

Saying 'So be it,' Mahādeva vanished in an instant from the sage.
He too, standing on the king's chariot, set out for the supreme sacred field.
On the second day, the king reached the site of Kapoteśa,
endowed with length and breadth, filled with water reservoirs and trees,
with Bilveśa on its eastern boundary, situated on the seashore.

the best of kings stationed [the troops] appropriately and in their proper places.
Having bowed to and worshipped Bilveśvara and Kapoteśa,
the wise [king] mounted the chariot together with the son of Brahmā;

2.2.m: The sages said: / "And how did the site of Kapoteśa become renowned, O great sage? / Who indeed was the pigeon, and who was the Lord? You ought to tell us this." / Jaimini said: / "Formerly, it was Kuśasthalī, unfit for resort by any living beings, / covered all around with thorns having the sharp edges of kuśa grass, / devoid of trees, without any reservoir of water, like an abode of piśācas. / When formerly no other god was worshipped besides the Blessed Lord, / Dhūrjaṭi [Śiva] then had a rivalry, [thinking:] 'May I also be worthy of worship!' / Reflecting thus, he fixed his mind on devotion to that very Viṣṇu: / 'Having stayed in a place free from all sensory objects, without possessions, / undertaking very great austerity, I shall please that Hari. / What should I say to the Lord of Ramā? What is the praise of the husband of Śāradā? / Or what else would cause satisfaction to the Lord of the entire universe? / Therefore, no other external object is indeed of use to him; / undertaking internal sacrifice with an guileless mind, / I shall worship Hari, the teacher of moving and unmoving beings, who gives himself to his devotees; / by his grace, may I become worthy of worship by all.' / Then, having formed this resolve, free from all dualities, / he went to holy Kuśasthalī near the blue mountain. / Then Maheśvara performed severe austerity, subsisting on air; / though the Lord has eight forms, he became minute like a pigeon. / Then the Blessed Lord, pleased, bestowed sovereignty upon him at that time, / by which he became equal to himself in worship, honor, and the like. / By the power of his austerity, the site became like Vṛndāvana, / its interior adorned with lakes, ponds, pools, and rivers, / with various trees and creepers bearing fruits and flowers in all seasons, / resounding with the humming of bees intoxicated with honey,

who consist of the triple Veda, who transcend the triad, who know the three divisions of time, obeisance!

by whom the darkness of ignorance is severed—to that one free from darkness, obeisance!

“O Dhūrjaṭi, remain in the temple, blocking the exit of the asuras.
Who other than you, O Śambhu, is capable of destroying the army of the demons?”
Having established Mahādeva, he then went to Dvārāvatī.
From that time forth, Bilveśa attained renown on earth.
That Bilveśa is the primal rule of the king of sacred fields, O twice-born.
Seeing that destroyer of sins, the imperishable husband of Mṛḍānī,
one obtains all desires and overcomes insurmountable misfortune.
The greatness of Kapoteśvara and Bilveśvara has indeed been told to you.
Beyond this, O sages, what else do you wish to hear?

Hearing that dreadful word, equal to the stroke of a thunderbolt,
the king fell unconscious upon the ground, O best of brahmins.
Seeing him fallen thus, led by the family priest,
all his affectionate companions rushed forward wailing in distress.
Sprinkling water cooled with camphor repeatedly upon his face,
they smeared all his limbs with sandalwood, aloe, and camphor.
They quickly fanned him with chowries and palm fans.
Even Nārada, agitated, concentrated with yogic meditation;
knowing the auspicious future there, he protected the king's vital breaths.
By these supreme efforts, the king at last regained consciousness.

the kings, the learned Vedic brahmins, and the Vaiṣṇavas in their thousands, [thought:] (25)

Even as they were wondering, a breeze from the south [arrived], (26)
and showers of flowers resounded with swarms of bees drawn by fragrance;
moistened with the water of the river of the three worlds that appeared, O twice-born ones, (27)
immediately thereafter came that Nārada, the son of Brahmā,
resting on an excellent aerial chariot brought forth by the power of his austerity; (28)
richly adorned by celestial women holding jewelled chowries in their hands,
bedecked with varied ornaments of gems and jewels, (29)
wearing celestial garlands and garments, anointed with celestial fragrant paste,
delightful, infused with life, fashioned by Viśvakarman, (2.2.16.30)
enveloped by an orb of light, and bestowing joy all around,
bringing the replica image of Narasiṃha, he arrived. (31)

2.2.s: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣitāḥ sarve rājā rājānuyāyinaḥ ..
2.2.d: तां दृष्ट्वा हर्षिताः सर्वे राजा राजानुयायिनः ..
2.2.m: Seeing it, all were overjoyed, the king and his attendants [wondering]:
“Has the Lord who had vanished been brought back by Nārada?” (32)
Rejoicing in heart, they praised that sage.
Discerning the form of Narasiṃha present there, O twice-born ones, (33)
they considered it the replica image of the primordial form of Nṛsiṃha.
Then, rising up, the king, with an inner self overjoyed,
circumambulated Hari and went to the ground with his head. (34)
With provisions suited to an abundance of faith, by order of the king,
the sage had [the image] brought into the temple endowed with auspicious marks. (35)
At an auspicious hour, O best of brahmins, the king praised
the image of the God of gods, accompanied by Dharā and Ramā, installed upon a jewelled altar,
its body fixed in yogic posture; Indradyumna then praised [him], (36)
together with Vaiṣṇavas, brahmins, kings, and the wise Nārada,
joyfully with secret Upaniṣads, traditional hymns, and scriptures: (37)
Indradyumna said:
“O you whose form is one and many, gross, subtle, and atomic; O beyond space, whose form is space, whose form is one;
having the form of space, all-pervading, dwelling in space, mounted on space, origin of the space-haired [Śiva] and lotus-born [Brahmā]! (38)
Save me from the ocean of suffering, O divine Lion, whose radiance is that of countless millions of risen suns!

2.2.s: nityāsanno dūrasaṃstho na dūro nāsanno vā bodhyabodhātmabhāva .. 39 ..

2.2.m: Eternally near, dwelling afar, neither distant nor near, the true nature of both the knower and the known! (39)
The object to be known among knowables, attainable through knowledge yet unattainable, beyond illusion, measurable by proof and inference,
the beginning of all, maker of all, approver, protector, destroyer, witness of the universe, homage to you! (2.2.16.40)

2.2.d: त्वत्पादब्जे भक्तिमग्र्यां सदा मे देहि स्वामिन्मूलभूतां चतुर्णाम् ..
2.2.m: Grant me forever foremost devotion to your lotus feet, O Lord, which is the root cause of the four [aims of life]!

2.2.m: These your wretched people, though constantly engaged in Vedic and traditional duties, remain bound here in the ocean of worldly existence. (42)
Whose feet are infinite, who have many hands and eyes, infinite ears, whose garment is the expanse of the directions,
adorned with the lords of day and night as beautiful ear-rings, whose lovely necklace is formed by the garland of constellations, (43)
to you, the wondrous, divine form of Nṛsiṃha, fulfiller of the devotees' desires, I fly for refuge!
Whose lotus foot blossoms through the jewels of the diadem of the Grandfather [Brahmā]; (44)
he whose material head rolls on the ground near whose pair of lotus feet,

2.2.s: taddivyapādaṃ śirasā vahaṃti surendranāryaḥ khalu taṃ namāmi .. 45 ..
2.2.d: तद्दिव्यपादं शिरसा वहंति सुरेन्द्रनार्यः खलु तं नमामि .. 45 ..
2.2.m: that divine foot the women of the king of gods carry on their heads; truly, I bow to him! (45)
To that divine Lion by whom multitudes of sins are destroyed, an ocean of compassion to those who seek refuge at his feet,
the fierce one against whom the vessel of the cosmic egg shatters by the clash of his lotus feet, I bow! (46)
By the shaking of the mass of whose mane dense clouds are torn and multitudes of sins are routed,
who drowns the sound of clouds with his fierce, loud laughter, who holds the three worlds within, to Nṛhari I bow!” (47)

2.2.s: namaste namaste namaste'dya viṣṇo paritrāhi dīnānukaṃpinnanātham ..
2.2.d: नमस्ते नमस्ते नमस्तेऽद्य विष्णो परित्राहि दीनानुकंपिन्ननाथम् ..
2.2.m: Homage to you, homage to you, homage to you today, O Viṣṇu! Protect [me], who am destitute, O compassionate lord!

2.2.s: bhavaṃtaṃ samāsādya me dehabandho murāre na saṃsārakārāgṛhe'stu .. 48 ..

2.2.m: Having reached you, O Murāri, let there be no bondage of a body for me in the prison-house of saṃsāra.
At the conclusion of the thousand horse-sacrifices, just as with physical eyes
I may behold your divine form, so have compassion, O Lord!
And so that my thousand sacrifices may be completed without obstacle,
O Lord of sacrifice, through your grace, let your presence be with me.

2.2.s: koṭayaḥ pāparāśīnāṃ kṣayaṃ yāṃti yathā prabho ..
2.2.d: कोटयः पापराशीनां क्षयं यांति यथा प्रभो ..
2.2.m: Just as crores of heaps of sins go to destruction, O Lord,

2.2.s: dharmārthakāmā hastasthā naiṣāṃ citraṃ stuvaṃti ye ..
2.2.d: धर्मार्थकामा हस्तस्था नैषां चित्रं स्तुवंति ये ..
2.2.m: duty, wealth, and desire rest in their hand—it is no wonder for those who praise [you];

2.2.s: mokṣasya bhājanaṃ viṣṇo te narā ye tavāśrayāḥ .. 51 ..
2.2.d: मोक्षस्य भाजनं विष्णो ते नरा ये तवाश्रयाः .. 51 ..
2.2.m: those men are recipients of liberation, O Viṣṇu, who take refuge in you.
Having thus praised that divine lion, the king, his mind joyful,
fell repeatedly to the earth in prostration like a staff.
Jaimini said:
That sacred field of Narasiṃha was created formerly by Brahmā
for the favor of Indradyumna and for the benefit of all worlds.

2.2.s: paśyaṃti ye nṛsiṃhaṃ taṃ śaṃbhunā saha saṃsthitam ..
2.2.d: पश्यंति ये नृसिंहं तं शंभुना सह संस्थितम् ..
2.2.m: Those who see that Nṛsiṃha situated together with Śambhu

2.2.s: na dehabandhaṃ te viprāḥ prāpnuvaṃti na saṃśayaḥ .. .. 54 ..
2.2.d: न देहबन्धं ते विप्राः प्राप्नुवंति न संशयः .. .. 54 ..
2.2.m: do not obtain bodily bondage, O brahmins; there is no doubt.
Whatever is desired by the mind, they obtain even more than that.
Those who praise that divine lion form with this hymn—
the god who grants all desires bestows liberation upon them.
On the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of Jyeṣṭha combined with the Svātī constellation,
on that [day] the divine lion was consecrated in the sacred field by the great seer,

2.2.s: sutena brahmaṇaḥ sākṣāttatra paśyaṃti taṃ ca ye .. 57 ..
2.2.d: सुतेन ब्रह्मणः साक्षात्तत्र पश्यंति तं च ये .. 57 ..
2.2.m: the son of Brahmā in person; and those who behold him there
obtain the full fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices.
Or with the five nectars, with milk, or with coconut water,

2.2.s: snāpayaṃti narā ye vai athavā gandhavāriṇā ..
2.2.d: स्नापयंति नरा ये वै अथवा गन्धवारिणा ..
2.2.m: those men who bathe [him], or with scented water,
having worshiped the great lion with offerings accompanied by milk-rice,
and with garlands of Chinese rose flowers, and with very lovely scented garlands,
with incenses, lamps with camphor, and extremely lovely betel leaves,
with beautiful songs, recitations of praise, and likewise with loud cries of victory,
with circumambulations, prostrations, gifts, and pleasing of brahmins—
pleasing that Narasiṃha, one reaches the world of Brahmā.
On the fourteenth day of Vaiśākha, on Saturday, under the constellation of Anila,
at the evening twilight was the primeval incarnation of the Lion, O twice-born ones.
Having worshiped Narasiṃha properly on that [day] with concentrated mind,
the heap of sins accumulated throughout thousands of crores of births
is burned away that very instant, like a pile of cotton by fire.

2.2.s: dṛṣṭvā spṛṣṭvā namaskṛtvā praṇipatya ca bhaktitaḥ ..
2.2.d: दृष्ट्वा स्पृष्ट्वा नमस्कृत्वा प्रणिपत्य च भक्तितः ..
2.2.m: Seeing, touching, bowing, prostrating with devotion,
and praising, one is freed from sins like a snake from its slough.

2.2.s: na tasya vyādhayaḥ saṃti na śokā nādhayastathā ..
2.2.d: न तस्य व्याधयः संति न शोका नाधयस्तथा ..
2.2.m: He has no diseases, nor griefs, nor mental afflictions;
he obtains all desires and likewise the fruit of a horse-sacrifice.

2.2.s: samīpe tasya bho viprā yajanaṃ dānameva ca ..
2.2.d: समीपे तस्य भो विप्रा यजनं दानमेव च ..
2.2.m: Near him, O brahmins, sacrifice and giving,
and other meritorious deeds performed even once by men
become crores and crores of times multiplied through the grace of Narasiṃha.

2.2.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe puruṣottamakṣetramāhātmye jaiminiṛṣisaṃvāde ṣoḍaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 16 ..
2.2.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे पुरुषोत्तमक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये जैमिनिऋषिसंवादे षोडशोऽध्यायः .. 16 ..
2.2.m: Thus ends the sixteenth chapter in the conversation of the seer Jaimini, in the Glorification of the Sacred Field of Puruṣottama, in the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
The sages said:
When Nārasiṃha had been consecrated in that sacred field, what did the king

2.2.s: kiṃ cakāra mune brūhi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ tu tat .. 1 ..
2.2.d: किं चकार मुने ब्रूहि परं कौतूहलं तु तत् .. 1 ..
2.2.m: do, O sage? Tell [us], for that is our supreme curiosity.
Jaimini said:
First, he invited all the thirty [gods] beginning with Indra;
then he invited thousands of seers and brahmins,
who had studied the four Vedas along with the six limbs, pada, and krama,
skilled in the sciences of sacrifice, firmly grounded in Mīmāṃsā,
who perform rituals according to the Kalpasūtras along with commentaries,
skilled in the eighteen sciences, knowing dharma,
purified by good conduct, of noble family, truthful in speech,
and especially Vaiṣṇavas, he respectfully invited.

2.2.s: trailokye ye ca rājānaḥ siddhāḥ saptarṣayo dvijāḥ ..
2.2.d: त्रैलोक्ये ये च राजानः सिद्धाः सप्तर्षयो द्विजाः ..
2.2.m: And whatever kings, siddhas, seven seers, twice-born,
virtuous śūdras, merchants, and rulers of islands were in the three worlds, they were invited.
Measuring two krośas, O brahmins, was the assembly hall of that king,
built of stone, lofty, and plastered with white mortar.
In some places the floor was made of jewels, in some places fashioned of gold;
in others it was of crystal and of silver, the ground suitably arranged.
With towering pillars made of jewels, draped all around with fine silk,
endowed with beautiful canopies, with perfumes, garlands, and chowries,
and with lovely windows set between pearl necklaces, auspicious,
sprinkled with black aloe resin and moistened with sandalwood water,
strewn with flowers of every season, and surrounded by bordering parks,
[it had] step-wells with crystal stairways and gates adorned with lotus motifs,
their waters covered by cakravāka birds, ducks, swans, and sweetly-calling cranes,
clear, cool, fragrant, and sweet.
All around it, O brahmins, were hundreds of easy descents,
arranged with cool shades and shining on all sides.
Just as the sacrificial hall of Marutta once was, O best of brahmins,
so was that of King Indradyumna, fashioned by Viśvakarman.
On an auspicious day and under an auspicious lunar mansion, having seated the assembly members,
and having seen the kings seated on thrones and also the seers seated,
along with the hosts of brahmin seers and siddhas seated on costly carpets,
the gods seated on golden pedestals, and then the brahmins appropriately,
and the others seated comfortably in their places on excellent seats,
[he saw] the lord of Śacī seated in the midst of the kings, gods, and seers,
upon his own jewelled throne having the marks of universal sovereignty.
With divine garlands, perfumes, garments, high seats, and the like,
along with his royal priest, [the king] first worshipped him magnificently;

2.2.s: vinīto dīnavattasya cakre pūjāṃ tathā nṛpaḥ .. 19 ..
2.2.d: विनीतो दीनवत्तस्य चक्रे पूजां तथा नृपः .. 19 ..
2.2.m: humble, like one who is poor, the king performed worship for him in that manner,
so that even this lord of the three worlds considered it a wonder.
Then, having worshipped the siddhas and divine sages like Indra,
he aroused the astonishment even of Kubera, possessed of superior wealth.
Then the lord of the earth worshipped the gods, whose own wealth was abundant,
with hospitality, completely undisturbed in mind.
He honoured the kings with paraphernalia suitable for kings,

2.2.s: yathā te menire bhūpā bhavāmaḥ sāṃprataṃ vayam ..
2.2.d: यथा ते मेनिरे भूपा भवामः सांप्रतं वयम् ..
2.2.m: so that those kings thought: 'Only now do we become [true kings]!
Truly kingship was obtained in due course, but never such paraphernalia!'
He further worshipped the Vaiṣṇavas, attending [them] with acts of hospitality,

2.2.s: śāṃtā api yathā citraṃ menire viṣayāgamam .. 24 ..
2.2.d: शांता अपि यथा चित्रं मेनिरे विषयागमम् .. 24 ..
2.2.m: so that, even though tranquil, they regarded this influx of sensory objects as a wonder.
Then, led by the sages, the king, overflowing with the quality of sattva,
properly worshipped the brahmins, the kṣatriyas, and the vaiśyas.
And having worshipped the others through his ministers, with great eagerness,
he was seen bowed with humility, with his palms joined in reverence.
Together with his royal priest Nārada, he addressed great Indra aloud:
Indradyumna said:
"By your grace, O lord of the gods, I desire this; be pleased with me:
with the horse sacrifice, I wish to worship the sacrifice's Lord.
Grant me permission, O god; you are the lord of sacrifices.
All who dwell in the three worlds are obeyers of your command.
As long as the completion of the thousand sacrifices takes place, O lord,
so long dwell in the sacrificial enclosure along with the gods.
I desire to sacrifice, O lord of the gods, not out of longing for your position;

2.2.s: sarveṣāṃ vetsi deveśa manovṛttiṃ sadā prabho .. 31 ..
2.2.d: सर्वेषां वेत्सि देवेश मनोवृत्तिं सदा प्रभो .. 31 ..
2.2.m: you know the mental disposition of all at all times, O lord of the gods.
Here lord Mādhava, endowed with form, was formerly seen by you in worship;
that very same one who concealed himself under the sands—
for the sake of revealing him once more, I shall perform a thousand horse sacrifices,
O Indra, by the instruction and command of the Four-faced One [Brahmā].
When he is revealed again, it will bring welfare to you as well."
When thus petitioned by the king, the gods headed by great Indra,

2.2.s: antarddhānotaraṃ yā ca śrutā pūrvaṃ sarasvatī .. 34 ..
2.2.d: अन्तर्द्धानोतरं या च श्रुता पूर्वं सरस्वती .. 34 ..
2.2.m: remembering that bodiless voice that had been heard previously,
after the disappearance [of the Lord], spoke this, delighted:
"Indradyumna, you are a great soul, truly among the truthful on earth!
That future act of yours was experienced by us in advance.
We shall be your helpers in this undertaking that purifies the three worlds,

2.2.s: sraṣṭā sa jagatāṃ yatra udyuktaḥ svayameva hi ..
2.2.d: स्रष्टा स जगतां यत्र उद्युक्तः स्वयमेव हि ..
2.2.m: where the Creator of the worlds himself has indeed undertaken the effort.
Right here the Lord said even to us upon the earth:
Entering out of compassion for them, I shall once more
make a wooden body; thus this has been resolved.

2.2.s: nātrāsmākaṃ vyalīkaṃ tu neṃdrasya ca mahīpate ..
2.2.d: नात्रास्माकं व्यलीकं तु नेंद्रस्य च महीपते ..
2.2.m: There is no displeasure in this for us, nor for Indra, O king;
your endeavor, destined by us, brings joy to us.
Sacrifice with ease, O king of kings, to Vaikuṇṭha, who loves his devotees,
by means of the horse sacrifice repeated a thousand times.
For hard to propitiate is the Lord, yet affectionate to devotees, even for us.
We too, abandoning godhood here, devoted to devotion,
shall worship, humble, in human form in this sacred field.

2.2.s: priyaṃ hi mānuṣe loke karma siddhyati vai kṛtam .. 42 ..
2.2.d: प्रियं हि मानुषे लोके कर्म सिद्ध्यति वै कृतम् .. 42 ..
2.2.m: For dear indeed is an action performed in the mortal world, and it attains success.”
Jaimini said:
When this was spoken by the gods together with Indra, with his inner self deeply pleased,
the king worshipped the Lord for the purpose of beginning the sacrifice
with thousands of services presented according to rule.
Then the king, endowed with faith, having seen to the hosts of ancestors,
and the well-adorned brahmins and sacrificers gathered in the sacrificial hall,
having placed the chosen deity Vaikuṇṭha in front along with the sacrificial fires,
awaiting the determined astrological moment when the chanting of auspiciousness had concluded,
stood present together with his wife, wearing pure and auspicious attire.
Having pure twice-borns recite auspiciousness, a blessing of good fortune, and the rite for prosperity,
he, having gathered all the provisions, then selected the priests.
Those chosen priests, consecrating the best of kings together with his wife,
having separated the fires for the initiation sacrifice, sacrificed as prompted by the assembly members.
Having brought forward that blazing Āhavanīya fire upon the altar—
was it the very splendour of Viṣṇu bringing auspiciousness to the three worlds?
Having well sprinkled and consecrated [the horse] with mantras, having obtained leave from the guardians of the directions,
they released the principal horse, marked with auspicious characteristics on its limbs.

2.2.s: tataḥ sa dīkṣito rājā vāgyato rauravīṃ tvacam ..
2.2.d: ततः स दीक्षितो राजा वाग्यतो रौरवीं त्वचम् ..
2.2.m: Then that consecrated king, keeping silence, seated upon the skin of a Ruru deer,
sat in the midst of the sacrificial hall like Mṛtyuṃjaya himself.
He gave directions with his eyes alone for the satisfaction of the invited guests.
By the king's command, the minister prepared very costly
gem-studded vessels for the dining of the gods in great abundance;
vessels of pure gold for the sages and rulers of the earth;
for the dining of the twice-borns, fresh ones every day, O twice-borns;

2.2.s: kṣatriyāṇāṃ viśāṃ viprā rājatāni śubhāni ca .. 54 ..
2.2.d: क्षत्रियाणां विशां विप्रा राजतानि शुभानि च .. 54 ..
2.2.m: and auspicious silver ones for the kṣatriyas and vaiśyas, O brahmins;
spotless bell-metal vessels indeed for the dining of the śūdras.
Day after day, at the end of dining, O best of twice-borns,
the vessels were cast into pits by the people like discarded leaf-plates.

2.2.s: tatra yajñotsave ye vai bhojanāya nimaṃtritāḥ .. 56 ..
2.2.d: तत्र यज्ञोत्सवे ये वै भोजनाय निमंत्रिताः .. 56 ..
2.2.m: Those indeed who were invited for dining at that sacrificial festival,
their sons, grandsons, and great-grandsons—their whole lineage—
were daily fed foods of five flavours, preceded by high honor,
by those who respected them, according to the command of King Indradyumna.
They stayed there like family members until the completion of the great sacrifice.
From whichever country the people came, the king was their guardian;
Nārada, who looked upon all equally and was eager to help others,
requested by Indradyumna, served as the liaison among kings.
For Indra and the other lords of the gods, and for the divine seers, the best of kings,
the lord of men himself performed service for the completion of the sacrifice.
Sixfold foods and drinks were prepared in two ways by men:
for the gods' banquet there, by experts in mantras and rituals,

2.2.s: martyānāṃ nala vidyāyāṃ kuśalaiḥ saṃskṛtāni vai .. 62 ..
2.2.d: मर्त्यानां नल विद्यायां कुशलैः संस्कृतानि वै .. 62 ..
2.2.m: and for mortals, by those skilled in the culinary science of Nala.
For the sky-dwellers, whose food is nectar, are unaware of hunger and thirst;
yet even to them that feast was a wonder because of its novelty.
Food such as that in Indradyumna's house was rare for men on the mortal plane.
The only difference between Indradyumna and Indra was living in the mortal world.
This was exceedingly wondrous: every day new and fresh
was the increase of honor, hospitality, and food, O best of twice-borns;
they grew mutually as if in rivalry with one another,
as did fragrant flower garlands and unguents of musk and other scents.
variegated fine silks, and seats with cushions,

These and other things, even those very hard to obtain,

The palaces of the king of kings were equal to the peoples’ own homes,
yet at that time, everything was not always available in their own homes.
There, whatever was beyond [mere] desire was abundant and easy to obtain.
When the sacrifice was thus joyfully undertaken for the pleasure of the Lord of Sacrifice,
the earth, all of whose wealth had previously been stripped
by the horse sacrifice of this king, became once again beautifully adorned by a rain of gold.
When the rite of gifts, honors, and food for the people
dwelling in the three worlds was thus performed according to rule day after day,
the people sang songs to one another concerning the horse sacrifice:
“Such preparation of a sacrifice enjoined by the ritual rules of scripture
of royal sage Indradyumna has never been, nor ever will be,
wherein none were beggars and none were non-givers, having been mutually invited,
wherein there was no frustration of desire even for the gods, O twice-born!”
Then the king's sovereign sacrifice, possessed of such prosperity, proceeded;
imbued with extraordinary faith and highly accomplished, each [sacrifice] surpassed the previous one.
Authors of the Smṛtis, authors of the Kalpa texts, and composers of the scriptures,
skilled in the performance of sacrifices and the crest-jewels of virtuous conduct,
conducted the rites in proper sequence from the laying of the fires to the final bath,
for the pleasure of the king, by the approval of the assembly, O twice-born.

Those who distinguished between merits and faults conducted the rites;
Yājñavalkya and other sages were chosen as officiating priests there.
Seated in the assembly hall, in the intervals of their conversations with one another,
theological debates, hymns, and secret Upaniṣads,
as well as Purāṇic verses, O brahmins, preceded by devotion to Viṣṇu,
and the deeds of Hari that remove the entire mass of sins—
these those sages recited there in the assembly of the ruler of the earth.

2.2.m: Indeed, they certainly had no desire in their hearts to return to Pātāla.
Thus the sacrifice was conducted, bringing delight to the three worlds,
by King Indradyumna in this sacred field of Puruṣottama,
by the command of Pitāmaha, for the grace of the Lord of the Universe.
In due order, the lord of the earth brought to completion
a thousand horse sacrifices, minus one, as enjoined by sacred rule.
Then, during the thousandth horse sacrifice, the ruler of the earth,
the king, attained day by day a divine state.
Seven days before the soma-pressing, during the night that occurred,
in its fourth watch, he meditated upon the imperishable Viṣṇu.
In that meditation, by virtue of his great fortune, the king beheld,
as if before his very eyes, Śvetadvīpa fashioned of crystal,
surrounded entirely on all sides by the Ocean of Milk;
with great wish-fulfilling trees whose fragrant blossoms filled the directions with perfume;
upon their fruits, sprouts, and bark, everywhere without and within,
adorned with all ornaments, radiant, marked with conch and discus,
in brilliant madder-red hues, the forms of the Enemy of Mura [stood].
In its midst was an excellent pavilion fashioned of divine jewels,
blazing with a jeweled throne radiant like the midday sun,
charming with the gentle breezes from the cool billows of the Ocean of Milk.
In its center he saw the God bearing the conch, discus, and mace,
resembling a dark raincloud, adorned with a forest garland,
the dwelling of all charm, the abode of beauty and grace,
dazzling by his form, clad in divine ornaments.
Standing at his right side was Ananta, the supporter of the earth,
resembling ten million moons, with a luster like the snow-clad mountain,
captivating, forming a canopy with the expanse of his hooded crowns,
marked with a pair of jeweled earrings, wearing a beautiful blue garment,
his four arms gleaming with a plow, pestle, conch, and discus,
adorned with necklaces, armlets, bracelets, and rings,
richly adorned with a girdle and waist-cord, embellished with divine gems,
his form intoxicated with divine wine, with a charming smile and beautiful eyes.
And standing on his right side he saw Lakṣmī endowed with auspicious marks,
holding the gestures of boon-giving and fearlessness and a lotus, radiant as saffron, with beautiful eyes,
whose wondrous form was the exemplar for all the maidens of the three worlds;
he saw the Daughter of the Ocean of Beauty seated upon a lotus throne.
He also saw Pitāmaha before Him with folded hands,
and the discus of the All-pervading Lord composed of diverse jewels standing on His left side.
He was being praised by Sanaka and other chief sages, the Teacher of the Universe;

Salutations to You, the foundation of the universe! O Soul of the universe, salutations unto You!
You who are Kaivalya, beyond the three guṇas, smeared with qualities, salutations unto You!
Salutations to You whose nature is purely clean, spotless knowledge;
salutations to You who are known as the Śabda-brahman, whose form is the cosmos!
O destroyer of the sorrow of those fallen and weary in saṃsāra, salutations unto You!
To the piercer of the hard-to-sever knot of the heart, salutations unto You!
Salutations to You, the central pillar of the abode of the fourteen worlds!
Salutations to the Discus-bearer, the architect fashioning millions of cosmic eggs!
Salutations, salutations to the abode of nectar, the ocean of the nectar of compassion!
Salutations to the ocean of mercy, the sole secret refuge for the deliverance of the wretched!
Salutations to the Light of lights that illuminate, such as the sun and others!
Salutations to the fire [consuming] inner sin, shining in each and every individual!
Salutations, salutations to the Purifier, the holy among the holy!
Salutations, salutations to the Heaviest, the Best, the Longest!
Salutations, salutations to the Nearest, the Farthest, the Smallest!
To the choicest one, to the most holy one, O Nārāyaṇa, homage be to you! // 26
Save [me], O Lord of the World, friend of the wretched, homage be to you!

Then the pressing of soma in the horse sacrifice of the king began.
In it, O twice-born, the three worlds became like a single abode. // 1

on the southern shore near Bilveśvara, // 4
the servants appointed by the king, arriving in haste,
with folded hands reported to the king, O twice-born: // 5
"O lord, a huge tree has been seen on the shore of the great ocean,
its top having entered the sea, its base floating on the billows, // 6

Near the bath pavilion, this most wonderful [tree] was seen by us. // 7

Having heard the words of the appointees, the king said to Nārada:

While the two of them, Nārada and the king, were thus pondering,
a bodiless voice was then heard from the sky:
As all who were listening marveled at it, [the voice said:]
“The Lord is not made by human hands; he remains beyond the path of speculation.
Upon the well-concealed great altar, he will descend of his own accord.
Let it remain covered for fifteen days.
This old carpenter who has arrived, tool in hand—
having led him inside, bar the door with care.
Let them play musical instruments outside as long as the fashioning takes place.
For the sound of the carving, if heard, causes deafness and blindness,
causes dwelling in hell, and destroys offspring.
One must not enter within, nor should one ever look.
If anyone other than the appointed one should look, for the king and the kingdom,
and for the beholder as well, there will be great dread and blindness in both eyes.
Therefore, no looking should be done until the completion of the images.

Jaimini said:
Then that protector of the earth, having acted in that way, [attended upon Him],
just as the goddess of speech moving in the sky had spoken, so indeed he attended [upon Him].
As day after day passed in this manner, a celestial fragrance was experienced,
and a shower of pārijāta blossoms, hard to find among mortals,
and the sound of celestial music, and charming songs,
and a shower of the celestial Gaṅgā's water, very beautiful with minute drops.
The fragrance of the rut of the elephants beginning with Airāvata,
which is intolerable to wild elephants, was experienced by all creatures as bringing pleasure.
The gods who had arrived for the sacrifice were all relieved of distress;
seeing Hari manifest, the brahmins performed worship, O twice-born ones.

during the worships offered to the gods, divine signs appeared.
The God Himself completed [the work] in due course on the fifteenth day:
that Lord manifested in four forms, just as I described earlier.
Such as He was described to you formerly, so He appeared,
seated on a celestial throne together with Balabhadra and Sudarśana.
Janārdana had arms radiant with the conch, discus, mace, and lotus;
holding a mace, pestle, discus, and lotus, [the other had] the form of a serpent,
with seven umbrella-shaped hoods, a crown, and bright earrings;
and Subhadrā was charming-faced, holding the gesture of boon-granting, a lotus, and the gesture of fearlessness.
This Lakṣmī manifested embodying all consciousness.

2.2.m: Victory, victory, O Nārāyaṇa, devoted to carrying [souls] across the boundless ocean of existence; whose divine reality is meditated upon by the foremost yogins such as Sanaka, Sanandana, and Sanātana; by whom all elemental principles have been transformed through the superimposition displayed by your own māyā; / O you who embody the three realities, bearer of the triple staff, whose divine knowledge is sung by the Triṇāciketa, Trimadhu, and Trisuparṇa hymns; composed of Vedic meters, fond of Suparṇa, your own seat; dear to devotees, singularly affectionate to devout people; whose true nature is hidden by the veil of your own māyā; universal-formed, illuminator of the universe, facing all directions, with eyes everywhere, with ears everywhere, with feet, heads, and necks everywhere, with hands, noses, tongues, skin, hair, body hair, and liṅga everywhere; soul of all worlds, bringing happiness to all worlds, benefactor of all worlds, saluted by all worlds; from whose lotus of play millions of lotus-born [Brahmās] arise; to whom all gods and demons of the three worlds bow down, along with Rudra, Indra, the Maruts, the Aśvins, the Sādhyas, and hosts of Siddhas; teacher of the three worlds; ungraspable by anyone's intellect: obeisance to you, obeisance! .. 26 ..
