2.2.m: And the other kings, learned scholars who have mastered the Vedas,
sages, twice-born, kṣatriyas, learned men, and vaiśyas .. 27 ..
praised the lotus-eyed, the strong one together with Bhadrā,
with Vedic hymns, praises, purāṇas, and poetic verses as best they could. .. 28 ..
Then Indradyumna addressed the sinless family priest
to perform the worship of Vāsudeva prepared with ceremonial offerings. .. 29 ..
That best of kings himself worshiped them in proper sequence
according to the instruction of Nārada, following the rules and through mantras. .. 30 ..
With the twelve-syllable mantra he worshiped Balabhadra,
by worshiping whom Dhruva attained the supreme state. .. 31 ..
With the great, purifying Puruṣasūkta celebrated in the three Vedas,
the king worshiped Nārāyaṇa according to his ability; .. 32 ..

2.2.s: devyāḥ sūktena bhadrāṃ tāṃ saudarśanyā sudarśanam ..
2.2.d: देव्याः सूक्तेन भद्रां तां सौदर्शन्या सुदर्शनम् ..
2.2.m: with the Devīsūkta [he worshiped] that Bhadrā, and with the Saudarśanī [hymn he worshiped] Sudarśana.
Having worshipped them with devotion according to his wealth, that best of kings,
for their pleasure, bestowed gifts with devotion upon the foremost brahmins:
great gifts, gifts of gold measured against one's weight, the king [gave].
And as ancillary elements of the horse sacrifice, he then gave crores of cows;
he likewise gave other adorned cows accompanied by abundant priestly fees.
From the digging up of the earth by their hooves, O best of brahmins, a ditch arose.
Filled indeed with the water poured in gift-giving, it became a sacred ford yielding great fruit.
Having bathed in it and properly gratified the ancestors and the gods, a man
attains the fruit of a thousand horse sacrifices; of this there is no doubt.
That lake became renowned by the name of King Indradyumna.
If a mortal offers balls of rice here dedicated to the ancestors,
he delivers twenty-one generations of his family and is honored in the world of Brahmā.
No sacred ford is superior to this, since it arose as a part of the horse sacrifice.
Or perhaps the lake of Indradyumna is equal to the Gaṅgā.
Thereupon the king set about the construction of the temple,
at an auspicious time, under a favorable lunar mansion prescribed by astrological rules,
at an auspicious hour, having worshipped the foremost brahmins headed by Nārada.
Having had words of blessing and the success of the undertaking recited, that best of kings
offered arghya at the site of the temple, remembering the Lord of the Universe (Jagannātha).
And having prayed to the Earth for a place to last as long as the moon and stars,
he honored the artisans, preceding it with the sacrifice to the deity of the site.
He also arranged a great festival with abundant singing and musical instruments;
he gave desired objects to the poor, the helpless, and the distressed.
He dismissed the kings with great respect,
who had accomplished their purpose and had their sins destroyed upon seeing that incarnation of Hari.

2.2.s: tataḥ sa koṭiśo vittaṃ dadau pāṣāṇadārake ..
2.2.d: ततः स कोटिशो वित्तं ददौ पाषाणदारके ..
2.2.m: Then that best of kings gave wealth by the crores for stone-cutting
and for fetching stones from many lands.
Filled with joy, the ruler of the earth said this in the assembly:
"Whatever was acquired by my prowess from the eighteen continents,
all of that has been dedicated to the temple of the Lord of the Universe.
Whatever toil was endured by me in the course of victory expeditions,
may that become fruitful for me through the expenditure of wealth for the temple of Viṣṇu!

2.2.s: ataḥ paraṃ me kiṃ bhāgyaṃ carācaraguruṃ harim .. 49 ..
2.2.d: अतः परं मे किं भाग्यं चराचरगुरुं हरिम् .. 49 ..
2.2.m: What fortune for me could be higher than this, that Hari, the teacher of moving and unmoving beings,
I shall propitiate with the wealth and prosperity acquired by the pair of my arms?
Prosperity is ever in the lotus-eyed one; my prosperity was born of her favor.
What indeed could one do without her favor toward the God of gods, the disc-bearer?
He upon whom his sidelong glance falls has all-pervading prosperity,
and the goddess consisting of the eighteen [sciences] dances at the tip of his tongue.
By worshipping whom, the Lord of the Universe, Brahmā attained the state of Brahmā,
Rudra [attained] the status of Maheśvara, and Indra the kingship of the heavenly world,
having worshipped him who is worshipped by the world, I shall worship the Eternal One.
By that great-souled one the threefold accumulation of sins is conquered,
by whom Kṛṣṇa has been worshipped according to the rule, with all his ancillaries and secondary parts.
This sacred field is the body, wherein the all-pervading Lord assumes identity;
for appearance, disappearance, and permanent abiding are of the Lord.
Here, having directly worshipped in bodily form the teacher of the worlds,
one directly attains one's goal, becoming a recipient of the four aims of life.
Whatever royal prosperity has been acquired by me through great expenditure and exertion,
may that become fruitful at his lotus feet through his very grace!
Having fully worshipped the God with all offerings, with materials brought from the sea-girdled earth,

2.2.s: yāvatsamāpnoti hi karmapākaḥ sāmrājyayātrā saphalā hi māstu .. 58 ..
2.2.d: यावत्समाप्नोति हि कर्मपाकः साम्राज्ययात्रा सफला हि मास्तु .. 58 ..
2.2.m: until the ripening of my deeds is complete, may the undertaking of my sovereignty not be in vain!

2.2.s: kiṃ dravyajātaṃ khalu yena viṣṇuṃ nopāharetsāṃgamapetakalmaṣaḥ ..
2.2.d: किं द्रव्यजातं खलु येन विष्णुं नोपाहरेत्सांगमपेतकल्मषः ..
2.2.m: What is the use of an abundance of wealth by which, free from taint, one does not offer everything to Viṣṇu?

2.2.s: kiṃ pauruṣeyaṃ yadi vāsudevaparicchado yena na sādhito me .. 59 ..

2.2.m: What is the use of manly prowess if by it the worshipful service of Vāsudeva has not been accomplished by me?"

2.2.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe puruṣottamakṣetramāhātmye jaimini ṛṣisaṃvāde viṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 20 ..
2.2.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे पुरुषोत्तमक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये जैमिनि ऋषिसंवादे विंशोऽध्यायः .. 20 ..
2.2.m: Thus ends the twentieth chapter in the Praise of the Sacred Field of Puruṣottama, in the Vaiṣṇava Section, in the compilation of eighty-one thousand verses, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the dialogue of the sage Jaimini.
Jaimini said:
To the royal sage speaking thus, a certain brahmin, a master of the Ṛgveda,
a knower of the Vedānta and devoted to wisdom, joyfully spoke these words:
"Ah, great indeed is your mass of fortune, by which the wooden image has appeared on earth,
the supreme worship of which the scripture declares as granting liberation to those deluded by ignorance of the Self!

2.2.s: ya eṣa plavate dāruḥ siṃdhoḥ pāre hyapauruṣam ..
2.2.d: य एष प्लवते दारुः सिंधोः पारे ह्यपौरुषम् ..
2.2.m: This wooden log without human origin that floats on the shore of the ocean—
By worshipping that [log], which is difficult to adore, they attain liberation, which is exceedingly hard to obtain.
Nārada, an actual treasury of the knowledge of Brahman, replied to that [with the words]:
“Indeed, there is no knowledge of Him other than the statement of the Vedānta.

2.2.s: na hi pravṛttirviṣṇostu vinā vedaṃ pravartate ..
2.2.d: न हि प्रवृत्तिर्विष्णोस्तु विना वेदं प्रवर्तते ..
2.2.m: Indeed, Viṣṇu’s manifestation does not occur without the Veda.
In the creation of others or of Himself, the Lord takes the authority of the Śruti [as supreme].
If He were to act without the Śruti, who would accept its authority?
Therefore, O king, this descent here is renowned in the Śruti.
Know this not to be [merely] an image, but the Person to be known through Vedānta, / sung of in the chants of the Sāmaveda,

2.2.s: pratimāṃ na tu jānīhi niḥśreyasakaraṃ nṛṇām .. 7 ..
2.2.d: प्रतिमां न तु जानीहि निःश्रेयसकरं नृणाम् .. 7 ..
2.2.m: the bringer of the highest good to men.

2.2.s: darśanādeva naḥ śāṃtaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ tama uttamam ..
2.2.d: दर्शनादेव नः शांतं सुदृढं तम उत्तमम् ..
2.2.m: By His very darśana, our most deep and dense darkness has been dispelled.
There are indeed ancient Śrutis that reveal worship of Him.
Worship of Him is truly praised when directed toward a real purpose.
Ah, how free of sin are the human beings dwelling in Bhāratavarṣa,
to whom Janārdana, the bestower of liberation, has manifested!
Even there, this land of Oḍhra is the very best of all,
dwelling in which they see Him whose nature is Brahman with physical eyes.
The path of the Śrutis and Smṛtis is difficult, crowded with ritual actions,
treading which, [men] wander here, agitated like water-wheels.
He, consisting of pure consciousness, is the cause of reaching the state free of deceit.
Without means such as [rituals enjoined by] the Śruti, He grants supreme bliss and liberation.
To wicked souls who are miserable with continuous coming and going,
this Viṣṇu in wooden form is a giver of happiness and a good friend.
The rules declared in the Śrutis and Smṛtis do not apply here, O king;
coming in whatever way into the range of sight, He gives liberation down to the outcaste.
Even if a man without devotion should see Him, merely following the crowd,
he will indeed obtain the entire fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices.
If, keeping observances, a devout man of firm mind worships Him,

2.2.s: asaṃśayaṃ sa sāyujyaṃ brahmaṇā labhate naraḥ ..
2.2.d: असंशयं स सायुज्यं ब्रह्मणा लभते नरः ..
2.2.m: that man without doubt attains union with Brahman.
Where is that [action] full of grief and toil, perishable without effort,
short-lived, yielding paltry fruit, and marked by rebirth,
and where is this wooden Brahman, a forest fire to the heap of sins,
granting the liberation of absolute isolation, existence, consciousness, and bliss, even by darśana?
The study of the Vedas and other [rites] are difficult to perform for wicked souls;
what is to be attained through these by great souls, that He will grant effortlessly.
In other sacred fields, the Lord is very far from mortal dwellers;
in His own sacred field, the omnipresent Lord, the bestower of liberation, resides eternally.
Therefore, O fortunate one, stay here, having the prowess of your own strength;
you are most wise and devoted; worship Him along with His major and minor limbs.”
Jaimini said:
Having heard those words of the twice-born [sage], Nārada, delighted in mind, [said]:
“Well spoken by the best of the twice-born, who follows the path of the Śruti!
At the beginning of creation, the collection of the Vedas arose from the breaths of Brahman;
there, this meaning of the Upaniṣads has now attained manifestation.
The blessed lotus-born Lord of creatures knows this meaning,
and I, O king, have just now learned [it] from his mouth.
By his command everything has been accomplished as desired by you.
Having worshipped Him, remain here; I am going into the presence of Brahmā.
I will report what has been done and the manifestation of the foe of Mura.

2.2.s: prāsādaṃ kuru bhūpāla dhanena mahatā tathā .. 27 ..
2.2.d: प्रासादं कुरु भूपाल धनेन महता तथा .. 27 ..
2.2.m: Build a temple, O king, with great wealth; / and likewise,
having installed Narasiṃha in the temple, you will be liberated.”
Jaimini said:

2.2.s: tacchrutvā sa tu bhūmīṃdraḥ pratyuvāca muniṃ tadā ..
2.2.d: तच्छ्रुत्वा स तु भूमींद्रः प्रत्युवाच मुनिं तदा ..
2.2.m: Hearing that, the lord of the earth then replied to the sage:
“O great seer, I wish to go with you to the presence of Brahmā,
by whose favor Jagannātha has become a guest of my eyes.

2.2.s: nivedya taṃ ca prāsādaṃ pratiṣṭhārthaṃ muradviṣaḥ .. 2.2.21.30 ..
2.2.d: निवेद्य तं च प्रासादं प्रतिष्ठार्थं मुरद्विषः .. 2.2.21.30 ..
2.2.m: Reporting that temple for the installation of the foe of Mura,
I shall request in his presence the festival of the temple’s installation,
so that the Grandfather, coming himself from the world of Brahmā,
will celebrate the great festival of the Lord in this temple.

2.2.s: tanmune māmapi vidheḥ saṃnidhiṃ prāpayasva ca .. 32 ..
2.2.d: तन्मुने मामपि विधेः संनिधिं प्रापयस्व च .. 32 ..
2.2.m: Therefore, O sage, bring me too into the presence of the Creator.
Having completed the consecration of the inner sanctuary in the temple, I have remained here, O sage.”
Afterwards, we two shall go. Wait for me for a short time.
Then that king [summoned] all those skilled in the science of architecture,
and individually in the work of joining stone blocks,
he respectfully engaged them with hospitality, gifts, and honors.

2.2.s: dine dine sughaṭitaḥ prāsādo vavṛdhe dvijāḥ .. 35 ..
2.2.d: दिने दिने सुघटितः प्रासादो ववृधे द्विजाः .. 35 ..
2.2.m: Day by day, O twice-born ones, the well-constructed temple grew,
being filled on all sides like the moon in the bright fortnight.
Even while being thus built up, though the temple was enlarged,
because of its immense height, it was not perceived [to grow] in a short time.
The count of stones might somehow be possible from the sequence of joining,

2.2.s: vittavyayastu koṭīnāṃ na saṃkhyātuṃ ca śakyate ..
2.2.d: वित्तव्ययस्तु कोटीनां न संख्यातुं च शक्यते ..
2.2.m: but the expenditure of crores of wealth cannot be counted.
As many people as lived in Bhārata-varṣa abiding by their duties,
they were all employed by King Indradyumna, ruler of the earth.
Those who were appointed one by one, joined together with one another,
and those appointed by others—they were all set to work there.
The great, continuous roar born of the joy of those employed,
pervading the sky, filled the regions of the directions.
Propitiated by the king's faith, devotion, and purity,
O brahmins, the king's fortune flourished together with his fame.
In some places it shone brightly with various gems inlaid in gold;
in some places its luster resembled an autumn cloud amid sections of crystal;
in some places the wall, made of sapphire stone, was dark and dense like a raincloud.
When the delightful temple of Viṣṇu was thus well constructed,
that best of kings, having properly performed the foundation rite of the sanctum,
in order to avert lightning strikes, breakage, and the like, as prescribed,
having placed jewels and other objects obtained by effort according to the treatises on architecture,
further, [collecting] whatever was appropriate for the equipment of the temple's construction,
he carefully deposited there an abundance of costly items.
Then, as this fame-increasing temple was being fashioned—

2.2.s: manasāpi na saṃbhāvye triṣu lokeṣu bhūbhujām .. 47 ..
2.2.d: मनसापि न संभाव्ये त्रिषु लोकेषु भूभुजाम् .. 47 ..
2.2.m: unimaginable even in thought to the kings in the three worlds,
not seen even by the gods who abide until the end of the kalpa, O twice-born ones—

2.2.s: prāsāda īdṛśo bhūmau kvacicca ghaṭito na hi .. 48 ..
2.2.d: प्रासाद ईदृशो भूमौ क्वचिच्च घटितो न हि .. 48 ..
2.2.m: “No such temple has ever been built on earth,
or in heaven!” Thus the Ādityas conversed among themselves:
“Ah, how lofty is his good intellect, which has matured in this way!
Longing through faith for the lotus feet of the Blessed Lord,
they indeed witness and even accomplish extraordinary deeds!
Which kings here on earth have been endowed with political wisdom,
universal emperors, conquerors of the realm of all enemies,

2.2.s: vittāni yaiḥ saṃcitāni subahūni ca koṭiśaḥ ..
2.2.d: वित्तानि यैः संचितानि सुबहूनि च कोटिशः ..
2.2.m: by whom wealth was amassed in very great abundance, in crores?
Yet the thousand horse sacrifices that were performed for the Lord of Heaven,

2.2.s: śakyaṃ vā syādbhūbhujāṃ tu nātaḥ pūrvamanuṣṭhitam..
2.2.d: शक्यं वा स्याद्भूभुजां तु नातः पूर्वमनुष्ठितम्..
2.2.m: could that be possible for [other] kings? Nothing like this was ever performed before!

2.2.s: na dṛṣṭaṃ na śrutaṃ vāpi vājimedhasahasrakam..53..
2.2.d: न दृष्टं न श्रुतं वापि वाजिमेधसहस्रकम्..53..
2.2.m: Never was a thousand horse sacrifices seen or heard of,
performed by any ruler of the earth, wherein the dwellers of the three worlds
assembled on earth together with this king to enjoy pleasures!

2.2.s: brahmaloka ivābhāti sabha yasya ca yajvinaḥ..
2.2.d: ब्रह्मलोक इवाभाति सभ यस्य च यज्विनः..
2.2.m: The sacrificial assembly of this sacrificer shines like the world of Brahmā,
where the three Vedas take embodied form, and the bull [of Dharma] stands on four legs,
and where the gods, their wishes fulfilled, were struck with wonder.
Indeed, this best of temples has become an object [comprehensible only] to his intellect,

2.2.s: mano'pi yatra bhavati na vā trailokyavāsinām ..
2.2.d: मनोऽपि यत्र भवति न वा त्रैलोक्यवासिनाम् ..
2.2.m: where even the mind of the inhabitants of the three worlds cannot reach.
What could be difficult to attain for a king whose helper is Nārada,
and the Grandfather, the creator of the worlds, the lord of all the immortals?
Or rather, nothing that a devotee of Viṣṇu desires to do is too distant;
there is no difference between Viṣṇu and the people who are his devotees, O twice-born one.”

2.2.s: tataḥ sa nāradaṃ prāha prāsādāṃte munīśvaram .. 59 ..
2.2.d: ततः स नारदं प्राह प्रासादांते मुनीश्वरम् .. 59 ..
2.2.m: Then, upon the completion of the temple, he said to Nārada, lord of sages:
“Everything that was impossible for gods and demons has succeeded for me.
Devoted to the non-dual worship of the Blessed Lord Viṣṇu directly,
may this temple, resembling the body of the Blessed Lord, endure long for me.”
Having spoken thus, he bowed with his head at the feet of Nārada.
Nārada, raising him up and honoring the best of kings, [said:]

2.2.s: tvatto na bhedo nṛpate mamāsti khalu tattvataḥ..63..
2.2.d: त्वत्तो न भेदो नृपते ममास्ति खलु तत्त्वतः..63..
2.2.m: “In truth, O king, there is no difference between me and you,
since Jagannātha himself has manifested directly, or [will do so] by what has been done.”
You must certainly worship him; you are now liberated while living.
Just as your mind is filled with devotion toward his lotus feet,

2.2.s: bhaktyā hyananyayā puṃsaḥ kimataḥ paramasti vai..64..
2.2.d: भक्त्या ह्यनन्यया पुंसः किमतः परमस्ति वै..64..
2.2.m: for a person possessed of undivided devotion, what indeed is higher than this?
What could be obtained through sacred fords, mantras, recitations, gifts, sacrifices with lavish priestly fees,
vows, Vedic study, O king, and austerities,

2.2.s: na śakyaṃ tava rājendra bhaktyā tatkaramāgatam ..
2.2.d: न शक्यं तव राजेन्द्र भक्त्या तत्करमागतम् ..
2.2.m: which was impossible [to attain], O best of kings, has come into your hand through devotion.

2.2.s: ataḥ paraṃ na śocasva bhaktiyoge namo'stu te .. 66 ..
2.2.d: अतः परं न शोचस्व भक्तियोगे नमोऽस्तु ते .. 66 ..
2.2.m: Therefore, grieve no more; homage to you in the yoga of devotion!
Remaining long on this earth, O supreme among kings, in great excellence,
worship Jagannātha with offerings and great festivals.

2.2.s: sa mūlaṃ jagatāmādistasya romāṇi yāni vai .. tāni kalpadrumākhyāni śaṃkhacakrāṃkitāni vai .. 61 ..
2.2.d: स मूलं जगतामादिस्तस्य रोमाणि यानि वै .. तानि कल्पद्रुमाख्यानि शंखचक्रांकितानि वै .. 61 ..
2.2.m: he is the root, the origin of the worlds. His hairs, indeed, / are named the wish-fulfilling trees, marked with the conch and the discus.
This tree, situated in their midst, is presided over by consciousness, O gods;
the True Person has arisen of himself in the water of the ocean.
Janārdana, having a wooden body, in order to enjoy the pleasures of the three worlds,
cultivated through the yoga of devotion across many thousands of births,
was prayed to by me formerly for the destruction of dreadful worldly existence,
with a mind distressed by repeated creation, dissolution, and maintenance.
For the destruction of all karmas, for the total liberation of the worlds,
even without the difficult yogas of concentration and meditation,
the Blessed One, Puruṣottama, became manifest for the sake of liberation.
His body is concealed; one should not scrutinize his sacred field.
According to the measure of the subject's perception, as he is seen, just so is he;

2.2.s: caturvargaprado devo yo yathā taṃ vibhāvayet .. 67 ..

2.2.m: the god grants the four aims of life according to however one conceives of him.
With the mass of their sins destroyed by his darśana, by degrees on earth
men become pure-souled and recipients of liberation."
Jaimini said:
Hearing this nectar of words from the Lotus-Born [Brahmā],
the delighted gods reflected with overjoyed inner selves:
"Leaving behind this fleeting divinity and going to the earth,
let us worship the god in this excellent sacred field, fully self-controlled."
Seeing the gods with faces blooming with joy, the Grandfather [said]:
"The Lord who has become visible to bestow grace on Indradyumna,
the image of his that has arrived here, will speak of his own accord;
the Blessed One, fond of his devotees, will grant many boons.
In order to consecrate the All-Pervading One in the temple of Indradyumna,

2.2.s: ahaṃ cāpi gamiṣyāmi yūyaṃ tatra prayāta vai .. 73 ..
2.2.d: अहं चापि गमिष्यामि यूयं तत्र प्रयात वै .. 73 ..
2.2.m: I too will go; you must go there indeed.
Let Indradyumna go ahead to gather the materials for the consecration;
you, whose terms of office are expired, be his assistants there.

2.2.m: The first manvantara has indeed passed now, O gods;
going there together with Indradyumna, O best of gods,
he shall maintain ownership of the temple and the images.
Therefore, having collected the provisions, accompanied by helpers, he now
on the earth, even from the remembrance of his lineage and connections—
by my command, the Padmanidhi will go with [him] to the earth
in preparation for all the items for the consecration of the Blessed One."

2.2.s: indradyumno'pi hṛṣṭātmā dṛṣṭvā brāhmīṃ śriyaṃ dvijāḥ .. 78 ..
2.2.d: इन्द्रद्युम्नोऽपि हृष्टात्मा दृष्ट्वा ब्राह्मीं श्रियं द्विजाः .. 78 ..
2.2.m: Indradyumna too, his soul delighted upon seeing the glory of Brahmā, O twice-born,

2.2.m: Thus ends the twenty-third chapter in the Puruṣottamakṣetra-māhātmya, in the second Vaiṣṇava Section of the eighty-one-thousand-verse collection of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the dialogue of the sage Jaimini. (23)
Jaimini said:
Having arrived before Jagannātha, his mind longing for a long time,
he bowed down like a staff, covered in an armor of dense horripilation:
"Reverence to the god friendly to brahmins, and for the welfare of cows and brahmins,
for the destruction of the affliction of the bowed, the sole cause of the four aims of life;
to the one having the form of Hiraṇyagarbha, the Spirit, the Primal Matter, and the manifest!
Oṃ, reverence to Vāsudeva, whose essential nature is pure knowledge!"
Uttering this praise, the king, with eyes filled with tears of joy,
making circumambulation again and again, bowed down repeatedly.
Then the other deities who had arrived there, filled with joy,
bowed down with palms joined in reverence, and praised the god with delight.
The gods said:
The Puruṣa has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet.
Pervading the earth on every side, he stood beyond it by ten fingers.
That Puruṣa who is sung as the supreme Brahman, the Supreme Self—

2.2.s: bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ ca sarvaṃ puruṣa eva tat .. 7 ..
2.2.d: भूतं भव्यं भविष्यं च सर्वं पुरुष एव तत् .. 7 ..
2.2.m: past, present, and future: all that is the Puruṣa alone.
Such is his greatness; yet greater than that is the Puruṣa, the Lord.
One quarter of him is all beings; three quarters of him are the immortal in heaven.
From you the Vedic meters were born, and from you the sacrificial Puruṣa also.
From you horses were born, as well as cows, sheep, and the rest.
The brahmins were born from your mouth; the kṣatriyas arose from your arms.
The vaiśyas arose from your thighs; likewise the śūdras came forth from your feet.
The moon was born from your mind, the sun from your eye.
From your ears the wind [arose], with the vital breaths; and from your tongue the bearer of oblations.
From your navel the atmosphere arose, and the sky from your head.

2.2.s: pādābhyāṃ te dharā jātā diśaścāṣṭau śrutergatāḥ .. 12 ..
2.2.d: पादाभ्यां ते धरा जाता दिशश्चाष्टौ श्रुतेर्गताः .. 12 ..
2.2.m: From your feet the earth was born, and the eight directions proceeded from your hearing.
Seven were its enclosing sticks, and thrice seven its kindling-sticks from you.
All things moving and unmoving were indeed born from you alone.
You alone are the Lord of the worlds; you alone are the protector;
and with a fierce form, you alone are the destroyer, O Supreme Lord!
You alone are the sacrifice, the sacrifice's share; you are the Lord of sacrifice, higher than the highest.
You are beyond the Sound-Brahman, yet you are the Sound-Brahman, the ruler of the universe.
You are the self-ruler, the emperor, Jagannātha, the cosmic sovereign, O Lord of the world!

2.2.s: adhaścordhvaṃ ca tiryaktvaṃ tvayā vyāptaṃ jaganmaya .. 16 ..
2.2.d: अधश्चोर्ध्वं च तिर्यक्त्वं त्वया व्याप्तं जगन्मय .. 16 ..
2.2.m: Below, above, and across—all has been pervaded by you, O you whose essence is the world!

2.2.s: prāpnuvaṃti paraṃ sthānaṃ tvāṃ yajaṃtaśca yājñikāḥ..
2.2.d: प्राप्नुवंति परं स्थानं त्वां यजंतश्च याज्ञिकाः..
2.2.m: Sacrificers who worship you attain the supreme abode.

2.2.s: bhojyaṃ bhoktā havirhotā havanaṃ tvaṃ phalapradaḥ .. 17 ..
2.2.d: भोज्यं भोक्ता हविर्होता हवनं त्वं फलप्रदः .. 17 ..
2.2.m: You are the food, the enjoyer, the oblation, the priest, the offering, and the bestower of fruits.
You are the enjoyer of all actions; you consist of all actions, O Lord!
You are the instrument of all actions, the bestower of the fruits of all actions.
You are indeed the instigator of action, the bestower of the attainment of duty, pleasure, and wealth.

2.2.s: tvāmṛte muktidaḥ ko'nyo hṛṣīkeśa namo'stu te .. 19 ..
2.2.d: त्वामृते मुक्तिदः कोऽन्यो हृषीकेश नमोऽस्तु ते .. 19 ..
2.2.m: Except for you, who else can grant liberation? O Hṛṣīkeśa, homage be to you!
Homage to the endless one of a thousand forms, with a thousand feet, eyes, heads, thighs, and arms!
Homage to the Puruṣa of a thousand names, the eternal one, the sustainer of thousands of crores of cosmic ages!
Having fallen from our offices, we have resorted to you for refuge, O Lord!
Save us, O lotus-eyed one; become the refuge of the refuge-less!
You alone are the refuge of a creature fallen into worldly existence, O Lord!
In all your creation there is no one like you who protects the distressed.
You are the sole refuge of the helpless and distressed, the father of the world, O Lord!
You alone, O Lord, are the protector, the nourisher, the averter of all calamities.

2.2.s: trāhi viṣṇo jagannātha trāhi naḥ parameśvara ..
2.2.d: त्राहि विष्णो जगन्नाथ त्राहि नः परमेश्वर ..
2.2.m: Save us, O Viṣṇu, Lord of the world! Save us, O Supreme Lord!
Except for you, O beloved of Kamalā, who is capable of protecting us?
Homage to the inner controller! Homage to the treasury of all splendour!
While praising [him] thus, those gods, having bowed down again and again,
along with Indradyumna, went outside, O best of brahmins.

2.2.s: kṣetraṃ śrīnarasiṃhasya gatvā taṃ praṇipatya ca ..
2.2.d: क्षेत्रं श्रीनरसिंहस्य गत्वा तं प्रणिपत्य च ..
2.2.m: Having gone to the sacred field of venerable Narasiṃha and prostrated before him,
having paid homage with supreme devotion and worshipped the man-lion,
they went to the peak of the Nīlācala mountain, where the supreme temple stood,
together with the treasure-spirit Padmanidhi, for the purpose of [gathering] materials.
They saw [the temple], towering exceedingly high, encompassing the vault of the sky,
as if it were the Vindhya mountain rising to block the path of the sun,
pervading all quarters, brilliant with wonderful construction,
wondrous with patterns of auspicious motifs that had endured over a great length of time.
And then that Vaiṣṇava Indradyumna reflected:
“Long ago I went from here to Satyaloka for the purpose of [its] construction.
After a very long time, this complete, excellent temple has come into the range of my vision.
This is indeed due to the grace of the Lord; human effort has no role here.
Where is the end of a manvantara, which obstructed [even] the sun, moon, and Indra?

2.2.s: tathāpi tiṣṭhate cāyaṃ prāsādo hyeṣa durlabhaḥ ... 33 ..
2.2.d: तथापि तिष्ठते चायं प्रासादो ह्येष दुर्लभः ... 33 ..
2.2.m: Even so, this temple, so hard to attain, still stands!
For temples built by men are like anthills:
they crumble from growing trees, their lifespan lasting but a short time.
Indeed, out of compassion for me, the dwelling of Hari has been preserved.”
Then he addressed those companions with humble words:
"Know that a temple for the Lord of the universe has been built by me.
The Lord himself manifested with a form made of wood.
Then a bodiless voice resounding in the sky spoke to me: // 36
'Have a temple measuring a thousand cubits built upon the summit of Nīlādri,
for the dwelling of the Lord of the universe.' // 37
In the rite of consecration of this [temple], he will come here in person—
the lotus-born [Brahmā] himself, together with the Siddhas, the brahmin seers, and the gods. // 38

2.2.s: tadatra kriyate ko vā saṃbhāro jñāyate katham ..
2.2.d: तदत्र क्रियते को वा संभारो ज्ञायते कथम् ..
2.2.m: Therefore, what provision is to be made here? How is it known?"
To him who had spoken thus, the gods, deprived of their offices, said: // 39
The gods said:
"Even we do not know that. Our teacher is the preceptor [Bṛhaspati];

2.2.s: idānīṃ na vaśe'smākaṃ sa hi svargaparo hitaḥ .. 2.2.24.40 ..
2.2.d: इदानीं न वशेऽस्माकं स हि स्वर्गपरो हितः .. 2.2.24.40 ..
2.2.m: he is not under our control now, for he is devoted to heaven and its welfare." // 40
Padmanidhi said:
"Master, by the instruction of Brahmā, I have come with you.

2.2.s: kartavyaṃ kiṃ mayā cātra kiṃ vā vastu pratīkṣyate .. 41 ..
2.2.d: कर्तव्यं किं मया चात्र किं वा वस्तु प्रतीक्ष्यते .. 41 ..
2.2.m: What must be done by me here, or what material is awaited?" // 41
Jaimini said:
As they were conversing thus, Nārada stood before them,
sent previously by Brahmā, expert in all sacred scriptures. // 42
"O sage, prepare all the materials of provision according to the scriptures;
the treasure Padmaka will provide them at your command." // 43

2.2.s: taṃ dṛṣṭvā te mudā yuktā uttasthurbrahmaṇaḥ sutam ..
2.2.d: तं दृष्ट्वा ते मुदा युक्ता उत्तस्थुर्ब्रह्मणः सुतम् ..
2.2.m: Seeing him, the son of Brahmā, filled with joy, they stood up;
the best of kings worshipped him with the worship of the sixfold offering. // 44
Those gods bearing human form also bowed down to him.
Indradyumna too spoke to him concerning the items for the consecration ritual: // 45
"I do not know, O best of sages, having long been abandoned by my family priest;
direct me in proper order, O brahmin, whatever is to be procured." // 46

2.2.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe puruṣottamakṣetramāhātmye jaiminiṛṣisaṃvāde caturviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 24 ..
2.2.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे पुरुषोत्तमक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये जैमिनिऋषिसंवादे चतुर्विंशोऽध्यायः .. 24 ..
2.2.m: Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter in the conversation of the sage Jaimini, in the Glorious Field of Puruṣottama, in the second Vaiṣṇava Section of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. // 24
Jaimini said:

2.2.s: ityukte nāradaḥ so'tha yathāśāstraṃ vicārya vai ..
2.2.d: इत्युक्ते नारदः सोऽथ यथाशास्त्रं विचार्य वै ..
2.2.m: When this was said, Nārada, deliberating according to the scriptures,

2.2.s: ālekhya kramaśaḥ patre rājñe tasmai nyavedayat .. 1 ..
2.2.d: आलेख्य क्रमशः पत्रे राज्ञे तस्मै न्यवेदयत् .. 1 ..
2.2.m: wrote it down in order on a leaf and presented it to that king. // 1
The king, too, hearing that document and considering it again and again,
handed over whatever was written there to Padmanidhi: // 2
"Procure [them], O Padmanidhi! Make a golden pavilion,

2.2.s: brahmaṇaḥ sadanaṃ divyaṃ brahmarṣīṇāṃ ca nirmalam .. 3..
2.2.d: ब्रह्मणः सदनं दिव्यं ब्रह्मर्षीणां च निर्मलम् .. 3..
2.2.m: a divine residence for Brahmā, and an immaculate one for the brahmin seers; // 3
for Indra and the other gods, for the Siddhas, for the inhabitants of the mortal realm,
for the chief sages, and for the dwelling of the kings who dwell in Pātāla; // 4
likewise for the serpent-kings, O treasure, and for the inhabitants of the three worlds.
Unflaggingly, house by house, equipped with appropriate seats, // 5
quickly have the entire collection of materials prepared, O treasure!
Viśvakarman also will render assistance to you." // 6
To Indradyumna, who was issuing these orders, that sage said:
"Aside from the provisions, this must be done with careful arrangement: // 7
a triad of fine chariots, well-fashioned with gold, decorated
with silk, necklaces of jewels, and the like, very costly, strong, and large. // 8
The chariot of glorious Vāsudeva should be marked with the Garuḍa banner;
let a lotus banner be fixed at the top of Subhadrā's chariot. // 9
A chariot with sixteen wheels should be made with effort for Viṣṇu,
one with fourteen for Bala, and one with twelve for Subhadrā. // 10
The chariot of the wielder of the discus should have a width of sixteen cubits,
fourteen for Bala, and twelve for Subhadrā. // 11
He is the seat of the worlds, repeatedly; he is himself the embodiment of his own seat;

2.2.s: tadyāne jagatāṃ nāśastato yānaṃ na vidyate .. 12 ..
2.2.d: तद्याने जगतां नाशस्ततो यानं न विद्यते .. 12 ..
2.2.m: in his conveyance lies the destruction of the worlds, therefore there is no [ordinary] vehicle. // 12
He sees the moving and unmoving universe in the spotless mirror of knowledge;
a spotless mirror is always located on the palm of his hand. // 13
Because it is in the palm (tala), it is a palm-tree (tāla); the Lord is always marked by it;
therefore, that belongs to Śeṣa, who has incarnated as Balabhadra. // 14
Or rather, for the plow-bearer, the plow itself should be made as the supreme banner;
a spotless banner is to be made, hence it is considered a palm-tree banner (tāladhvaja). // 15
This deity must not be placed upon an unconsecrated chariot, O king;

2.2.s: prāsāde maṃḍape vāpi pure tanniṣphalaṃ bhavet .. 16 ..
2.2.d: प्रासादे मंडपे वापि पुरे तन्निष्फलं भवेत् .. 16 ..
2.2.m: in a temple, in a hall, or in a city, that would become fruitless. // 16

2.2.s: tasmātpratiṣṭhā prathamaṃ hareḥ kāryā rathasya vai ..
2.2.d: तस्मात्प्रतिष्ठा प्रथमं हरेः कार्या रथस्य वै ..
2.2.m: "Therefore, the consecration of Hari's chariot must certainly be performed first.

2.2.s: saṃbhāraḥ kriyatāṃ tasya hyanuṣṭheyā mayā tu sā .. 17 ..
2.2.d: संभारः क्रियतां तस्य ह्यनुष्ठेया मया तु सा .. 17 ..
2.2.m: Let the provisions for it be prepared; and it must indeed be carried out by me.
Having obtained this instruction from my father, O king, I shall quickly come [back]."
Hearing that speech of his, the triad of chariots was constructed
in a single day by Viśvakarman with materials procured from the treasury:
with excellent axles, excellent wheels, excellent pillars, very spacious, with beautiful archways,
with splendid standards and fine banners, delightful with diverse decorative work,
adorned with arrays of sculpted figures of couples in varied embraces,
embellished with half-gold, resembling the very chariot of the Sun,
with a rumble deep as a cloud, endowed with ropes for pulling when seen,
yoked with horses swift as wind, a hundred in number and radiant white.
It was consecrated by Nārada according to the injunctions of the scriptures,
at an auspicious ascendant, an auspicious muhūrta, and on a favorable lunar day indicated by astrology.
The sages said:

2.2.s: bhagavañjaimine brūhi sarvajñosi mato hi naḥ ..23..
2.2.d: भगवञ्जैमिने ब्रूहि सर्वज्ञोसि मतो हि नः ..23..
2.2.m: O venerable Jaimini, tell us; for we consider you omniscient.

2.2.s: vidhinā kena hi rathaḥ pratiṣṭhāpyo harerayam ..
2.2.d: विधिना केन हि रथः प्रतिष्ठाप्यो हरेरयम् ..
2.2.m: By what rite should this chariot of Hari be consecrated?
Tell us accurately, so that we may know the full details of the ritual.
Jaimini said:
How it was consecrated by that high-souled Nārada,

2.2.s: tadvo vadiṣyāmi vidhiṃ yathā dṛṣṭaṃ purā mayā .. 25 ..
2.2.d: तद्वो वदिष्यामि विधिं यथा दृष्टं पुरा मया .. 25 ..
2.2.m: that rite I shall tell you, just as it was seen by me formerly.
Having erected a very beautiful pavilion in the northeast direction of the chariot,

2.2.s: tanmadhye maṇḍapaṃ kṛtvā vediṃ tatra sunirmalām ..26..
2.2.d: तन्मध्ये मण्डपं कृत्वा वेदिं तत्र सुनिर्मलाम् ..26..
2.2.m: and having made a hall in its center, [he made] a spotless altar there,
four-cornered, measuring four cubits, and one cubit high, O twice-born ones.
On the night preceding the day of consecration, to the north, at an auspicious
muhūrta, having recited auspicious benedictions, he should perform the offering of sprouts;
and having given offerings to the thirty-two deities according to rule,
in the morning he should then draw a diagram in the middle of the altar:

2.2.s: padmaṃ vā svastikaṃ vāpi kumbhaṃ tatra nidhāpayet .. 29 ..
2.2.d: पद्मं वा स्वस्तिकं वापि कुम्भं तत्र निधापयेत् .. 29 ..
2.2.m: either a lotus or a svastika; and he should place a water-pot there.
The wise [priest] should fill its interior with the decoction of five trees,
sacred waters from the Gaṅgā and other rivers, sprouts together with earth,
all kinds of perfumes, the five jewels, and the collection of all medicinal herbs.
Having filled it according to rule, the preceptor, pure and facing east,
meditating on Viṣṇu, should subsequently fill it with the five products of the cow;
tied with fine cloth at its neck, with garlands and very beautiful perfumes,
furnished with fruits and sprouts, and having auspicious festive threads tied [to it].
There he should worship the Lord of gods, the flawless Narasiṃha,
with the king of mantras according to rule, and with internal offerings;
having prayed [to him] for grace, and invoking that Hari into it,
he should worship him with various external offerings according to rule, O twice-born ones.
To the northwest of that water-pot, sacrificial twigs, clarified butter, and boiled oblation-rice,
one thousand and eight [oblations], the guru should offer into the fire according to rule;
and at the end of that, he should place the residual drops into the middle of the pot.
Having made the chariot very beautiful with banners, perfumes, and garlands,
he should sprinkle all its parts with scented sandalwood water.
He should fumigate it with black agallochum, amid sounds of conches and large horns;
and having installed Samīraṇa upon the banner of that Nṛsiṃha,
and having worshipped [him] according to rule with red garlands, perfumes, and wreaths,

In a level place, free from portents, and in accordance with prescribed ritual rules,
the gods were brought near the temple at an auspicious moment.
Then an immense pavilion, fashioned with jeweled colors,
was constructed by Viśvakarman at the command of Indradyumna.

various kinds of food, as well as manifold songs and dances [were arranged].

Jaimini said:
To Gāla, that elephant among kings, who was making this submission,
he, smiling, spoke these words: "O king, why do you speak at such length?
You too are a devotee of Hari, a universal sovereign and ruler of the earth.
This lordship over the land is common to kings who dwell on earth.
For at present, you are the sole monarch here on earth.
All religious rites of mortals and even of the gods depend upon the king.
The king was created by Brahmā from portions of the guardians of the eight directions;
indeed, a king intent on protecting his subjects has not made small merit.

2.2.m: Gāla stood near him as if he were an obedient servant;
he quickly carried out everything that Indradyumna commanded.
Thus, with all materials gathered, the lord seated on the throne,
Indradyumna, surrounded by gods, shone like Śakra.
Then auspicious sounds born from celestial kettle-drums were heard,
the sounds of clay drums, flutes, lute, cymbals, large drums, and the like,
many trumpetings of Airāvata and other elephants in the sky,
and shouts of victory on all sides mingled with showers of flowers,
drops of water from the heavenly Gaṅgā mixed with Mandāra flowers,
the scents of divine garlands, unguents, and incenses pervading the directions,
and the tinkling sounds of clusters of small bells belonging to gods in their aerial chariots.
And then a mass of brilliance filling the space between heaven and earth,
covering the eyes of those standing on earth, appeared, O twice-born ones.
Looked upon in front by the subjects with rows of upturned eyes,
then by degrees was seen that foremost aerial chariot of the Lord of Creatures,
carried on the shoulder from all sides by hundreds of golden swans,
attended in front by the guardians of the directions with hands busy holding fly-whisks,
with the water of the Jāhnavī and Yamunā sprinkled around by their hands,
with two parasols held on both sides by the Moon and the Sun,
whose canopies trembled gently with the movement of the wind,
being praised with secret hymns by the brahmin seers headed by Gautama,
seated in its center, the Lord of Creatures, praised by Indradyumna and others,
was seen, extolled with shouts of victory by the hosts of gods.
Courtesans headed by Rambhā danced with reverent awe,
and singers headed by Hāhā and Hūhū were singing;
he was accompanied respectfully on the lute by hosts of Siddhas and Vidyādharas,
and worshipped from afar by ascetics with joined hands.
Sāvitrī and Śāradā, by varied compositions of speech,
were bringing him satisfaction—who else would be capable of pleasing him?
His body was sprinkled with the water of the Jāhnavī and Yamunā.
And those Gandharvas, Siddhas, and others, the twice-born headed by Nārada,
holding canes in their hands, were showing the divine stairway with humility.
Great was that crowd of gods moving in the sky;

Jaimini said:
Then, from the sky, a flight of stairs fashioned of jewels and gold,
attached to the footstool of the lotus-born [Brahmā] residing in his vimāna,
with its base touching the earth for the Creator's descent,
provided with a wide flight of steps four fathoms across,
like a radiant rainbow between the chariot and the temple,
suddenly appeared, beheld with wonder by the people. // 3
Then, O twice-born ones, led by kings of the Gandharvas / holding cane wands of jewels in their hands,
who pointed out the path, saying, 'This is the way, O Lord, come!',
resting his hands in the hands of Durvāsas and Nārada,
he descended the stairs, purifying the world with his glance. // 5
Smiling as he beheld the chariots and the splendidly adorned temple,
and the pavilion extending to the ends of the quarters, beautified with jeweled pillars,
which even struck wonder into Indra, filled with all kinds of provisions,
he descended from the vimāna, [accompanied] by gods, brahmin seers, and kings,
praised on all sides by those whose folded hands touched their diadems.
Whichever quarter the Grandfather favored with his sidelong glance,
tens of millions of folded hands were raised to heads in dense crowds there.
Seeing Indradyumna bowed at his lotus feet, the Lord of creatures
spoke with gentle words, his lips parted in a smile,
pointing with his finger to the gods, the ancestors, the brahmin seers, and the ascetics,
as well as the Siddhas, Vidyādharas, Yakṣas, Gandharvas, and apsarases,
all gathered together at once, filled with joy: // 11
'Behold, O Indradyumna, your good fortune, which captivates all the worlds!
For your sake, all of them have assembled together at once, placing me at their head.' // 12
Having said this, he then went quickly to the chariot of Nārāyaṇa.
Bowing low to Jagannātha and circumambulating [him] three times, the Grandfather,
plunged into an ocean of bliss, his body bristling with horripilation,
then praised his own Self directly before him, his voice choked [with emotion]: // 14

Jaimini said:
Then, by the majesty of the mantra, the Man-Lion, the Lord,
was seen by Indradyumna and all the others in a wondrous form,
licking the entire universe all around with his blazing tongue,
as if risen to swallow the entire Rudra of cosmic fire at the end of time,
pervading the vault of heaven and earth with his fiercely scorching splendour,
the all-pervading Lord possessing manifold eyes, faces, necks, hands, feet, and ears,
a deity full of all wonders, a sheer repository of fiery energy.
Terrified with fear and agitated, they were not even able to praise the Lord.
Seeing him of such a form, Nārada then
asked his father: “O blessed one, why does he appear thus?
Nārada said:
He descended for blessing, yet he inspires fear.
All are now petrified with fear, suspecting the cosmic dissolution.
You alone, O blessed one, know his divine sport, O Lord of the worlds.”
Hearing those words of Nārada, the lotus-born [Brahmā], smiling,
spoke curious words beneficial to all.
Brahmā said:
“Seeing Jagannātha descended and bearing a wooden body,
the worlds will disregard him, though he is directly of the nature of Brahman.
Foolish people who do not know the truth must know his greatness.
He has been addressed with the king of mantras by which Parameṣṭhin,
invoked by which formerly, tore apart the great asura.
Having assumed such a form exceedingly difficult to behold and terrifying,
this form is the highest culmination of Viṣṇu of immeasurable fiery energy,
by worshipping which people attain the state from which rebirth is hard to encounter.
Facing Nṛsiṃha, he, filled with joy, spoke this praise:
“Obeisance to you, peerless lion among the foremost gods! Obeisance to you, sole lion to the elephants of masses of sins!
Obeisance to you, lion on the farther shore of the ocean of sorrow! Obeisance to you, divine lion made of light!
Obeisance to you, wondrous lion embodying all forms! Obeisance to you, lion who liberates from afflictions!

2.2.s: yātrāḥ sarvā bhagavatā ājñaptāḥ sādhu kāraya ..
2.2.d: यात्राः सर्वा भगवता आज्ञप्ताः साधु कारय ..
2.2.m: "Duly arrange all the festivals and processions commanded by the Lord.
When Jagannātha is pleased, all the moving and unmoving world is pleased."
Placing the command of the lotus-born upon his head, the lord of the earth,
prosperous and rich with abundant treasures, together with Nārada,
carried out all the festivals, beginning with the ablution in Jyeṣṭha.

2.2.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe puruṣottamakṣetramāhātmya ekonatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 29 ..
2.2.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे पुरुषोत्तमक्षेत्रमाहात्म्य एकोनत्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. 29 ..

The sages said:

2.2.s: cakāra kena vidhinā janmasnānaṃ śriyaḥ pateḥ ..

2.2.m: By what rite did he perform the birth-ablution of the husband of Śrī?
Tell us duly about all the other festivals as well, O sage!

2.2.s: nāradena purā proktaṃ sarvaṃ te munisattama ..
2.2.d: नारदेन पुरा प्रोक्तं सर्वं ते मुनिसत्तम ..
2.2.m: Everything was told to you long ago by Nārada, O best of sages;

2.2.s: sa hi veda tamaḥpāre brahma brahmasuto muniḥ .. 2 ..

2.2.m: for he, the sage born of Brahmā, knows Brahman beyond the darkness.

2.2.s: tatsarvaṃ brūhi tattvena mune krautūhalaṃ hi naḥ ..

2.2.m: Tell all that in truth, O sage; great indeed is our curiosity!
Oh, how fortunate is King Indradyumna, O sage,
that at the end of such an undertaking of his, this great marvel occurred!

2.2.s: na śrutā hi na dṛṣṭā hi pratimā dārunirmitā .. 4 ..
2.2.d: न श्रुता हि न दृष्टा हि प्रतिमा दारुनिर्मिता .. 4 ..
2.2.m: Never has an image fashioned of wood been heard of or seen,
which, like a living body in person, would grant boons like a human being!
Remembering and remembering the sin-destroying deeds of the Lord,
and the deed of that king, which is difficult to attain for mortals,
there is no satiation for us who listen, O divine, great sage!
Therefore, recount in sequence to us the processions that destroy all sins,
by the sight of which dwelling in Vaikuṇṭha is certain!
Since Madhusūdana in person was the speaker of the māhātmya of the processions,
tell that to us, O fortunate one, out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds!
Jaimini said:
I shall explain the ritual ablution of Jyeṣṭha; listen now, O sages.
On the tenth day of the bright fortnight of Jyeṣṭha, having resolved upon the vow, restraining one's speech,
Rising at dawn, one should perform [the rites] according to the procedure of the five sacred fords.

2.2.s: mārkaṃḍeya vaṭaṃ gatvā ācamya prayataḥ pumān .. 2.2.30.10 ..
2.2.d: मार्कंडेय वटं गत्वा आचम्य प्रयतः पुमान् .. 2.2.30.10 ..
2.2.m: Having gone to the Mārkaṇḍeya banyan tree, having sipped water, restrained, a man,
Having bowed to Śaṃkara, with folded hands before him, should pray:
“O exceedingly fierce one of immense form, resembling the fire of cosmic dissolution!
Homage to you, O Bhairava! You ought to grant permission.”

2.2.s: tataḥ praviśya tīrthaṃ tu vaidikaiḥ paṃca vāruṇaiḥ ..
2.2.d: ततः प्रविश्य तीर्थं तु वैदिकैः पंच वारुणैः ..
2.2.m: Then, having entered the sacred ford, with the five Vedic Vāruṇa [hymns],
Or with the Aghamarṣaṇa hymn repeated thrice, O twice-born ones,
Having bathed properly, he should bathe in the end with this mantra:
“Homage to Śiva, peaceful and the remover of all sins.

2.2.s: snānaṃ karomi deveśa mama naśyatu pātakam .. 14 ..
2.2.d: स्नानं करोमि देवेश मम नश्यतु पातकम् .. 14 ..
2.2.m: I perform the ritual ablution, O Lord of gods; let my sin perish!
Drowned in the ocean of worldly existence, seized by sin, mindless,

2.2.s: trāhi māṃ bhaganetraghna tripurāre namo'stu te .. 15 ..
2.2.d: त्राहि मां भगनेत्रघ्न त्रिपुरारे नमोऽस्तु ते .. 15 ..
2.2.m: Save me, O crusher of Bhaga’s eyes, O enemy of Tripura! Homage be to you.”
Having thus bathed and gone outside, wearing clean garments, adorned with sectarian marks,
And having offered libations to the gods, seers, and ancestors according to the rule,
Entering the abode of Śaṃkara, touching the bull on its testicles
With this mantra, O brahmins, one obtains the fruit of all sacrifices:
“You are four-footed Dharma, you are sacrifice, with golden horns, having the three Vedas as your body.
O lord of cattle, whose form is the mount, I bow to you, who bear the trident-bearer.”
Then he should worship the one whose mount is the bull with the Aghora mantra,
And with the five Brahmā verses he should touch the supreme liṅga.
He should touch the liṅga with his thumb and the Śakti [pedestal] with his fist;
Having worshipped according to the rule and praised the god who is the enemy of the cities,
He attains the unsurpassed fruit of ten horse-sacrifices.

2.2.s: mārkaṃḍeyavaṭe snātvā dṛṣṭvā devaṃ tu śaṃkaram .. 21 ..
2.2.d: मार्कंडेयवटे स्नात्वा दृष्ट्वा देवं तु शंकरम् .. 21 ..
2.2.m: Having bathed at the Mārkaṇḍeya banyan tree and seen the god Śaṃkara,
He obtains the complete fruit of the royal consecration and horse-sacrifices.

2.2.s: ante śivasya sālokyaṃ prāpya jñānaṃ tato naraḥ .. 22 ..
2.2.d: अन्ते शिवस्य सालोक्यं प्राप्य ज्ञानं ततो नरः .. 22 ..
2.2.m: In the end, attaining the world of Śiva, and having acquired knowledge, a mortal
Gradually obtains liberation by the grace of Jagannātha.
Then, maintaining silence, he should go to the flawless god Nārāyaṇa,
[And to] the excellent banyan tree situated to his south, having the form of Viṣṇu,
Which destroys the accumulation of sins even upon seeing it.
Having seen it, he should bow from afar, meditating on Puruṣottama;
Then he should perform circumambulation, uttering this mantra:
“You are immortal, lasting for an aeon, the great dwelling of Viṣṇu.

2.2.s: nyagrodha hara me pāpaṃ viṣṇurūpa namo'stu te .. 26 ..
2.2.d: न्यग्रोध हर मे पापं विष्णुरूप नमोऽस्तु ते .. 26 ..
2.2.m: O banyan tree, remove my sin; O you whose form is Viṣṇu, homage be to you!
Homage to the unmanifest form, remaining through the great dissolution;
To the sole refuge of the worlds, to the wish-fulfilling tree, homage to you!”
Praising and reciting [prayers] with devotion to Janārdana at its base,
He is indeed freed from sins born of hundreds of millions of births.
Even by traversing its shadow, a man becomes free from sin.
Then he should bow to Suparṇa, who is the mount, in front of Hari.
Standing before Viṣṇu, bowed in devotion, with folded hands in joy:
“O composed of Vedic metres, O abode of the world, whose form is the mount, whose body is the threefold [Veda],
Whose form is sacrifice, all-pervading one of the universe, homage to you who are pleased!”
Having thus praised Garuḍa, he is freed from sins born of many births.
Restrained in speech, mind, and action, reflecting thus, he should go;

2.2.s: praviśya devatāgāraṃ kṛtvā taṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇam .. 32 ..
2.2.d: प्रविश्य देवतागारं कृत्वा तं त्रिः प्रदक्षिणम् .. 32 ..
2.2.m: Having entered the temple of the deity and circumambulated it thrice,
He should worship with the king of mantras, or with the Puruṣasūkta,
Or with the twelve-syllable mantra, or wherever his inclination lies.
All brahmins, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas are qualified to perform worship;
For others, [it is performed] through darśana with devotion and from chanting their names.
He should worship the Supreme Lord by means of the fivefold offerings;
Having folded his hands, he should recite this hymn:
“O God of gods, O Jagannātha, O saviour from the ocean of worldly existence,
Always gracious to devotees, protect me who am bowed at your feet!
Victory, O Kṛṣṇa, O Jagannātha! Victory, O destroyer of all sins!
Victory, O one whose lotus-feet are adored by the entire universe! Homage be to you!
Victory, O Lord of millions of cosmic eggs, whose breath is the wind of the Vedas,
Support of the entire universe, O Supreme Self, homage be to you!”
Victory to you who dispel the distress of the bowing host of gods headed by Brahmā, Indra, and Rudra!
Victory, O abode of the entire universe, O inner controller, obeisance unto you! (39)
Victory, O ocean of unmotivated compassion, affectionate to the destitute,
O sole refuge of the poor and helpless, witness of the universe, obeisance unto you! (40)
In the water of the ocean of worldly existence, in the whirlpool of delusion that is very difficult to cross,
impassable with the host of six waves, fearful with the sea-monsters of evil deeds, (41)
without shelter, without support, unsubstantial, frothy with suffering,
bound by the strands of your māyā, helpless, and fallen therein, (42)
lift me up, O Lord of gods, with looks from the corners of your merciful eyes,
sunk as I am there, O best of gods, revealer of sublime grace! (43)
You alone, O Lord of the world, are the friend of those afraid of worldly existence.

2.2.s: bubhukṣā ca pipāsā ca prāṇasya manasaḥ smṛtau .. 44 ..
2.2.d: बुभुक्षा च पिपासा च प्राणस्य मनसः स्मृतौ .. 44 ..
2.2.m: Hunger and thirst belong to vital breath; in traditional teaching, grief and delusion
belong to the mind; old age, death, and birth of a body belong to the body.
In your creation there is no one else who protects the destitute such as this. (45)
You have descended, O Lord, with the intent of bestowing grace upon the worlds;
for you whose desires are fulfilled, O Master, what other reason could there be on earth? (46)
Having attained your lotus feet, there is no anxiety, O Lord of the universe,
since your lotus feet are the sole means for the four ends of life, (47)
granting the fruit of all desires to all people through darśana.
Then one should worship him who has the plough as his emblem with the Śeṣa mantra, (48)
or with the twelve-syllable mantra, or by his name preceded by the syllable Om.
Becoming single-minded, bowing down, one should propitiate him: (49)
"Victory, O Rāma, who always takes delight, whose form is being, consciousness, and bliss!
Obeisance to you whose form is pure, free from the mud of ignorance! (50)
Victory to you who are free from the fatigue of bearing the weight of the entire world!
You ever brandish the plough to tear away the three afflictions. (51)
With open lotus eyes to protect the destitute who take refuge,
you alone, O Lord, are able to wash away the entire mass of highest sins. (52)
O ocean of gracious mercy, friend of the destitute, obeisance unto you!
By whom the earth, together with mobile and immobile beings, is borne upon the tip of his hood; (53)
deliver me from this impassable, boundless ocean of worldly existence!
O Supreme Lord higher than the high and the low, obeisance unto you!" (54)
Having thus praised the king of serpents, Bala, bearer of the pestle,
one should worship the prime cause of the worlds, whose eyes are auspicious. (55)

2.2.s: stutvā jayāṃ tāṃ bho viprāḥ praṇipatya prasādayet ..
2.2.d: स्तुत्वा जयां तां भो विप्राः प्रणिपत्य प्रसादयेत् ..
2.2.m: Having praised that victorious one, O brahmins, one should bow down and propitiate her:
"Victory, O goddess, great goddess! Be gracious, O deliverer from worldly existence! (56)
O firestick that produces happiness for those who take refuge, victory, O bringer of contentment!
The effect among embodied effects, and the cause among causes, (57)
the support among things supported—I bow down to you, the primordial one;
resting on the chest of Viṣṇu, bearing half the body of Śambhu, (58)
seated on the lotus mouth of Brahmā, dear to the world, I bow to you.
For the Supreme Self's acts of creation, maintenance, destruction, and the rest,

2.2.s: tvamekā śaktiratulā tvāṃ vinā so'pi neśvaraḥ ..
2.2.d: त्वमेका शक्तिरतुला त्वां विना सोऽपि नेश्वरः ..
2.2.m: you are the one incomparable power; without you, even he is powerless. (59)
You, the mother of all worlds, the māyā of Viṣṇu, practicing austerity,
Subhadrā, whose form is auspicious, who is the root cause—to her I bow." (60)
Then, for bathing in the ocean, one should pray to Puruṣottama: (61)
"Obeisance to you, O Lord Viṣṇu, pervading the moving and unmoving universe!
May my bath in the ocean reach completion without obstacles, O Lord! (62)
Obeisance to you, O Lord of the worlds, holding the conch, discus, and mace!
Give me, O God, permission to resort to your sacred ford." (63)
Then, observing silence, meditating on Viṣṇu, [and on] the lord of rivers,
having asked permission from Ugrasena situated on the path, composed in mind: (64)
"O mighty-armed Ugrasena, powerful one of fierce valor,
having received a boon from the well-pleased [Lord], you stay on the shore of the ocean; (65)
O bestower of the fully complete fruit of the ritual ablution performed in the king of sacred fords,
I shall perform my ocean ritual ablution; please grant me permission." (66)
Then one should proceed further, O best of twice-born, to Svargadvāra,
by which the gods come to this sacred field of Puruṣottama, (67)
this heaven on earth, day after day to have darśana of the Lord of the universe.
"By the path of the descent from heaven, I bow to both of you standing there." (68)

2.2.s: māmapyūrdhvaṃ nayetāṃ vai sākṣiṇau karmaṇāṃ satām ..
2.2.d: मामप्यूर्ध्वं नयेतां वै साक्षिणौ कर्मणां सताम् ..
2.2.m: May you two indeed lead me upward, you witnesses of the deeds of the virtuous,
born from the ocean's waters, supreme and endowed with all virtues.
Between the two of you I go to the opened gate of heaven."
Having prayed thus, one should then go into the presence of the king of sacred fords,

2.2.s: yaṃ dṛṣṭvā dūrataḥ pāpānmucyate mahato dhuvam ..
2.2.d: यं दृष्ट्वा दूरतः पापान्मुच्यते महतो धुवम् ..
2.2.m: seeing whom from afar one is surely released from great sin.
Having washed one's hands and feet, having sipped water, on a pure seat,
seated facing east, one should draw a mandala in front:
four-cornered, with four gates and svastikas at the four corners.
In its center one should draw a very beautiful eight-petaled lotus.
Then one should place the eight-syllable mantra upon the hands and upon the body.
The placement on the six limbs with six syllables has been declared by the wise;

2.2.s: śeṣau kukṣau ca pṛṣṭhe ca nyastavyau ca tataḥ punaḥ ..74..
2.2.d: शेषौ कुक्षौ च पृष्ठे च न्यस्तव्यौ च ततः पुनः ..74..
2.2.m: the remaining two should then be placed on the belly and on the back.
On the feet, the shanks, the thighs, the buttocks, and the sides;

2.2.s: nābhau pṛṣṭhe bāhuyugme hṛdi kaṇṭhe ca kakṣayoḥ .. 75 ..
2.2.d: नाभौ पृष्ठे बाहुयुग्मे हृदि कण्ठे च कक्षयोः .. 75 ..
2.2.m: on the navel, the back, the pair of arms, the heart, the throat, and the armpits;
on the lips, the ears, the eyes, the cheeks, and the nostrils;
on the eyebrows, the forehead, and the head, [placing] the mantra syllables in proper order,
having placed [them], concentrated in mind, one should perform the pervasive placement with all [the syllables].
One should perform three breath-controls, twenty-five times with the root [mantra].
One should put on the divine armor that dispels all sins:

2.2.s: pūrve māṃ pātu goviṃdo vārijākṣastu dakṣiṇe .. 78 ..
2.2.d: पूर्वे मां पातु गोविंदो वारिजाक्षस्तु दक्षिणे .. 78 ..
2.2.m: "May Govinda protect me in the east, and the Lotus-Eyed One in the south;
may Pradyumna protect me in the west, and likewise Hṛṣīkeśa in the north;
Narasiṃha in the southeast, and Madhusūdana in the southwest;

2.2.s: vāyavyāṃ śrīdharaḥ pātu aiśānyāṃ ca gadādharaḥ ..
2.2.d: वायव्यां श्रीधरः पातु ऐशान्यां च गदाधरः ..
2.2.m: may Śrīdhara protect in the northwest, and the Mace-Bearer in the northeast;
may Trivikrama protect above, and below the Holder of the Boar's Form;
may the god bearing the conch, discus, and mace protect me everywhere.
May Nārāyaṇa protect the mind, and the One whose emblem is Garuḍa protect consciousness;
may Janārdana, whose self is the three qualities, protect my intellect and ego;
may the Destroyer of the Daitya host always protect the senses."

2.2.s: evaṃ baddhvā ca kavacaṃ niṣpāpo jāyate pumān ..
2.2.d: एवं बद्ध्वा च कवचं निष्पापो जायते पुमान् ..
2.2.m: Having put on this armor, a person becomes freed from sin.
With the sixteen services conceived in the mind, a person,
having duly worshipped Puruṣottama according to rule, O brahmins,
having invoked the disease-free God of gods in that mandala,
having worshipped according to the rite with [offerings] augmented according to one's means,
meditating upon oneself [as one with] the king of sacred fords, the God of gods,
having folded one's hands in reverence, one should utter this mantra:
"O Sudarśana, praise be to you, of brilliance equal to ten million suns!
Show the path of Viṣṇu to one blinded by the darkness of ignorance."
Having prayed thus, O brahmins, near the water of the king of sacred fords,
going down on the earth with both knees, filled with devotion, one should bow:
"Praise be to you, king of sacred fords, to Viṣṇu who has the form of water,
the sustenance of living beings, the cause of supreme liberation.

2.2.s: agniśca te yonirilā ca dehe retodhā viṣṇoramṛtasya nābhiḥ ..
2.2.d: अग्निश्च ते योनिरिला च देहे रेतोधा विष्णोरमृतस्य नाभिः ..
2.2.m: Agni is your womb, and the earth is in your body; you are the seed-placer of Viṣṇu, the navel of nectar.
I approach your form, which has no other cause, full of bliss, having entered into the waters."
Reciting this mantra, O brahmins, one should enter into the midst of the water.
One should invoke the king of sacred fords, meditating on the Lord of the worlds,
the Lord of the waters, abiding therein to grant the fruit of the bath performed.
With the Aghamarṣaṇa hymn, accompanied by the Nārāyaṇa [hymn],
repeated three times, and with the fivefold Vāruṇa hymn,
[one should perform] once the invocation and the other six ancillary rites during the ablution.
The invocation was spoken of before; now the manifestation is described:
the visualization of presence for the attainment of the desired fruit by the bather.
For internal purification, one should sip [water] after drinking that which is consecrated with mantras;
for external bodily purification, one should sprinkle oneself with kuśa grass water.
For inner and outer purity, with water consecrated by mantras,
one should sprinkle three handfuls onto one's head; in the ocean there is no muttering underwater.
Through three immersions, one's sins committed over ten million births
are washed away in that water, while meditating on the destroyer of sins.
Having risen and sipped water according to rule, one should pray, uttering the mantra:
"You are Agni, O Lord of the worlds, the placer of seed, the kindler of desire,
the primary source of all elements, the imperishable master of living beings."
You are indeed the fire-drill of nectar, the source of the gods, O lord of waters!

2.2.s: vṛjinaṃ hara me sarvaṃ tīrtharāja namostu te ..
2.2.d: वृजिनं हर मे सर्वं तीर्थराज नमोस्तु ते ..
2.2.m: Take away all my wickedness, O king of sacred fords! Salutation to you!
Whatever sin has been earned previously across thousands of millions of births,

2.2.s: tadaśeṣaṃ layaṃ yātu dehi me brahma śāśvatam..
2.2.d: तदशेषं लयं यातु देहि मे ब्रह्म शाश्वतम्..
2.2.m: may all of that dissolve without remainder! Grant me eternal Brahman!"
And then, having bathed, having stepped out onto the bank and sipped water, restrained in speech,
he should wear two white garments and bright-figured sect-marks,
and with devotion sectarian marks of the conch, discus, mace, and lotus.
Properly contemplating the gods and ancestors with a mind fixed on the Lord,
he should offer libations according to rule, O brahmins, completely focused in mind.
Then, having drawn a mandala as before, facing north,
he should worship with the basic mantra and with these mantras with devotion:
"Nārāyaṇa, four-armed, holding the conch, discus, and mace,
accompanied by Dharā and Ramā, or alone, O best of the twice-born!"
Having meditated on him pleased with internal sacrifice, he should then invoke him externally:
"Come, Supreme Bliss, all-pervading one, whose nature is the world!
For grace, O Lord of gods, make your presence in the mandala!
All this moving and unmoving world is established here;
dwelling within it, you alone are the Lord. I prepare a seat for you!
When whose lotus feet were washed by Dharma in the form of Brahman,
the Gaṅgā born from them purifies the world—I offer foot-water to him!
With beams of light from crest-jewels set with priceless gems,
Brahmā and the others meditate day after day upon his lotus feet—
to him, the priceless one, the abode of the world, I offer this guest-water!
By whom, taking the form of Agastya, the king of sacred fords was sipped—
to him I offer fragrant water for sipping!
He who, having attained contact with Madhu, destroyed the one who took the form of water—
for the removal of all sins, I offer the honey-mixture!
He who, assuming the form of a boar, rescued this earth
submerged in the ocean of dissolution—I bathe him with water!
Whose universal form is wrapped in crores of cosmic eggs—
for the covering of all things, I offer two auspicious garments!
Without whom even a performed sacrifice would surely be unperformed—
for him, the Lord of sacrifice, I prepare this sacred thread!
Attaining contact with whose limbs ornaments indeed shine—
for the ornament of the universe, I prepare ornaments!
From contact with the wind touching whose limbs the trees born on Malaya
are endowed with fragrant sap—for him [is this] fragrant ointment!

Jaimini said:
Henceforth I shall describe the great festival of the Mahāvedī,
by which even one blinded by the darkness of ignorance may go to the radiant abode.
In the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha, the third day, which destroys sins,
and is conjoined with the constellation of Prajāpati, revealed itself.
On that [day], having made a resolve, the king, pure, should choose the preceptor,
and, with respect, one or three carpenters of proven skill.
He should choose [them] for the forest sacrifice with garments, ornaments, and the like.
Having gone with the carpenter to the forest filled with fine trees,
having placed the fire in the midst of it, one knowing the mantras, with the king of mantras,
having offered a hundred and eight oblations mixed with clarified butter collected from offerings,
should sprinkle clarified butter at the root of each tree.
Having given an offering to the guardians of the directions, as well as animal offerings to the guardian of the field,
he should offer an oblation of a hundred [portions of] rice cooked in milk to the lord of the forest.
Then, taking an axe, at the roots of the trees in the various directions,
at the spots consecrated with clarified butter, the preceptor, uttering the mantra,
should make small cuts, meditating on the one whose banner is Garuḍa.
While musical instruments resound with trumpeting noises, and auspicious songs are sung,

Having fashioned the chariot, he should begin the great festival of the king of obstacles.
With sixteen spokes, with sixteen firm wheels made of iron,

surrounded by dolls in various artistic compartments,
rich in various multicolored designs, adorned with pieces of sugarcane,
provided with four archways, four doors, and very beautiful,
rich in various multicolored designs, adorned with bands of gold,
twenty-two cubits in height, adorned with banners.
And he should make a Garuḍa banner crafted from red sandalwood,
with a long beak, a stout body, adorned with a pair of earrings,
holding a snake bitten in the tip of his beak, decorated with all ornaments,
extending both wings in the sky as if about to take flight,
destroying the strength and arrogance of the host of Daityas and Dānavas.
Having covered his entire body with gold, one should make him splendid.
One should make Hari's chariot furnished with a fine seat and well embellished.
And one should make the chariot of the plow-holder with fourteen wheels.
One should make Subhadrā's excellent chariot with twelve wheels.
One should make the plow banner of the plow-holder out of saptacchada wood.
One should make the goddess's lotus banner crafted from padma wood.
Having constructed the chariots, the king should perform the consecration as before.
According to the mantra, according to the scripture, he should place his trust in brahmins.
Brahmins are traditionally considered the mobile bodies of the Lord of the Universe.

Hereafter I shall describe the excellent festival of sleep.
Starting from the full moon of Āṣāḍha, the slumber of Hari occurs when the sun enters Cancer,
throughout the four rainy months, until the full moon of Kārttika, O twice-born ones.
This is the most sacred time for the worship of Hari.
Whatever fruit is spoken of from dwelling in Kāśī for many yugas, established in vows and restraints,
one should know that [same fruit is obtained] in the sacred field of the glorious Puruṣottama
by dwelling in the presence of Hari for even a single day of Cāturmāsya.
As for the days of the four rainy months that one might spend dwelling
in the sacred field in the presence of Jagannātha, with a pure heart,
he directly obtains the fruit of a thousand horse sacrifices.
Having bathed in the holy water of the ocean and beheld the glorious Puruṣottama,
abiding in the vow of Cāturmāsya, he grieves for nothing whatsoever.
Dwelling in the sacred field of the glorious Puruṣottama during Cāturmāsya
and the direct vision of the Lord—these two are the means to liberation.
Therefore, abandoning all Vedic and Smṛti duties, a man
should make every effort to dwell in the sacred field of the glorious Puruṣottama.
Asleep on the seat of the serpent's coils during Cāturmāsya, the Lord,

Throughout all twelve months the Lord is embodied here;

Whatever fruit one obtains by residing for eight months and beholding Viṣṇu day by day,
he surely obtains that from a single day during the Cāturmāsya.
By residing during the Cāturmāsya in the sacred field Śrī Puruṣottama,
day by day [he gains] the great merit born of residing in all sacred fields;
the Lord grants the fruit derived from residing a year in the sacred field.
Even if attached to every sin, and even if fallen from all proper conduct,
even if cast out from all righteousness, one should reside in Puruṣottama.
If a man who has committed sins should then observe a single Cāturmāsya,
abandoning all sins and becoming pure both outside and within,
by the grace of Narasiṃha he goes to the abode of Vaikuṇṭha.
Therefore, with all one's being, [concentrating] on the sleeping state of Viṣṇu,
a man should reside in Puruṣottama during the four rainy months.
Whether he does anything else or not, he attains the fulfillment of his birth.

Indeed, this was proclaimed for the ages dominated by Vedic conduct;

In that dreadful Kaliyuga, three-quarters of dharma is ruined;
dharma exists on only one foot, and out of fear of that [age] it moves about only in some places.
All are intent on untruth, hypocritical, subsisting on mere words,
mostly averse to dharma, devoted to the tongue and the genitals;
they never meditate, perform austerity, or keep vows.
Full of adharma, all are violent and exceedingly greedy;
they rejoice in censuring others, without doing anything virtuous of their own.
Through association or in sport they ruin another’s work;
out of desire for their own petty aims, they obstruct the tasks of others.
Despising a charming wife obtained according to dharma in their own house,
they cling to reprehensible women of others, behaving like beasts.
The agnihotra and other rites, or other vows, are rarely found anywhere;

2.2.s: manasā cintayatyevaṃ nirnimittaṃ kathaṃ nu me ..

2.2.m: He reflected thus in his mind: 'How indeed without cause has there been for me,

As he was thinking thus, at the end of three nights the thought occurred:

What offense has been committed by us against this Puruṣottama?

Śāṇḍilya said:

One should practice dharma only through them—such is the conclusion of the scriptures.
Incarnation after incarnation is indeed for the purpose of protecting that dharma.
He who lives transgressing it is surely one who commits an offense against you.

2.2.s: ahaṃ te devadeveśa karmaṇā manasā girā .. 67 ..

Therefore be gracious, O Lord of the World, toward your servant who always offends;

Awakening, he contemplated that dream, his mind filled with wonder:

The cosmos of eighteen [and] fourteen [worlds], washing whose lotus feet
with liquid dharma, purified itself with that water—
he whom Śakra and the others worship with supreme divine enjoyments,

Filled with wonder in this way, O twice-born ones, with that [food]

Then, all of them became free of disease, their minds delighted by good speech;

where, by giving his own leftover food, he frees human beings from sin.

This image of Viṣṇu is to be anointed; the ointment is superior to all others,

no other paste is commended, for that alone is approved for Viṣṇu's limbs.

Formerly, the Daitya Damanaka, who moved through the waters of the ocean,
afflicted human beings, possessing the prowess of illusory power.
The Lord also, master of illusion, at the command of the Grandfather [Brahmā],
entered the ocean as the all-pervading fish incarnation;
having searched for him and dragged him to the shore, he crushed him on the ground.
On the fourteenth lunar day of the bright fortnight of Madhu, that best of Dānavas fell.
From contact with the Lord's hand, he became a fragrant plant.
The Lord, with an astonished mind, took it properly under the demon's own name [damanaka].
Making a garland that met with the woodland garland on his chest,
he reflected on its fragrance, which remained for a long time.
Its fragrance also surpasses the perfume of all [other] flowers,
and its very beautiful colour became equal to the body of the Lord.
A garland made of it brings supreme delight to the Lord;

produces great pleasure in Viṣṇu, which bestows liberation.
The person who wears with devotion a garland taken down from [his] limbs
attains without doubt the fruit of a thousand horse sacrifices.
A devotee who places on their head, around their neck, or upon their chest

2.2.s: dhārayenmūrdhni kaṃṭhe ca bhakto yo vinyaseddhadi ..

2.2.m: a garland fashioned from tulasī that has been taken down from Viṣṇu's limbs
undisturbed obtains the fruit of the same number of horse sacrifices.
As many nirmālya tulasī leaves of Hari as one eats,
for that many thousands of births one is exalted in the world of Viṣṇu.
Eating the food offering of Hari mixed with tulasī leaves,
with every mouthful one enjoys the fruit equal to drinking soma.
Eating it throughout one's life, one will surely attain liberation.
The remains of Viṣṇu's arghya offering and the like, as well as the water for rinsing the mouth,
the water from washing his feet, and the bath water—each destroys sin,
bestows the fruit of ablutions in all sacred fords, destroys the baneful influence of evil planets,
destroys misfortune, sins, and rakṣasas, and annihilates bhūtas and vetālas;
it is supreme in destroying the fault of touching corpses and other impure things;
it grants the fruits of all initiations and vows, and increases sovereignty;
it takes away untimely death, suppresses hosts of diseases,
and destroys hosts of sins such as consuming intoxicating liquor and meat.
If a man whose body has been bathed with these [waters] should hear of a birth-impurity,
no ritual impurity exists for him, and he remains qualified for all rites.
One who takes a lifelong vow and partakes of these, or even of just one,
whether in abundance or a little, is liberated by Viṣṇu's grace.
Thus the God, residing there out of a desire to show grace to the worlds,
sporting together with Śrī, liberates [beings] without exertion.
Through the offering of his garland-remains and foot-water, through the gift of foodstuffs, through the sight of him and bows to him,
and through offerings of worship, he is the granter of liberation in this best of sacred fields known as Puruṣottama.

The sages said:
"O sage, from you has been fully heard the māhātmya of the Lord of the Universe,

Jaimini said:
"In every way Puruṣottama acts for the welfare of the world,
through the manifestations of his various qualities and the deeds of his diverse forms.
Through the play of diverse forms, he has diverse selves, consisting of the whole universe; / O best of twice-born, without egoism there is no fruit of action.
By egoism people are bound in the prison called worldly existence.
When a man undertakes an action united with intellect and egoism,
he obtains the fruit of that, whether good or bad, endowed with the qualities.
Their intellect, however, is threefold, shaped by the difference of the qualities.
Among them, those who are sāttvika and virtuous, indifferent to obtaining fruits,
perform action for the pleasure of the Lord, desiring liberation.

the giver of liberation when meditated upon, seen, or remembered; of this there is no doubt.
