Hereafter I will describe the turning of the side
of the Lord of the universe who is asleep, who turns the ages.
When the day of Hari arrives in the bright fortnight of the month of Nabhasya,
one should go quietly to the door of Viṣṇu's bedchamber, enter,
bow down joyfully to Jagannātha lying on his couch,
cover him, approach softly, and worship him with articles of worship.
Having bowed with devotion at his feet, praising him with secret Upaniṣads,
and reciting this mantra, one should cause the God to lie facing north:
'O God of gods, O Jagannātha, O turner of world-ages,
by whom this whole universe, both stationary and moving, is turned,
merely by the movements of your will, through the states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep,
protect me, O Lord of the universe, who am immersed in the ocean of worldly existence!'
"You have slept for the welfare of the world; turn over onto [your other] side.
This is the time to turn over for your protection of the universe.
By your command, even Śakra, standing eager upon his banner,
longing to see your lotus feet, releases water through the clouds,
and floods the surface of the earth in order to protect its creatures."
Having thus prayed to the Lord of gods, one should repeatedly please him,
and, performing this auxiliary ritual, fan him with fans and chowries.
One should smear his whole body with fragrant sandalwood paste,
and [offer] sweet preparations of sugarcane, modified milk-rice,

Having worshipped the Lord of the World during the great festival called Kaumudī

An image of Dāmodara made of a niṣka of gold,

I shall tell its procedure; listen now, O sages.
One skilled in the rites should perform the preliminary consecration of the cloths on the night of the fifth.
In front of the deity, in a pavilion, he should make an eight-petalled lotus.
He should worship the regents of the quarters in their directions, and [worship] Kṣetrapāla and the lord of the Gaṇas.
Outside, in the four directions, he should worship Caṇḍa and Pracaṇḍa.
Having placed a vessel in the center, he should sprinkle it with water through a cloth.
With the mantra “Dyutānastu…” he should cover it with a celestial garment.
A collection of cloths numbering twenty-one, well-perfumed with incense,
he should place in the middle thereof, while reciting a Vaiṣṇava mantra.
Having covered that diligently with another cloth,
and touching it, he should repeat this mantra, meditating on Puruṣottama:

He should wrap the deities with seven cloths each;

Then, having offered betel and camphor sprigs,
and having worshiped with dūrvā grass and unbroken grains, he should perform the waving of lamps for the Lord.

With a shower of a thousand streams [one should bathe] the God; then one should remove the previous offerings.
One should smear the limbs of the God and his form with fragrant substances and sandalwood paste.
One should apply the ornaments in their proper places and for proper splendor;
immediately after, one should adorn [him] with fragrant flower garlands.
One should place the God's eight weapons, beginning with the discus, in front [of him].
Holding up a jeweled umbrella, one should worship Puruṣottama,
accompanied by Lakṣmī, again, O brahmins, splendidly with presentations,
while conches are blown, resounding smoothly and deeply,
while beautiful courtesans are occupied in waving chowries,
with auspicious songs, dances, and recitations of praises by bards,
and while the twice-born repeatedly shout cries of victory.
Having worshipped Keśava with three handfuls of dūrvā grass and unbroken grains,
with extremely pure golden vessels holding lamps of cow's clarified butter
and wicks infused with camphor, one should wave lights before Jagannātha.
Pleasing betel, well prepared and set in a golden vessel,
one should slowly present to each near the mouth.
One should give sacrificial fees to the preceptor and worship the brahmins.
Those who, filled with joy, witness the sacred festival of the Puṣya ablution,
having all their desires fulfilled, go to the abode of Viṣṇu.
One fallen from kingship regains his kingdom and obtains universal sovereignty;

Jaimini said:
In the month of Phālguna, one should perform the supreme swing festival,
Where Govinda sports indeed for the sake of bestowing grace upon the world.
One should make a secondary image of the God of Gods named Govinda;
In front of the temple, one should make an elevated sixteen-pillared
Square pavilion with four doors, furnished with an altar platform,
With a beautiful canopy, adorned with garlands, chowries, and banners,
And an auspicious seat upon the altar platform, made of śrīparṇī wood.
One should celebrate the Phalgūtsava for five days or three days.
Prior to the full moon day of Phālguna, O brahmins, on the fourteenth day at nightfall,
One should celebrate the fire festival to the east of the swing pavilion.
That is proclaimed as a constituent rite of the pilgrimage favoured by Govinda.
Having chosen the preceptor, with fire produced from friction,
Having prepared the ground according to the prescribed rules, [he should gather] a very high heap of straw;

In a delightful spot in Vṛndāvana, arranged with trees

2.2.m: Those who see Kṛṣṇa at that moment attain liberation; of this there is no doubt.
The destruction of the group of five sins, beginning with the murder of a brahmin, shall take place.
Thus one should swing the God three times, he who removes all sins,
who shows grace to men through devotion, the sole cause of worldly enjoyment and liberation,
whose sportive activities, both artificial and natural,
destroy the multitude of sins and dispel primal ignorance.
Seeing him a second time destroys minor sins such as cow-slaughter;
at the third time, it destroys all sins without remainder; of this there is no doubt.
Having seen the God swinging, one is freed from all sins;
one is released from [sufferings] that are spiritual, material, and supernatural.
Having caused this festival to be performed, a king becomes a universal emperor;
a brahmin certainly becomes a master of the four Vedas and endowed with wisdom.

2.2.m: Having thus spent a year in the observance known as the Mūrtipañjara,
one should perform the concluding rite of consecration for the attainment of the full fruit.
Twelve images of Viṣṇu fashioned of gold,
made according to one's means, are to be placed on twelve pitchers,
which are covered with vessels of mango wood, directly on them, individually,
wrapped in white cloths, containing fragrant water and sprouts,
in the eight directions and the four directions, on a sarvatobhadra maṇḍala.
Those pitchers should be set up, and the images worshipped upon them,
with the twelve-syllable mantra, with individual offerings,
and first a ceremonial bath of all with the five nectars, O twice-born ones,
accompanied by songs, instrumental music, dances, and so forth, as well as worship of brahmins,
with twelve pairs of garments, and likewise pairs of parasols and sandals,
with fans, water pitchers, and beds with pedestals,
with perfumes, garlands, good betel leaves, and likewise finger-rings and earrings.
Lamps fueled with ghee should be lit, twelve by twelve in order.

2.2.m: Having spent the night in this manner, in the morning the fire ritual [is performed]—
three hundred [oblations] of firewood, ghee, and sacred cooked food for each deity,
and then a thousand and eight with sesame seeds accompanied by the vyāhṛtis.
At the end of the fire oblation, having partaken of the remnants, one should give the preceptor's sacrificial fee:
twelve brown cows adorned with ornaments should be given.
Then one should feed one hundred and forty-four brahmins.
That host of deities, together with the pots, the canopy, and the chowries,
along with all the offerings, he should present to the preceptor.
Having performed this king of observances, one obtains all desires.
The twelve festivals of Viṣṇu that are renowned, beginning with the Guṇḍicā—
the religious merit born from witnessing them is attained through this observance.
The state of Indra, universal sovereignty, and the status of an emperor,
and the eight supernatural powers he attains by the grace of the God of gods.
This most sacred observance was performed by Nārada;
having performed it for twelve years, the sage became liberated while living.

You too, self-restrained, should perform this supreme observance.

Jaimini said:
I shall describe the vernal festival, the Damanabhañjikā,
by performing or beholding which Puruṣottama is pleased.
The herb named damanaka, which was mentioned of old, O brahmins—
on the thirteenth day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, one should gather it by the roots.
In the middle of it, one should make a very auspicious maṇḍala named padma.
Inside it, one should install the worshipped substitute image of the deity,
accompanied by Śrī and Satyabhāmā, and worship them according to the rules.
At midnight, indeed, one should have this rite of the God of gods performed.
Formerly, at midnight as well, the Lord crushed the asura Damana;

2.2.s: bhaṃktvā lebhe parāṃ prītiṃ tadaṃgotthaṃ ca tattṛṇam ..7..

2.2.m: having crushed him, he experienced supreme delight, and that herb arose from his body.
On that very thirteenth day, one should meditate upon the herb as the demon.
Having folded his hands in reverence, he should utter this speech:
'You slew the demon Damana of old, the thorn of the three worlds;
he, transformed in this manner, stands before you.
Whatever delight you had at his origin then, O Mādhava,
let there be the very same delight now in the crushing of Damana.'

2.2.s: ityuktvā tṛṇameke tu kare devasya dāpayet ..

Then one should pass the remainder of the night with dance, song, and the like.
Then, when the sun has risen, taking the deity preceded by the herb,
one should convey him near the Lord of the Universe, O best of the twice-born.
Then, one should worship Jagannātha with offerings as before.
Having slain Hiraṇyakaśipu, [Viṣṇu wore] the garland of entrails produced from his body—
Having placed [it] on your neck, just as you were pleased after slaying Hiraṇyakaśipu / and [putting on] the garland of entrails born of his body, so this damana grass

Having recited this, one should place the auspicious fragrant grass upon Hari's head.
Then, beholding with joy Hari's lotus-face that brings delight,
freed from worldly sorrow, one attains unsurpassed happiness.
Taking a sprig of it on one's head as it falls from Viṣṇu's head,
freed from all sins, one shall dwell firmly in the city of Viṣṇu.

Jaimini said:
Hereafter I shall declare the pilgrimage that grants imperishable liberation
without effort to the foolish whose minds are bound by latent desires.
In the bright fortnight of the month of Vaiśākha, in the middle of the night of the second [lunar day],
one should make a four-cornered pavilion, smeared with plaster and furnished with an altar,
and then enclose it with clean, well-washed cloth like a curtain,
provided with good steps and fitted with a beautiful canopy.
In its middle one should firmly set down an excellent, auspicious seat.
On it, covered with a robe, one should place a golden vessel.

2.2.s: tasya paścimabhāge vai svāsīno brāhmaṇaḥ śuciḥ ..
2.2.d: तस्य पश्चिमभागे वै स्वासीनो ब्राह्मणः शुचिः ..
2.2.m: On the western side of it, indeed, a pure brahmin should seat himself comfortably.
In another vessel he should take twenty-five [palas] of sandalwood,
finely ground, and take more than a pala of black oil.
There should be half as much agallochum as saffron, and half as much incense-resin as saffron;
the measure of musk and camphor should equal the incense-resin.
He should grind all this together with water derived from trumpet flowers.
Then he should add two palas of excellent oil of agallochum;
having stirred it together, he should deposit it in the previous vessel.
Covering it with ketakī leaves, he should wrap it in Chinese silk.
He should protect it with the mantra 'Gandhas te soma' and the Garuḍamudrā.
Thus he should deposit the preparatory offering in that pavilion.
Then, at the time of dawn, he should take it into the presence of Kṛṣṇa.
Having circumambulated the temple with conches, fly-whisks, umbrellas, and the like,
and placing it before the Lord, he should worship Puruṣottama.
He should then uncover the cloths and gaze with a divine vision;
he should consecrate what was sprinkled with the king of mantras by snapping fingers and other [protective rites].
Having worshipped [him] with perfume, flowers, and unbroken grains, he should anoint [him] with the hymn of Śrī,
with a soft touch, slowly, slowly on all the limbs of the Lord of Śrī.
The Vaiṣṇavas then praise Hari with cries of victory;
the learned praise him with various hymns and Upaniṣads.
With flutes, lutes, and various dances, songs, and instrumental music,
with fans, fly-whisks, umbrellas, and diverse other offerings,
pleasing Jagannātha, he should anoint him at the start of the third [lunar day].
He, by the mere thought of whom the torments of embodied beings are destroyed—
he indeed removes the torments of men by his darśana then, O twice-born ones.
Inconceivable is the majesty of Viṣṇu, ever beyond 'it is such or such'.
Then, with fine garments, garlands, chewable and solid foods, beverages,
and various agreeable items, boiled and auspicious cow products,
and with well-prepared betel, he should then worship the God.

having smeared sandalwood on the limbs [of the Lord] in the bright fortnight of the month of Mādhava
on the third [lunar day], he joyfully sang this praise to Jagannātha.
Dakṣa said:
'O God of gods, O Lord of the world, spotless with innate bliss,
save us who are immersed in the ocean of worldly existence, O Supreme Lord!
Tormented by varied afflictions are these human beings;
by your thought of pity for me, and with your auspicious, nectar-like glance,
Nourish [these men], who are dried up like withered grass, O Kṛṣṇa, [rain-]cloud! Homage to you!
In order to deliver those confounded by the impurities of the Kali [age], O Lord of the worlds,
This incarnation has taken place within the cavern of the Nīlācala mountain.
Of immense sins grown over a long time, difficult to abandon,
You alone are capable of burning the heap, O compassionate one towards the miserable and helpless!
In this great yoga consisting of your darśana, free of the eight limbs beginning with restraint,
Those whose mind is resolved on the sole attainment of the four aims of life

Knowledge of the Self independent of rites, O Lord of gods, does not liberate;

Victory, O Kṛṣṇa! Victory, O Lord! Victory, O imperishable one! Victory, O unalterable one!
Be pleased! Show grace to these miserable, foolish, and mindless people!”
Having praised him thus, he fell like a rod before his lotus-feet,
Proclaiming: “Be pleased, O Lord! Be pleased, O Lord! Be pleased, O Lord!”
Then the Blessed One spoke to the Prajāpati in a sweet voice:

2.2.d: उत्तिष्ठ वत्स ते दत्तं दुर्लभं यद्वरं त्वया .. 33 ..
2.2.m: “Arise, my child! The rare boon that you have desired
Is granted to you: by my grace it will be so, without doubt.
My grace is hard to attain for those of little merit, as you well know.
You are born from my limb, and you have petitioned me;
Having pleased me with my festival, I therefore grant it to you:
Those who with devotion and joy behold this inexhaustible festival procession
Shall obtain at that time whatever they desire in their mind.
Just as anointing with sandalwood paste removes burning heat,
So this festival of mine, O Dakṣa, destroys the threefold affliction.
Your intellect was impelled by me, and so you performed the festival;
Indeed, this was conceived by me in mind for the deliverance of the wretched.
I shall give you all that was desired by you, O Prajāpati.
These twelve great festival processions, beginning with Guṇḍicā, are purifying;
Each one bestows liberation; all promote virtue, love, and wealth.
Whoever beholds with devotion even one among them

2.2.s: ekayāpi bhavābdhiṃ sa tīrtvā viṣṇupadaṃ vrajet .. 41 ..
2.2.d: एकयापि भवाब्धिं स तीर्त्वा विष्णुपदं व्रजेत् .. 41 ..

Jaimini said:
Having spoken thus to the lord of creatures, the Blessed One vanished.
Dakṣa Prajāpati too, being full of faith, by his command,
Dwelt on the mountain for a year and witnessed the great festivals.
Becoming an omniscient brahmin in the best lineage of Kauśika,
He engaged the people according to rule in the great sacrifices.
The festival processions are proclaimed for the faith of those of small intellect;
And he, the guru of the world, whose form is the Supreme Brahman manifest,
Was propitiated by the lord of the gods for the grace of the world.

The sages said:
“O Blessed One, knower of all scriptures, the supreme marvel has been heard:
The sin-destroying greatness of the Blessed One consisting of festival processions.
Tell us, then, how the god is worshipped by seekers of desires as the bestower of all desires,

2.2.m: That wooden [form] is indeed the single path to the four [aims of life], dharma and the rest.
The path of dharma is dense, obstructed by numerous scriptures;
no one at all is capable of determining its truth, O best of brahmins.
Wealth and pleasure, having their root in it, thus always have coarse courses.
The Lord effortlessly causes these three to prosper.
For dharma is the Lord Viṣṇu, and this world is rooted in dharma;
and Janārdana is the sovereign lord of both dharma and the world.
He whose devotion is firmly established in him who consists of the aims of life,

2.2.s: sa sarvakāmatṛptātmā na śocati na kāṃkṣati .. 9 ..

2.2.m: his soul contented with all desires, neither grieves nor craves.
When worshipped in the form of Indra, he gives sovereignty over the three worlds;
meditated upon in the form of Dhātṛ, Hari increases one's lineage.
In the form of Sanatkumāra, he bestows a long life;
meditated upon in the form of Pṛthu, he indeed grants abundance of livelihood.
Worshipped as Bṛhaspati, he grants the fruit of the Gaṅgā and other sacred fords;
meditated upon in the form of the Sun, he dispels inner darkness.
Worshipped as the Moon, he would grant incomparable good fortune;
[one becomes] a knower of the truth of the eighteen sciences, meditating [on him] as the Lord of Speech.
He, the eternal one, gives the fruit of the horse sacrifice and other rites;
this deity composed of the universe, meditated upon in the form of the Lord of Sacrifice,
[and] contemplated in the form of Kubera, would grant matchless prosperity.
Thus this ocean of compassion, dwelling on that Nīlācala,
has an illusory wooden body in order to show grace to the wretched and the helpless.

The sages said:
At the conclusion of the temple consecration, as for the boons that Hari

Jaimini said:
Having obtained boons from Jagannātha, who is the direct embodiment of Brahman,

Indradyumna said:
O King, you are deeply learned, committed to devotion to dharma;
your devotion also is directed to the Lord by deed, mind, and speech.
The Lord does not instruct for the sake of only one [person];
for he is the teacher of the moving and unmoving, and the universe has become his disciple.
With the purpose of bestowing grace upon me, the Lord of the universe has descended;
for the uplifting of those whose minds are distressed, he will remain here for a long time.

2.2.m: Neither mother, nor father, nor friend, nor wife, nor son
is such a benefactor to the wretched who take refuge as He is.
Therefore, worship Him, who bestows the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
Together with the citizens and subjects, conduct those festivals in an abundant manner.
This is the common path of dharma for kings, O best of kings:
what is instituted by a predecessor is maintained by his successor.
Worship Nṛsiṃha, O lord of kings, with grand offerings of rich splendor;
worship Him at the three junctures of the day, and attain supreme nirvāṇa.
They say that preserving what another has done is superior to one's own doing;
whoever protects what was given by another, that indeed is superior to what is given by oneself.”
Jaimini said:
Then, with folded palms, that Śveta, the best of kings,
placed those words upon his head, as though a garland possessing virtues.
The royal seer Indradyumna too, having propitiated Puruṣottama,
the glorious one went to the world of Brahmā.
Thus has been related to you this sacred, supreme māhātmya of the sacred field,
and the māhātmya of the Wooden Brahman who dwells there perpetually.
Whoever hears this being recited with devotion, O best of brahmins,
he shall obtain the entire fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices.
Whatever astrological conjunction is known as Ardhodaya, described by Skanda,
a crore times multiplied is the merit from proclaiming the māhātmya of Viṣṇu.
Whoever hears it morning after morning becomes [equal to] the giver of a hundred tawny cows;
he obtains the fruit of an ablution with waters from the Gaṅgā and the Puṣkara lake.
It brings fortune, brings fame, grants long life, is sacred, increases offspring,
confers a place in heaven, and removes all sins.
This secret has been declared, well concealed in the Purāṇas;

The sages said:
O venerable Jaimini, master of all the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,
by your grace, the māhātmya of the Lord of the Universe,
of this king of sacred fields, and of all the festivals in every detail,
as well as the fruit of consuming the Lord's leftover food,
the exceedingly rare history of King Indradyumna,
the manifestation of Nīlamādhava and of the Wooden Brahman,
has been heard as it flowed properly from the lotus of your mouth.
Now we wish to hear from you, O best of speakers,
everything in detail, O holy one, all of us filled with joy:
that fruit which has been stated precisely for the hearing of the Purāṇa,

Jaimini said:

2.2.m: Well done, well done, O best of sages, that you have asked with supreme joy!
In that, incomparable delight has arisen in me, causing my hair to stand on end.
I shall tell you all of that; listen attentively.
At the beginning of listening to a Purāṇa, according to one's own means,
having first made the ritual resolve according to the rule, [one should select] a brahmin born of a pure lineage,
free from defective limbs, peaceful, belonging to one's own Vedic branch, or one's own family priest,
knowing the true meaning of all treatises; with exceedingly radiant ornaments,
with garments, sandalwood paste, garlands and the like, one should appoint him for reading and recitation.
Having folded his hands in supplication, he should then pray to the twice-born:

2.2.s: tvaṃ viṣṇurviṣṇureva tvaṃ na tu bhedaḥ kadācana .. 11 ..
2.2.d: त्वं विष्णुर्विष्णुरेव त्वं न तु भेदः कदाचन .. 11 ..

vaddarśanena mukto'bhavaditi dṛṣṭvā brahmaṇā vismayaḥ,. atha kṣetra prabhāva iti jñātvā sāścaryaṃ bhagavantaṃ nīlādrau dṛṣṭvā brahmadevakṛtā bhagavataḥ stutiḥ, yamasya tatrāgamanam, yamakṛtā bhagavatstutiḥ, bhagavadājñayā yamaṃ prati lakṣmyā uktiḥ, kṣetramāhātmyaśravaṇe lakṣmīṃ prati yamaprārthanā -.... - - -. -. - 56 2
2.2.d:
2 तत्र पुरुषोत्तमक्षेत्रे ब्रह्मण आगमनम्, तावत्कश्चिद्वायसस्त्स्मिन्कुण्डे स्नात्वा भग
वद्दर्शनेन मुक्तोऽभवदिति दृष्ट्वा ब्रह्मणा विस्मयः,. अथ क्षेत्र प्रभाव इति ज्ञात्वा साश्चर्यं भगवन्तं नीलाद्रौ दृष्ट्वा ब्रह्मदेवकृता भगवतः स्तुतिः, यमस्य तत्रागमनम्, यमकृता भगवत्स्तुतिः, भगवदाज्ञया यमं प्रति लक्ष्म्या उक्तिः, क्षेत्रमाहात्म्यश्रवणे लक्ष्मीं प्रति यमप्रार्थना -.... - - -. -. - 56 2
2.2.m: 2. The arrival of Brahmā there in Puruṣottamakṣetra; then, Brahmā's wonder upon seeing that a crow, having bathed in that pool, was liberated upon obtaining darśana of the Lord; then, realizing the power of the sacred field, the praise of the Lord composed by Brahmadeva on beholding the Lord in astonishment on Nīlādri; the arrival of Yama there; the praise of the Lord composed by Yama; by the command of the Lord, Lakṣmī's speech to Yama; Yama's petition to Lakṣmī to hear the māhātmya of the sacred field. (56, 2)

2.2.s:
3 yamalakṣmīsaṃvādaprasaṃgena pralaye mārkaṇḍeyasya nāvi samārohaṇaṃ jale sarvatra bhramaṇañca,
etatkṣetranikaṭe vaṭavṛkṣadarśanam, bālavacanaṃ śrutvā samīpāgamanañca, tatra bhagavaddarśanam mārkaṇḍeyakṛtā bhagavatstutiḥ, tato mārkaṇḍeyasya prasannasya bhagavato mukhe praveśaḥ, sahasrabrahmāṇḍavyāptaṃ tadbhagavata udaraṃ dṛṣṭvā tadaṃtaṃ cāgatvā mārkaṇḍeyasya bahirāgamanama, tatraiva cāvasthānam, iti lakṣmyuktavṛttāṃtaṃ śrutvā yamena yameśvaretināmnā liṅgasthāpanama....... - - - - - - -. -. 57
2.2.d:
3 यमलक्ष्मीसंवादप्रसंगेन प्रलये मार्कण्डेयस्य नावि समारोहणं जले सर्वत्र भ्रमणञ्च,
एतत्क्षेत्रनिकटे वटवृक्षदर्शनम्, बालवचनं श्रुत्वा समीपागमनञ्च, तत्र भगवद्दर्शनम् मार्कण्डेयकृता भगवत्स्तुतिः, ततो मार्कण्डेयस्य प्रसन्नस्य भगवतो मुखे प्रवेशः, सहस्रब्रह्माण्डव्याप्तं तद्भगवत उदरं दृष्ट्वा तदंतं चागत्वा मार्कण्डेयस्य बहिरागमनम, तत्रैव चावस्थानम्, इति लक्ष्म्युक्तवृत्तांतं श्रुत्वा यमेन यमेश्वरेतिनाम्ना लिङ्गस्थापनम....... - - - - - - -. -. 57
2.2.m: 3. In the context of the dialogue between Yama and Lakṣmī, Mārkaṇḍeya's boarding a boat at the dissolution and wandering everywhere in the waters; sighting the banyan tree near this sacred field, and approaching upon hearing the words of the child; obtaining darśana of the Lord there; the praise of the Lord composed by Mārkaṇḍeya; then, Mārkaṇḍeya's entering into the mouth of the gracious Lord; seeing the Lord's belly pervading thousands of universes and coming to its end, Mārkaṇḍeya's coming outside and remaining in that very place; hearing this account spoken by Lakṣmī, the installation of a liṅga by Yama under the name Yameśvara. (57)

2.2.s:
4 lakṣmīyamasaṃvādaprasaṃgena pratitīrthakiñcitkathādarśanam, tatra ca kapālamocanatīrthavarṇa-
nama sindhurājasya salilādvaṭasyāmūlāntasthitānāmābrahmasthāvarāntānāṃ sarveṣāṃ
muktirbhavatīti tatsthānamāhātmyakathanam, tataḥ kāmākhyanṛsiṃhatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanam, maṅgalādyaṣṭadevatānāmaṣṭasu dikṣu saṃsthāpanam, kapālamocanayameśvaramārkaṇḍeya-
bilveśavaṭeśanīlakaṇṭheśānakṣetrapālādyaṣṭaliṅgasthāpanam indradyumnasya kathānakam,
tadanantaraṃ yamabrahmaṇoḥ svasthānaṃ prati gamanama bhagavato dārumayavapurdhāraṇapūrvaka-
mindradyumnāya varapradānam, dāruvapuṣmato harerguṇānuvādaśravaṇasaṃjātakautukayordurva-
tanakariṇoḥ puṇḍarīkāṃbarīṣakanāmnorbrāhmaṇakṣatriyayostatrāgamanam, tatraiva cendra-
dyumnena dārumayatīrthasthāpanam, tanmāhātmyavarṇanaṃ ca -.... - .. 59 1
2.2.d:
4 लक्ष्मीयमसंवादप्रसंगेन प्रतितीर्थकिञ्चित्कथादर्शनम्, तत्र च कपालमोचनतीर्थवर्ण-
नम सिन्धुराजस्य सलिलाद्वटस्यामूलान्तस्थितानामाब्रह्मस्थावरान्तानां सर्वेषां
मुक्तिर्भवतीति तत्स्थानमाहात्म्यकथनम्, ततः कामाख्यनृसिंहतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, मङ्गलाद्यष्टदेवतानामष्टसु दिक्षु संस्थापनम्, कपालमोचनयमेश्वरमार्कण्डेय-
बिल्वेशवटेशनीलकण्ठेशानक्षेत्रपालाद्यष्टलिङ्गस्थापनम् इन्द्रद्युम्नस्य कथानकम्,
तदनन्तरं यमब्रह्मणोः स्वस्थानं प्रति गमनम भगवतो दारुमयवपुर्धारणपूर्वक-
मिन्द्रद्युम्नाय वरप्रदानम्, दारुवपुष्मतो हरेर्गुणानुवादश्रवणसंजातकौतुकयोर्दुर्व-
तनकरिणोः पुण्डरीकांबरीषकनाम्नोर्ब्राह्मणक्षत्रिययोस्तत्रागमनम्, तत्रैव चेन्द्र-
द्युम्नेन दारुमयतीर्थस्थापनम्, तन्माहात्म्यवर्णनं च -.... - .. 59 1
2.2.m: 4. In the context of the dialogue between Lakṣmī and Yama, an account given for each sacred ford: therein, description of Kapālamocanatīrtha; the proclamation of the māhātmya of that place stating that all beings from Brahmā down to immobile creatures, situated from the water of the ocean king to the root of the banyan tree, obtain liberation; then, description of the māhātmya of the sacred ford called Kāmākhya-Nṛsiṃha; the installation of the eight deities headed by Maṅgalā in the eight directions; the installation of the eight liṅgas headed by Kapālamocana, Yameśvara, Mārkaṇḍeya, Bilveśa, Vaṭeśa, Nīlakaṇṭheśa, and the Kṣetrapāla; the narrative of Indradyumna; after that, the departure of Yama and Brahmā to their respective realms; the granting of a boon to Indradyumna by the Lord after assuming a wooden form; the arrival there of a brahmin and a kṣatriya named Puṇḍarīka and Ambarīṣaka, who were misbehaved but whose curiosity had been aroused upon hearing the recitation of the virtues of Hari with a wooden form; and Indradyumna's establishment of the wooden sacred ford right there, and the description of its māhātmya. (59, 1)

2.2.s:
5 tattīrthaprabhāvena puṇḍarīkāṃbarīṣakayorveśyādiduḥsaṃgatyāgavarṇanam, tayordoṣabāhulyā-
dbhagavatsvarūpasyādarśanam, bhagavaddarśanaṃ vinā'nnāgrahaṇarūpanigrahaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavatā
tayorniśīthe darśanadānam, tābhyāṃ bhagavatstutikaraṇam, satataṃ bhagavannāmagrahaṇena
tayormuktivarṇanama... ..... - -. - - - - - 61 1
2.2.d:
5 तत्तीर्थप्रभावेन पुण्डरीकांबरीषकयोर्वेश्यादिदुःसंगत्यागवर्णनम्, तयोर्दोषबाहुल्या-
द्भगवत्स्वरूपस्यादर्शनम्, भगवद्दर्शनं विनाऽन्नाग्रहणरूपनिग्रहं दृष्ट्वा भगवता
तयोर्निशीथे दर्शनदानम्, ताभ्यां भगवत्स्तुतिकरणम्, सततं भगवन्नामग्रहणेन
तयोर्मुक्तिवर्णनम... ..... - -. - - - - - 61 1
2.2.m: 5. By the power of that sacred ford, the description of Puṇḍarīka and Ambarīṣaka abandoning bad company such as courtesans; their inability to obtain darśana of the Lord's form due to the abundance of their faults; seeing their self-restraint in the form of refusing food without darśana of the Lord, the Lord's granting of darśana to them at midnight; their offering of praise to the Lord; the description of their liberation through constantly chanting the name of the Lord. (61, 1)

2.2.s:
6 etādṛśaṃ mahatpuṇyapradaṃ puruṣottamakṣetraṃ kva vartata iti ṛṣipraśnaṃ śrutvā jaimininā nānādrumasaṃkulārāmopaśobhitānekasatpuruṣasevita puṇyapradadakṣiṇodadhigāminīṛṣikulyā-
nadītīrasthotkaladeśavartīdaṃ kṣetramiti praśnottaradānam.. ... 62
2.2.d:
6 एतादृशं महत्पुण्यप्रदं पुरुषोत्तमक्षेत्रं क्व वर्तत इति ऋषिप्रश्नं श्रुत्वा जैमिनिना नानाद्रुमसंकुलारामोपशोभितानेकसत्पुरुषसेवित पुण्यप्रददक्षिणोदधिगामिनीऋषिकुल्या-
नदीतीरस्थोत्कलदेशवर्तीदं क्षेत्रमिति प्रश्नोत्तरदानम्.. ... 62
2.2.m: 6. Hearing the seer's question, "Where is such a Puruṣottamakṣetra, which bestows great merit, situated?", Jaimini's answering the question: "This sacred field is located in the land of Utkala on the bank of the Ṛṣikulyā river, which flows into the southern ocean and bestows merit, attended by many virtuous people and adorned with groves dense with diverse trees." (62)

2.2.s:
7 avaṃtīnagarasthendradyumnasya tīrthayātrāsamutsukasyājñayā purohitabhrāturvidyāpate rohiṇīkuṇḍakalpavṛkṣādipariveṣṭitaṃ puruṣottamakṣetraṃ gantumudyuktasya pathi śabaradarśanam
vidyāpatiśabarabhāṣaṇaṃ ca.. ..- 63 1
2.2.d:
7 अवंतीनगरस्थेन्द्रद्युम्नस्य तीर्थयात्रासमुत्सुकस्याज्ञया पुरोहितभ्रातुर्विद्यापते रोहिणीकुण्डकल्पवृक्षादिपरिवेष्टितं पुरुषोत्तमक्षेत्रं गन्तुमुद्युक्तस्य पथि शबरदर्शनम्
विद्यापतिशबरभाषणं च.. ..- 63 1
2.2.m: 7. By the command of Indradyumna, residing in the city of Avanti, who was eager to go on pilgrimage: the priest's brother Vidyāpati sets out to go to Puruṣottamakṣetra, surrounded by the Rohiṇī pool, the wish-granting tree, and other landmarks; his sighting of a Śabara on the road; and the conversation between Vidyāpati and the Śabara. (63, 1)

2.2.s: 8 dinatrayopoṣitaṃ vidyāpatiṃ dṛṣṭvā rājakāryamakṛtvā bhagavaddarśanaṃ vinā naivānnagrahaṇamiti tanniścayaṃ jñātvā cintayānasya śabarasya vidyāpatinā saha vanaprayāṇapūrvakarohiṇīkuṃḍagamanama , tatra bhagavaddarśanama , tena bhagavatstutikaraṇam, paścādvidyāpateḥ svadeśagamanotsukatvavarṇanama,. 65
2.2.d: 8 दिनत्रयोपोषितं विद्यापतिं दृष्ट्वा राजकार्यमकृत्वा भगवद्दर्शनं विना नैवान्नग्रहणमिति तन्निश्चयं ज्ञात्वा चिन्तयानस्य शबरस्य विद्यापतिना सह वनप्रयाणपूर्वकरोहिणीकुंडगमनम , तत्र भगवद्दर्शनम , तेन भगवत्स्तुतिकरणम्, पश्चाद्विद्यापतेः स्वदेशगमनोत्सुकत्ववर्णनम,. 65
2.2.m: 8. Seeing that Vidyāpati had fasted for three days, and knowing his resolve not to take food without having darśana of the Lord before accomplishing the king's business, the Śabara considers [the matter] and goes with Vidyāpati to the Rohiṇī pool after journeying through the forest; obtaining darśana of the Lord there; the praise of the Lord offered by him; and afterward, the description of Vidyāpati's eagerness to return to his own country. (65)

2.2.s:
9 yāvadvidyāpatiḥ svadeśaṃ gantumudyuktastāvanpūjāsamaye caṇḍavātena sarvadevānāṃ netre
mtrarṇasikatāyā vikarṣaṇam, tena teṣāṃ devānāṃ bhagavaddarśanarāhityena bhagavadavalokanaprāptyai bhagavatstutivarṇanam, ita uttaraṃ bhagavaddarśanaṃ keṣāmapi naiva bhavediti bhagavaduktivarṇanama, tato vidyāpateravantyāṃ dinātyaye pratinivṛtyāgamanam, rājakṛtotthānādisatkāreṇa vidyāpatinā rājñaḥ kaṇṭhe nirmālyamālāyāḥ samāropādivarṇanam, vidyāpatīndradyumnābhyāṃ bhagavatstutikaraṇam, vidyāpatikathitapuruṣottamakṣetrarohiṇīkuṇḍāditīrthaprabhāvavarṇanam.. 66 2
2.2.d:
9 यावद्विद्यापतिः स्वदेशं गन्तुमुद्युक्तस्तावन्पूजासमये चण्डवातेन सर्वदेवानां नेत्रे
म्त्रर्णसिकताया विकर्षणम्, तेन तेषां देवानां भगवद्दर्शनराहित्येन भगवदवलोकनप्राप्त्यै भगवत्स्तुतिवर्णनम्, इत उत्तरं भगवद्दर्शनं केषामपि नैव भवेदिति भगवदुक्तिवर्णनम, ततो विद्यापतेरवन्त्यां दिनात्यये प्रतिनिवृत्यागमनम्, राजकृतोत्थानादिसत्कारेण विद्यापतिना राज्ञः कण्ठे निर्माल्यमालायाः समारोपादिवर्णनम्, विद्यापतीन्द्रद्युम्नाभ्यां भगवत्स्तुतिकरणम्, विद्यापतिकथितपुरुषोत्तमक्षेत्ररोहिणीकुण्डादितीर्थप्रभाववर्णनम्.. 66 2
2.2.m: 9. Just as Vidyāpati was prepared to depart for his own country, at the time of worship a fierce wind blew sea sand into the eyes of all the gods, whereby, deprived of the Lord's darśana, those gods uttered a hymn of praise to the Lord in order to obtain a vision of Him; the description of the Lord's statement that henceforth no one at all would have darśana of the Lord; then Vidyāpati's return to Avantī after several days; the king's reception of him with rising and other honours, Vidyāpati placing the garland of consecrated flowers around the king's neck; the praise of the Lord sung by Vidyāpati and Indradyumna; and the description of the power of Puruṣottamakṣetra, Rohiṇīkuṇḍa, and other sacred places as related by Vidyāpati. 66 2

2.2.s: 10 indradyumnavacasā vidyāpatinā puruṣottamakṣetrastha bhagavatsvarūpādi vaṭavṛkṣādyanekatīrthamāhātmyapūrvakaṃ sāyāhne caṃḍavātena vyathitadevasthitisvarūpavarṇanam, tatrāṃtare tatsamīpe nāradāgamanam, indradyumnakṛtanāradasatkāraḥ, indradyumnaṃ prati- nāradakathita vaiṣṇavamāhātmyavarṇanama........ 68 1
2.2.d: 10 इन्द्रद्युम्नवचसा विद्यापतिना पुरुषोत्तमक्षेत्रस्थ भगवत्स्वरूपादि वटवृक्षाद्यनेकतीर्थमाहात्म्यपूर्वकं सायाह्ने चंडवातेन व्यथितदेवस्थितिस्वरूपवर्णनम्, तत्रांतरे तत्समीपे नारदागमनम्, इन्द्रद्युम्नकृतनारदसत्कारः, इन्द्रद्युम्नं प्रति- नारदकथित वैष्णवमाहात्म्यवर्णनम........ 68 1
2.2.m: 10. At Indradyumna's request, Vidyāpati's description of the Lord's form and related matters situated in Puruṣottamakṣetra, prefaced by the māhātmya of the banyan tree and various other tīrthas, along with the state of the deities distressed by the fierce wind in the evening; meanwhile, the arrival of Nārada in his presence; Indradyumna's hospitality toward Nārada; and the description of the Vaiṣṇava māhātmya related by Nārada to Indradyumna. 68 1

2.2.s: 11 nīlādristhabhagavaddarśanasamutsuko'yamiti jñātvā tvāṃ tatra neṣyāmīti nāradavacanamākarṇya rājñaḥ purohitena samaṃ sarvanāgarikānanulakṣīkṛtya sarvaiḥ saha nīlamādhavadarśanaṃ grahītuṃ nāradena samaṃ bherīmṛdaṃgādivādyaiḥ saha caturaṅgasainyaṃ gṛhītvā bahiḥ prasthānam, pathi cotkaladeśasīmāsthāṃ carcikānāmnīṃ devī dṛṣṭvā tasyā varṇanam, oḍhrarājakṛtendradyumnasvāgatavarṇanam tayormithaḥ saṃbhāṣaṇottaraṃ niśīthe oḍhrarājña indradyumnājñayā nijanagaraṃ pratyāgamanādivṛttāntavarṇanam ...... -.. 70 2
2.2.d: 11 नीलाद्रिस्थभगवद्दर्शनसमुत्सुकोऽयमिति ज्ञात्वा त्वां तत्र नेष्यामीति नारदवचनमाकर्ण्य राज्ञः पुरोहितेन समं सर्वनागरिकाननुलक्षीकृत्य सर्वैः सह नीलमाधवदर्शनं ग्रहीतुं नारदेन समं भेरीमृदंगादिवाद्यैः सह चतुरङ्गसैन्यं गृहीत्वा बहिः प्रस्थानम्, पथि चोत्कलदेशसीमास्थां चर्चिकानाम्नीं देवी दृष्ट्वा तस्या वर्णनम्, ओढ्रराजकृतेन्द्रद्युम्नस्वागतवर्णनम् तयोर्मिथः संभाषणोत्तरं निशीथे ओढ्रराज्ञ इन्द्रद्युम्नाज्ञया निजनगरं प्रत्यागमनादिवृत्तान्तवर्णनम् ...... -.. 70 2
2.2.m: 11. Knowing that [the king] was eager to behold the Lord dwelling on the Blue Mountain, hearing Nārada's word, 'I shall lead you there', the king, taking into account all the citizens along with the royal priest, set out with all of them to obtain darśana of Nīlamādhava, accompanied by Nārada, taking a fourfold army with musical instruments such as kettledrums and mṛdaṅgas; on the road, seeing the goddess named Carcikā residing on the border of the Utkala country, a description of her; the description of Indradyumna's welcome by the king of Oḍhra; after their mutual conversation, at midnight, by Indradyumna's command, the description of the account of the king of Oḍhra's return to his own city and other events. 70 2

2.2.s:
12 oḍhrarājagamanānantaraṃ gatena nāradenendradyumnāya madhyemārgaṃ parvatopari sthitasya śivamaṃdirasya vṛttāntakathanam, tatra gaurīpriyaṃ kurvatā śaṃkareṇa vārāṇasīsamīpasthā-
vimuktikṣetrasthāpanam, kāśīrājena śivato varalabdhiḥ, śrīkṛṣṇakāśirājayoryuddhaṃ,
kāśīnagaropari śrīkṛṣṇapreṣitasudarśanena kāśirājasya śiraśchittvā kāśīnagarīdāhaḥ, tadroṣitena śivena śrīkṛṣṇopari pāśupatāstrapraharaṇam, pāśupataṃ vijitya kāśyāṃ nirdagdhāyāṃ bhītena śaṃkareṇa viṣṇustutikaraṇam, stutiprasannena viṣṇunā mannāmnākhyātaṃ puruṣottametikṣetrasthāpanaṃ kurvityādeśakaraṇama, viṣṇvājñayā
śrīśaṃkareṇa puruṣottamakṣetrasthāpanam, iti tatkṣetrasthāpanamāhātmyaṃ śrutveṃdradyumnena
nīlamādhavapuruṣottamastutikaraṇam, tata ekāmranāmakaṃ tryambakakṣetramāgatya taṃ pūjayitvā koṭiliṃgeśasya stutikaraṇam, tena prasannena koṭiliṃgeśena indradyumnasya
vaiṣṇavatvavarṇanama, śivāntardhānam, tata indradyumnasya nāradena sākaṃ kapāteśakṣetre gamanam, bilveśādidevatā namaskṛtya nāradena saha rathamāsthāya bhagavaccintanaṃ
kurvata indradyumnasya bhagavatsānnidhye gamanam. .. ... .. 73
2.2.d:
12 ओढ्रराजगमनानन्तरं गतेन नारदेनेन्द्रद्युम्नाय मध्येमार्गं पर्वतोपरि स्थितस्य शिवमंदिरस्य वृत्तान्तकथनम्, तत्र गौरीप्रियं कुर्वता शंकरेण वाराणसीसमीपस्था-
विमुक्तिक्षेत्रस्थापनम्, काशीराजेन शिवतो वरलब्धिः, श्रीकृष्णकाशिराजयोर्युद्धं,
काशीनगरोपरि श्रीकृष्णप्रेषितसुदर्शनेन काशिराजस्य शिरश्छित्त्वा काशीनगरीदाहः, तद्रोषितेन शिवेन श्रीकृष्णोपरि पाशुपतास्त्रप्रहरणम्, पाशुपतं विजित्य काश्यां निर्दग्धायां भीतेन शंकरेण विष्णुस्तुतिकरणम्, स्तुतिप्रसन्नेन विष्णुना मन्नाम्नाख्यातं पुरुषोत्तमेतिक्षेत्रस्थापनं कुर्वित्यादेशकरणम, विष्ण्वाज्ञया
श्रीशंकरेण पुरुषोत्तमक्षेत्रस्थापनम्, इति तत्क्षेत्रस्थापनमाहात्म्यं श्रुत्वेंद्रद्युम्नेन
नीलमाधवपुरुषोत्तमस्तुतिकरणम्, तत एकाम्रनामकं त्र्यम्बकक्षेत्रमागत्य तं पूजयित्वा कोटिलिंगेशस्य स्तुतिकरणम्, तेन प्रसन्नेन कोटिलिंगेशेन इन्द्रद्युम्नस्य
वैष्णवत्ववर्णनम, शिवान्तर्धानम्, तत इन्द्रद्युम्नस्य नारदेन साकं कपातेशक्षेत्रे गमनम्, बिल्वेशादिदेवता नमस्कृत्य नारदेन सह रथमास्थाय भगवच्चिन्तनं
कुर्वत इन्द्रद्युम्नस्य भगवत्सान्निध्ये गमनम्. .. ... .. 73
2.2.m: 12. After the departure of the king of Oḍhra, Nārada, having gone on, related to Indradyumna the account of the temple of Śiva situated on a mountain along the way; Śaṃkara, doing what pleased Gaurī, established there the Avimuktakṣetra near Vārāṇasī; the obtaining of a boon by the king of Kāśī from Śiva; the battle between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and the king of Kāśī; by the Sudarśana [discus] dispatched by Śrī Kṛṣṇa against the city of Kāśī, the severing of the head of the king of Kāśī and the burning of the city of Kāśī; the hurling of the Pāśupata weapon at Śrī Kṛṣṇa by Śiva, who was enraged by that; having defeated the Pāśupata weapon and when Kāśī was burnt, Śaṃkara, terrified, praised Viṣṇu; Viṣṇu, pleased by the hymn, gave the command, 'Establish a kṣetra named after me called Puruṣottama'; the establishment of Puruṣottamakṣetra by Śrī Śaṃkara at Viṣṇu's command; hearing the māhātmya of the establishment of that kṣetra, Indradyumna uttered a hymn of praise to Nīlamādhava Puruṣottama; then, arriving at Tryambakakṣetra named Ekāmra and worshipping him, he uttered a hymn of praise to Koṭiliṅgeśa; Koṭiliṅgeśa, pleased thereby, described the Vaiṣṇava nature of Indradyumna; Śiva's disappearance; then Indradyumna's journey with Nārada to the Kapāteśa kṣetra; bowing to the deities such as Bilveśa, mounting the chariot with Nārada, Indradyumna, meditating on the Lord, entered the Lord's presence. 73

2.2.s:
13 śaṃkaradhṛtakapotaveṣeṇa bhagavadārādhanāṃ kṛtvā tatprasādena kapoteśasthalīsthāpanama, tataḥ pātālavāsibhirdaityaiḥ pīḍitāṃ bhuvaṃ dṛṣṭvā tadasuranibarhaṇāya śrīkṛṣṇena bilvaphalaṃ
gṛhītvā bhagavadārādhanāṃ kṛtvā tryaṃbakakṛpayā asurāñjitvā bilveśakṣetrasthāpanam
tanmāhātmyavarṇanaṃ ca... ... .. ... 76
2.2.d:
13 शंकरधृतकपोतवेषेण भगवदाराधनां कृत्वा तत्प्रसादेन कपोतेशस्थलीस्थापनम, ततः पातालवासिभिर्दैत्यैः पीडितां भुवं दृष्ट्वा तदसुरनिबर्हणाय श्रीकृष्णेन बिल्वफलं
गृहीत्वा भगवदाराधनां कृत्वा त्र्यंबककृपया असुराञ्जित्वा बिल्वेशक्षेत्रस्थापनम्
तन्माहात्म्यवर्णनं च... ... .. ... 76
2.2.m: 13. Śaṃkara, having assumed the guise of a dove, performed the worship of the Lord and, through His grace, established the site of Kapoteśa; then, seeing the earth afflicted by the daityas residing in Pātāla, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, in order to destroy those asuras, took a bilva fruit and performed the worship of the Lord, and by the grace of Tryambaka defeated the asuras and established the Bilveśakṣetra; and the description of its māhātmya. 76

2.2.s:
14. sapurohitasyendradyumnasya nāradena saha nīlakaṇṭhakṣetraṃ prati gamanam, vartmani vāma-
bāhusphuraṇādyapaśakunāndṛṣṭvā suduḥkhitena rājñā nāradaṃ prati kimimamiti praśnaḥ tato nāradena tvayā samaṃ puruṣottamakṣetre gatvā'ntarhite'pi bhagavati dāravatanuṃ dṛṣṭvā'śvakratuṃ vidhāya te bhagavaddarśanaṃ niścayena kārayiṣyāmīti pratijñāpūrvakamindradyumnasya sāntvanam -....... .. 76
2.2.d:
14. सपुरोहितस्येन्द्रद्युम्नस्य नारदेन सह नीलकण्ठक्षेत्रं प्रति गमनम्, वर्त्मनि वाम-
बाहुस्फुरणाद्यपशकुनान्दृष्ट्वा सुदुःखितेन राज्ञा नारदं प्रति किमिममिति प्रश्नः ततो नारदेन त्वया समं पुरुषोत्तमक्षेत्रे गत्वाऽन्तर्हितेऽपि भगवति दारवतनुं दृष्ट्वाऽश्वक्रतुं विधाय ते भगवद्दर्शनं निश्चयेन कारयिष्यामीति प्रतिज्ञापूर्वकमिन्द्रद्युम्नस्य सान्त्वनम् -....... .. 76
2.2.m: 14. Indradyumna with his priest went with Nārada toward the Nīlakaṇṭha kṣetra; seeing bad omens on the path such as the throbbing of the left arm, the king, exceedingly sorrowful, asked Nārada, 'What is this?'; then Nārada consoled Indradyumna with a vow, saying: 'Going with you to Puruṣottamakṣetra, even though the Lord has disappeared, having seen the wooden form and performed a horse sacrifice, I shall surely bring about your darśana of the Lord.' 76

2.2.s: 15 tato nāradena saha saviprasyendradyumnasya nīlaparvatopari tiṣṭhantaṃ devaṃ draṣṭuṃ nīlakaṇṭhasakāśato nirgatya nīlabhūdharaśikharopari narasiṃhadarśanam,bhagavaddarśanaṃ gṛhītvā tato nāradena puruṣottamabhagavatsthitisthaladarśanam, tataḥ sarvaiḥ sahendradyumnena bhagavatstutikaraṇam, stutiprasannena bhagavatā'śarīriṇyā vāṇyendradyumnāya vājimedhaṃ kurvityājñākaraṇam, bhagavadājñayendradyumnakṛtavājimedhasamāraṃbhavarṇanam. .. 77
2.2.d: 15 ततो नारदेन सह सविप्रस्येन्द्रद्युम्नस्य नीलपर्वतोपरि तिष्ठन्तं देवं द्रष्टुं नीलकण्ठसकाशतो निर्गत्य नीलभूधरशिखरोपरि नरसिंहदर्शनम्,भगवद्दर्शनं गृहीत्वा ततो नारदेन पुरुषोत्तमभगवत्स्थितिस्थलदर्शनम्, ततः सर्वैः सहेन्द्रद्युम्नेन भगवत्स्तुतिकरणम्, स्तुतिप्रसन्नेन भगवताऽशरीरिण्या वाण्येन्द्रद्युम्नाय वाजिमेधं कुर्वित्याज्ञाकरणम्, भगवदाज्ञयेन्द्रद्युम्नकृतवाजिमेधसमारंभवर्णनम्. .. 77
2.2.m: 15. Then, Indradyumna with the brahmins and Nārada, setting out from the vicinity of Nīlakaṇṭha to see the god dwelling on the Blue Mountain, had darśana of Narasiṃha upon the peak of the Blue Mountain; having received the darśana of the Lord, Nārada then showed the place of the Lord Puruṣottama's dwelling; then Indradyumna along with all praised the Lord; the Lord, pleased by the hymn of praise, gave the command to Indradyumna with a bodiless voice: 'Perform a horse sacrifice'; and the description of the commencement of the horse sacrifice undertaken by Indradyumna at the Lord's command. 77

2.2.s: 16 nāradānujñayā narasiṃhamūrtisthāpanārthamagrata indradyumnasya gamanam, candanadrumasamīpamāgatyendradyumnaṃ prati tvadarthe narasiṃhālayaṃ ghaṭayiṣyāmīti devaśilpisutasya saṃbhāṣaṇam, indrādyumnājñayā devaśilpinā devālayanirmāṇam, tato nāradahastena narasiṃhamūrtisthāpanam, sthāpitanṛsiṃhamūrterindradyumnakṛtastutivarṇanam, nṛsiṃhamāhātmya varṇanam -.. 0... ...... 78 2
2.2.d: 16 नारदानुज्ञया नरसिंहमूर्तिस्थापनार्थमग्रत इन्द्रद्युम्नस्य गमनम्, चन्दनद्रुमसमीपमागत्येन्द्रद्युम्नं प्रति त्वदर्थे नरसिंहालयं घटयिष्यामीति देवशिल्पिसुतस्य संभाषणम्, इन्द्राद्युम्नाज्ञया देवशिल्पिना देवालयनिर्माणम्, ततो नारदहस्तेन नरसिंहमूर्तिस्थापनम्, स्थापितनृसिंहमूर्तेरिन्द्रद्युम्नकृतस्तुतिवर्णनम्, नृसिंहमाहात्म्य वर्णनम् -.. 0... ...... 78 2
2.2.m: 16. With Nārada's permission, Indradyumna went forward to install the image of Narasiṃha; approaching a sandalwood tree, the divine architect's son spoke to Indradyumna: 'For your sake I will fashion an abode for Narasiṃha'; by Indradyumna's order, the divine architect constructed the temple; then, the installation of the image of Narasiṃha by Nārada's hand; the description of the hymn of praise made by Indradyumna to the installed image of Nṛsiṃha; and the description of the māhātmya of Nṛsiṃha. 78 2

2.2.s:
17 indradyumnena kratukaraṇārthaṃ sendrāndevānstutvā āmantrya ca devasāhāyyena vājimedhakratuyajñamahotsavakaraṇam, tadyajñaprabhāveṇendradyumnasya dinedine kāntyādhikyaṃ gatasya svapne śeṣaśāyibhagavaddarśanam, nāradaṃ prati svapnavṛttānte prokte nāradena tasya
svapnasya suphalakathanam.... - -.. .. .... 80 1
2.2.d:
17 इन्द्रद्युम्नेन क्रतुकरणार्थं सेन्द्रान्देवान्स्तुत्वा आमन्त्र्य च देवसाहाय्येन वाजिमेधक्रतुयज्ञमहोत्सवकरणम्, तद्यज्ञप्रभावेणेन्द्रद्युम्नस्य दिनेदिने कान्त्याधिक्यं गतस्य स्वप्ने शेषशायिभगवद्दर्शनम्, नारदं प्रति स्वप्नवृत्तान्ते प्रोक्ते नारदेन तस्य
स्वप्नस्य सुफलकथनम्.... - -.. .. .... 80 1
2.2.m: 17. Indradyumna, in order to perform the sacrifice, praised and invited the gods headed by Indra, and with the help of the gods celebrated the great festival of the horse sacrifice; by the power of that sacrifice, Indradyumna, whose splendour increased day by day, saw the Lord reclining on Śeṣa in a dream; when the account of the dream was related to Nārada, Nārada explained the auspicious fruit of that dream. 80 1

2.2.s: 18 atha bilveśvarāsannapradeśe samudrasya taṭānte'kasmādāgatya prādurbhūtaṃ kaṃcidvṛkṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayamāpannaistadrakṣakai rājānaṃ prati vṛkṣadarśanavṛttāntanivedanam, tato'vabhṛthasnānena yajñaparisamāptiḥ, bhagavadromabhirnirmito'yamiti nāradena tadvṛkṣamāhātmyavarṇanam, . vṛkṣasthāpanam, tataḥ kasmiṃścitsamaye pūjāṃ kartuṃ sthitenendradyumnena kīdṛśī viṣṇumūrtirvidhayetyevaṃ nāradaṃ prati praśnaḥ, ko vā cedṛśīṃ mūrtiṃ vidhāsyatīti cintayatastasya rājño'gre bhagavadbhṛtavṛddhavarddhakisvarūpadarśanam, ahaṃ tāṃ mūrtiṃ vidhāsyāmīti kathayitvā tasya tasyāṃ paṭācchāditāyāṃ vedyāmevāntardhānama. ... 82 2
2.2.d: 18 अथ बिल्वेश्वरासन्नप्रदेशे समुद्रस्य तटान्तेऽकस्मादागत्य प्रादुर्भूतं कंचिद्वृक्षं दृष्ट्वा विस्मयमापन्नैस्तद्रक्षकै राजानं प्रति वृक्षदर्शनवृत्तान्तनिवेदनम्, ततोऽवभृथस्नानेन यज्ञपरिसमाप्तिः, भगवद्रोमभिर्निर्मितोऽयमिति नारदेन तद्वृक्षमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, . वृक्षस्थापनम्, ततः कस्मिंश्चित्समये पूजां कर्तुं स्थितेनेन्द्रद्युम्नेन कीदृशी विष्णुमूर्तिर्विधयेत्येवं नारदं प्रति प्रश्नः, को वा चेदृशीं मूर्तिं विधास्यतीति चिन्तयतस्तस्य राज्ञोऽग्रे भगवद्भृतवृद्धवर्द्धकिस्वरूपदर्शनम्, अहं तां मूर्तिं विधास्यामीति कथयित्वा तस्य तस्यां पटाच्छादितायां वेद्यामेवान्तर्धानम. ... 82 2
2.2.m: 18. Then, in the vicinity of Bilveśvara, at the edge of the seashore, seeing a certain tree that had suddenly appeared and manifested, its guards, filled with wonder, reported the occurrence of seeing the tree to the king; then, with the avabhṛtha ritual ablution, the sacrifice was concluded; Nārada's explanation of the māhātmya of that tree, saying, "This has been created from the hairs of the Lord"; the installation of the tree; then, when Indradyumna stood at a certain time to perform worship, his question to Nārada as to what sort of image of Viṣṇu should be made; while that king was wondering who indeed would make such an image, the Lord's manifestation before him in the form of an old carpenter; having declared, "I shall make that image," his disappearance within that very altar-platform covered with a cloth. ... 82 2

2.2.s: 19 athendradyumnaṃ pratyākāśavāṇyā siddhamūrtisaṃskārapūrvaka sthāpanādipūjāpravṛttiviṣayakājñākaraṇam, tataḥ paccadaśadinottaraṃ mahāvediveṣṭanamunmocya siṃhāsanasthitarāma-kṛṣṇasubhadrāvāsudevasudarśanānāṃ darśanam, taddarśanasaṃjāta mahānandanimagnasyendradyumnasya nāradena bhāgyodayādhikyavarṇanam ... ... ... 83
2.2.d: 19 अथेन्द्रद्युम्नं प्रत्याकाशवाण्या सिद्धमूर्तिसंस्कारपूर्वक स्थापनादिपूजाप्रवृत्तिविषयकाज्ञाकरणम्, ततः पच्चदशदिनोत्तरं महावेदिवेष्टनमुन्मोच्य सिंहासनस्थितराम-कृष्णसुभद्रावासुदेवसुदर्शनानां दर्शनम्, तद्दर्शनसंजात महानन्दनिमग्नस्येन्द्रद्युम्नस्य नारदेन भाग्योदयाधिक्यवर्णनम् ... ... ... 83
2.2.m: 19. Then, an order issued by a voice from the sky to Indradyumna regarding proceeding with worship such as installation preceded by the consecration of the completed images; then, after fifteen days, uncovering the enclosure of the great altar-platform, the darśana of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Subhadrā, Vāsudeva, and Sudarśana seated on the throne; Nārada's description of the exceptional rise of good fortune for Indradyumna, who was immersed in great bliss born of that darśana. ... 83

2.2.s:
20 nāradabodhitena rājñā viṣṇustutikaraṇam, nāradena ca gadyarūpeṇa bhagavadrūpadhāriṇaḥ
sthāṇoḥ stutikaraṇam, anyairṛṣyāddibhirapi bhagavadvarṇanakaraṇam, indradyumnenā-
nekamantrasūktādibhiḥ saparivārasya bhagavataḥ pūjanam, tataśca rājñā brāhmaṇebhyastatra
koṭyavadhigopradānam, tataścendradyumnena bhagavadbhavyaprāsādanirmāṇāyārambhakaraṇam,
indradyumnavinirmitaprāsādapratiṣṭhāpanārthaṃ vidhyājñayā devānāṃ tatrāgamanam.. 84
2.2.d:
20 नारदबोधितेन राज्ञा विष्णुस्तुतिकरणम्, नारदेन च गद्यरूपेण भगवद्रूपधारिणः
स्थाणोः स्तुतिकरणम्, अन्यैरृष्याद्दिभिरपि भगवद्वर्णनकरणम्, इन्द्रद्युम्नेना-
नेकमन्त्रसूक्तादिभिः सपरिवारस्य भगवतः पूजनम्, ततश्च राज्ञा ब्राह्मणेभ्यस्तत्र
कोट्यवधिगोप्रदानम्, ततश्चेन्द्रद्युम्नेन भगवद्भव्यप्रासादनिर्माणायारम्भकरणम्,
इन्द्रद्युम्नविनिर्मितप्रासादप्रतिष्ठापनार्थं विध्याज्ञया देवानां तत्रागमनम्.. 84
2.2.m: 20. The king, instructed by Nārada, offering praise to Viṣṇu; Nārada offering praise in prose to the Pillar that assumed the Lord's form; other seers and people also describing the Lord; Indradyumna worshiping the Lord along with His retinue using numerous mantras, hymns, and so forth; then the king donating as many as ten million cows to the brahmins there; then Indradyumna commencing the construction of a magnificent temple for the Lord; the arrival of the gods there by order of Brahmā for the consecration of the temple built by Indradyumna. ... 84

2.2.s:
21 śrutyādivihitopāyairvinā naiva bhagavaddarśanamiti kasyacidṛgvedapāṭhino brāhmaṇasya
mukhāddāruvapurmāhātmyavarṇanaṃ śrutvā nāradenendradyumnarājñe vedavihitabhagavadupāsanopade-
śakaraṇapūrvakaṃ pratiṣṭhākāle brahmaṇo nimatraṇārthaṃ svasya brahmalokaṃ prati gaṃtumicchā-
prakaṭanam, rājño'pi vrahmāṇaṃ nimantrayituṃ brahmalokaṃ prati nāradāgre svecchāpra-
kaṭanam. .... 85 1
2.2.d:
21 श्रुत्यादिविहितोपायैर्विना नैव भगवद्दर्शनमिति कस्यचिदृग्वेदपाठिनो ब्राह्मणस्य
मुखाद्दारुवपुर्माहात्म्यवर्णनं श्रुत्वा नारदेनेन्द्रद्युम्नराज्ञे वेदविहितभगवदुपासनोपदे-
शकरणपूर्वकं प्रतिष्ठाकाले ब्रह्मणो निमत्रणार्थं स्वस्य ब्रह्मलोकं प्रति गंतुमिच्छा-
प्रकटनम्, राज्ञोऽपि व्रह्माणं निमन्त्रयितुं ब्रह्मलोकं प्रति नारदाग्रे स्वेच्छाप्र-
कटनम्. .... 85 1
2.2.m: 21. Hearing from the mouth of a certain Ṛgveda-reciting brahmin the description of the māhātmya of the wooden form, namely that darśana of the Lord does not occur without the means prescribed by the Vedic revelation and other scriptures, Nārada, after instructing King Indradyumna in the worship of the Lord prescribed by the Vedas, expressing his desire to go to the world of Brahmā in order to invite Brahmā at the time of consecration; the king also expressing his desire before Nārada to go to the world of Brahmā in order to invite Brahmā. ... 85 1

2.2.s: 22 atha nāradena samamindradyumnasya puṣparathavimānena brahmalokaṃ prati gamanam, madhyemārgaṃ rājyacintayā vyākulitacittaṃ nṛpaṃ prati śokakāraṇaviṣaye nāradena praśnakaraṇam, rājñaścintākāraṇaṃ śrutvā nāradena nṛpasya samādhānakaraṇapūrvakaṃ cintādūrīkaraṇam, tata indradyumranāradayoḥ sarvalokānbhrāntvā brahmalokaṃ prati prāptipūrvakaṃ dvārapālādikṛtasatkāravarṇanama.. -.. 87 2
2.2.d: 22 अथ नारदेन सममिन्द्रद्युम्नस्य पुष्परथविमानेन ब्रह्मलोकं प्रति गमनम्, मध्येमार्गं राज्यचिन्तया व्याकुलितचित्तं नृपं प्रति शोककारणविषये नारदेन प्रश्नकरणम्, राज्ञश्चिन्ताकारणं श्रुत्वा नारदेन नृपस्य समाधानकरणपूर्वकं चिन्तादूरीकरणम्, तत इन्द्रद्युम्रनारदयोः सर्वलोकान्भ्रान्त्वा ब्रह्मलोकं प्रति प्राप्तिपूर्वकं द्वारपालादिकृतसत्कारवर्णनम.. -.. 87 2
2.2.m: 22. Then, the departure of Indradyumna together with Nārada for the world of Brahmā in the Puṣparatha aerial chariot; along the way, Nārada questioning the king regarding the cause of his grief as the king's mind was anxious with concern for his kingdom; hearing the reason for the king's worry, Nārada removing his anxiety by reassuring the monarch; then, after wandering through all the worlds, Indradyumna and Nārada reaching the world of Brahmā, and the description of the hospitality extended by the doorkeepers and others. ... 87 2

2.2.s:
23 indradyumnena brahmadevapraṇāmakaraṇam, kimarthamāgamanamiti brahmaṇā praśne kṛte satīndradyumnena mayā nirmite prāsāde devasthāpanaṃ kartuṃ bhavadbhirāgantavyameveti brahmāṇaṃ prati prārthanākaraṇama, athendradyumnāya bhūtale bahukālātyayavṛttāntakathanapūrvakaṃ padmanidhinā devaiśca saha bhūtalaṃ prati gamanāyājñākaraṇam, pratiṣṭhākarmaṇi svasyā-
gamanāyāśvāsanapradānam, tato brahmājñayendradyumnamahīpateḥ sarvadevaiḥ padmanidhinā
brahmarṣibhiśca saha bhūtalaṃ pratyāgamanam .. 88 1
2.2.d:
23 इन्द्रद्युम्नेन ब्रह्मदेवप्रणामकरणम्, किमर्थमागमनमिति ब्रह्मणा प्रश्ने कृते सतीन्द्रद्युम्नेन मया निर्मिते प्रासादे देवस्थापनं कर्तुं भवद्भिरागन्तव्यमेवेति ब्रह्माणं प्रति प्रार्थनाकरणम, अथेन्द्रद्युम्नाय भूतले बहुकालात्ययवृत्तान्तकथनपूर्वकं पद्मनिधिना देवैश्च सह भूतलं प्रति गमनायाज्ञाकरणम्, प्रतिष्ठाकर्मणि स्वस्या-
गमनायाश्वासनप्रदानम्, ततो ब्रह्माज्ञयेन्द्रद्युम्नमहीपतेः सर्वदेवैः पद्मनिधिना
ब्रह्मर्षिभिश्च सह भूतलं प्रत्यागमनम् .. 88 1
2.2.m: 23. Indradyumna offering obeisance to Brahmā; when Brahmā asked the purpose of his arrival, Indradyumna entreating Brahmā: "You must certainly come to install the deity in the temple built by me"; then [Brahmā] narrating to Indradyumna the lapse of a long period of time on the mortal realm, and commanding him to return to earth along with Padmanidhi and the gods; his giving assurance of his own arrival for the consecration ceremony; then, by order of Brahmā, King Indradyumna returning to earth together with all the gods, Padmanidhi, and the brahmin seers. ... 88 1

2.2.s: 24 devairvipraiḥ padmanidhinā ca sahendradyumnena tatrāgatya bhagavaddarśanaṃ gṛhītvā puruṣasūktena bhagavatstutikaraṇam, tataḥ padmanidhidvārā dārumūrtiṃ sthāpayeti nabhovāṇyā bhagavadvacanam-. -. ... 90 1
2.2.d: 24 देवैर्विप्रैः पद्मनिधिना च सहेन्द्रद्युम्नेन तत्रागत्य भगवद्दर्शनं गृहीत्वा पुरुषसूक्तेन भगवत्स्तुतिकरणम्, ततः पद्मनिधिद्वारा दारुमूर्तिं स्थापयेति नभोवाण्या भगवद्वचनम्-. -. ... 90 1
2.2.m: 24. Indradyumna arriving there with the gods, brahmins, and Padmanidhi, receiving darśana of the Lord, and praising the Lord with the Puruṣasūkta; then the utterance of the Lord by a voice from the sky: "Install the wooden image through Padmanidhi." ... 90 1

2.2.s: 25 nāradalikhitasāhityasaṃbhārasaṃgrahapatraṃ śrutvendradyumnājñayā padmanidhinā svarṇaśālānirmāṇam, nāradājñayā viśvakarmaṇā syandanatrayanirmāṇam, tasya rathasya nāradakareṇa sthāpanam, tatprasaṃgena rathasthāpanavidhiprakāravarṇanam, rathadhvaje nṛsiṃhamūrtiṃ vidhāya samantrakāṃ garuḍaprārthanāṃ kṛtvā rathe bhagavanmūrtipratiṣṭhāpanavarṇanam, paścādbhagavatprārthanāṃ kṛtvā kena rathāvayavena naṣṭena kasya vināśa ityapaghātādidoṣavarṇanam, rathasyāsamaṃtato digdevatāsthāpanādiprakāravarṇanam, bhagavatsvarūpavarṇanam, bhagavatā lokānāmāśīrvādapradānam ..... -... 91 1
2.2.d: 25 नारदलिखितसाहित्यसंभारसंग्रहपत्रं श्रुत्वेन्द्रद्युम्नाज्ञया पद्मनिधिना स्वर्णशालानिर्माणम्, नारदाज्ञया विश्वकर्मणा स्यन्दनत्रयनिर्माणम्, तस्य रथस्य नारदकरेण स्थापनम्, तत्प्रसंगेन रथस्थापनविधिप्रकारवर्णनम्, रथध्वजे नृसिंहमूर्तिं विधाय समन्त्रकां गरुडप्रार्थनां कृत्वा रथे भगवन्मूर्तिप्रतिष्ठापनवर्णनम्, पश्चाद्भगवत्प्रार्थनां कृत्वा केन रथावयवेन नष्टेन कस्य विनाश इत्यपघातादिदोषवर्णनम्, रथस्यासमंततो दिग्देवतास्थापनादिप्रकारवर्णनम्, भगवत्स्वरूपवर्णनम्, भगवता लोकानामाशीर्वादप्रदानम् ..... -... 91 1
2.2.m: 25. Hearing the inventory of required materials written by Nārada, Padmanidhi constructing a golden hall at Indradyumna's command; Viśvakarman constructing three chariots by order of Nārada; the installation of that chariot by Nārada's hand; in that connection, the description of the rules and procedure for chariot installation; making an image of Narasiṃha on the chariot's banner, praying to Garuḍa with mantras, and describing the consecration of the Lord's image upon the chariot; then, praying to the Lord, describing the faults such as accidents—as to the destruction of what would occur with the destruction of which chariot part; the description of the procedure for installing the guardian deities of the directions all around the chariot; the description of the Lord's true form; the Lord bestowing blessings upon the people. ... 91 1

2.2.s: 26 prāsādasthāpitasya bhagavata indradyumnena pūjanakaraṇam, svarāṣṭre'nyarājña āgamanaśaṃkayā kruddhasya sasainyasya gālanṛpatestatrāgamanam, tasya gālabhūbhṛta indradyumnasaṃpāditāndurlabhasaṃbhārāndṛṣṭvā''ścaryacakitatvam, paścānnamrībhūtena gālenendradyumnaṃ prati svasya yuddhārthāgamanādisarvavṛttakathanam, tato gālendradyumnayormithaḥ saṃbhāṣaṇottaramindradyumnasya svātmapūrvavaṃśapuruṣatvaṃ jñātvā gālabhūpatinendradyumnasya svarājyasiṃhāsane sthāpanapūrvakaṃ tadājñāvartitvasvīkaraṇam .. .. ... 92 2
2.2.d: 26 प्रासादस्थापितस्य भगवत इन्द्रद्युम्नेन पूजनकरणम्, स्वराष्ट्रेऽन्यराज्ञ आगमनशंकया क्रुद्धस्य ससैन्यस्य गालनृपतेस्तत्रागमनम्, तस्य गालभूभृत इन्द्रद्युम्नसंपादितान्दुर्लभसंभारान्दृष्ट्वा'ऽश्चर्यचकितत्वम्, पश्चान्नम्रीभूतेन गालेनेन्द्रद्युम्नं प्रति स्वस्य युद्धार्थागमनादिसर्ववृत्तकथनम्, ततो गालेन्द्रद्युम्नयोर्मिथः संभाषणोत्तरमिन्द्रद्युम्नस्य स्वात्मपूर्ववंशपुरुषत्वं ज्ञात्वा गालभूपतिनेन्द्रद्युम्नस्य स्वराज्यसिंहासने स्थापनपूर्वकं तदाज्ञावर्तित्वस्वीकरणम् .. .. ... 92 2
2.2.m: 26. Indradyumna's worship of the Lord installed in the temple; King Gāla's arrival there with an army, enraged by the apprehension that another king had arrived in his realm; that King Gāla being struck with wonder upon seeing the rare materials procured by Indradyumna; Gāla subsequently humbling himself and narrating to Indradyumna his entire story, such as his coming for battle; then, after a mutual conversation between Gāla and Indradyumna, King Gāla, having learned that Indradyumna was his own ancestral forebear, installing Indradyumna upon the throne of his own kingdom and submitting to his command. ... 92 2

2.2.s:
27 atha brahmendrādibhirindradyumnakṛtabhagavanmandirapratiṣṭhārthaṃ brahmalokādbhūlokamāgatyendradyumnabhaktivaibhavavarṇanam, tato brahmāgamanasaṃtuṣṭenendradyumnena brahmadevaprārthanākaraṇam, brahmadevena rathaprāsādādikānāṃ darśanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavatstotrakaraṇam, tataḥ subhadrāsyandanaṃ gatvā brahmadevakṛtasubhadrāstutivarṇanam, balabhadrasya stotrakaraṇam, syandanatrayapūjana-
phalaśrutikathanam.... 93
2.2.d:
27 अथ ब्रह्मेन्द्रादिभिरिन्द्रद्युम्नकृतभगवन्मन्दिरप्रतिष्ठार्थं ब्रह्मलोकाद्भूलोकमागत्येन्द्रद्युम्नभक्तिवैभववर्णनम्, ततो ब्रह्मागमनसंतुष्टेनेन्द्रद्युम्नेन ब्रह्मदेवप्रार्थनाकरणम्, ब्रह्मदेवेन रथप्रासादादिकानां दर्शनं गृहीत्वा भगवत्स्तोत्रकरणम्, ततः सुभद्रास्यन्दनं गत्वा ब्रह्मदेवकृतसुभद्रास्तुतिवर्णनम्, बलभद्रस्य स्तोत्रकरणम्, स्यन्दनत्रयपूजन-
फलश्रुतिकथनम्.... 93
2.2.m: 27. Then, Brahmā, Indra, and others coming from the world of Brahmā to the mortal realm for the consecration of the Lord's temple built by Indradyumna, and the description of the magnificence of Indradyumna's devotion; then Indradyumna, delighted by Brahmā's arrival, offering a prayer to Brahmā; Brahmā receiving darśana of the chariots, temple, and other structures, and offering a hymn of praise to the Lord; then going to Subhadrā's chariot, the description of Brahmā's hymn of praise to Subhadrā, the hymn of praise to Balabhadra, and the recital of the fruits of worshiping the three chariots. ... 93

2.2.s: 28 tato'kasmātprakaṭitaṃ bhayaṃkaraṃ narakesarisvarūpaṃ dṛṣṭvendradyumnādikānāṃ bhayatrastatāvarṇanam, nāradavacasā brahmaṇā nṛsiṃhaprabhāvakathanam nṛsiṃhasya brahmaṇā stotrakaraṇam, devatāpratiṣṭhāsamayoccāritamaṃtraistattaddevatānāṃ pratyakṣadarśanaṃ svasthānāvasthānaṃ ca, vedādīnāmapi pratyakṣamūrtibhirāgamanama, brahmadevenendradyumnāya mantropadeśakaraṇam tato lakṣmīnarasiṃhayoḥ śāntikaraṇam, dārudevatāpūjanamāhātmyavarṇanam... 95 2
2.2.d: 28 ततोऽकस्मात्प्रकटितं भयंकरं नरकेसरिस्वरूपं दृष्ट्वेन्द्रद्युम्नादिकानां भयत्रस्ततावर्णनम्, नारदवचसा ब्रह्मणा नृसिंहप्रभावकथनम् नृसिंहस्य ब्रह्मणा स्तोत्रकरणम्, देवताप्रतिष्ठासमयोच्चारितमंत्रैस्तत्तद्देवतानां प्रत्यक्षदर्शनं स्वस्थानावस्थानं च, वेदादीनामपि प्रत्यक्षमूर्तिभिरागमनम, ब्रह्मदेवेनेन्द्रद्युम्नाय मन्त्रोपदेशकरणम् ततो लक्ष्मीनरसिंहयोः शान्तिकरणम्, दारुदेवतापूजनमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्... 95 2
2.2.m: 28. Then, description of the terror of Indradyumna and the others upon seeing the terrifying form of the Man-Lion suddenly manifested; Brahmā's exposition of the power of Nṛsiṃha at Nārada's word; Brahmā's composition of a hymn of praise to Nṛsiṃha; the direct vision of those respective deities through the mantras chanted at the time of deity-installation, and their taking residence in their own abodes; the arrival also of the Vedas and others in personified bodies; Brahmā's transmission of the mantra to Indradyumna; then the propitiation of Lakṣmī and Narasiṃha; description of the māhātmya of worshipping the wooden deities... 95.2

2.2.s:
29 indradyumnena balabhadrasya dvādaśākṣaramaṃtrairnārāyaṇasya puruṣasūktena devyā devīsūktena
cārcanam, tato brahmadevena dārudehasyendradyumnabhaktapālanāya stotrakaraṇam, dārudehena bhagavatendradyumnāya varapradānam, dārudehena svamukhato rājñe sthānamāhātmyakathanam, māsatithyādiyogaparatvena japadānādiphalaśrutivarṇanam .. 96 2
2.2.d:
29 इन्द्रद्युम्नेन बलभद्रस्य द्वादशाक्षरमंत्रैर्नारायणस्य पुरुषसूक्तेन देव्या देवीसूक्तेन
चार्चनम्, ततो ब्रह्मदेवेन दारुदेहस्येन्द्रद्युम्नभक्तपालनाय स्तोत्रकरणम्, दारुदेहेन भगवतेन्द्रद्युम्नाय वरप्रदानम्, दारुदेहेन स्वमुखतो राज्ञे स्थानमाहात्म्यकथनम्, मासतिथ्यादियोगपरत्वेन जपदानादिफलश्रुतिवर्णनम् .. 96 2
2.2.m: 29. Worship by Indradyumna of Balabhadra with the twelve-syllable mantras, of Nārāyaṇa with the Puruṣasūkta, and of the goddess with the Devīsūkta; then Brahmā's composition of a hymn of praise to the wooden body to protect the devotee Indradyumna; the bestowal of a boon on Indradyumna by the Lord in the wooden body; the recitation of the māhātmya of the site by the wooden body from his own mouth to the king; description of the fruits heard of recitation, gift-giving, and other rites relative to the conjunctions of months, lunar days, and so forth... 96.2

2.2.s:
30 jyeṣṭhamāse snānadānādimāhātmyavarṇanam, mārkaṇḍeyāvaṭapañcavāruṇanyagrodhanārāyaṇa
sīradhvajasyandanatrayastha dārudehaviṣṇubalabhadrasubhadrādisvargadvāra catuḥsvastikakoṇaka-
siṃdhurājādi tīrthakṣetrasthānamāhātmyavarṇanapūrvakaṃ stotrapūjādyanekavidhividhānaphala-
kathanam... 98 1
2.2.d:
30 ज्येष्ठमासे स्नानदानादिमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, मार्कण्डेयावटपञ्चवारुणन्यग्रोधनारायण
सीरध्वजस्यन्दनत्रयस्थ दारुदेहविष्णुबलभद्रसुभद्रादिस्वर्गद्वार चतुःस्वस्तिककोणक-
सिंधुराजादि तीर्थक्षेत्रस्थानमाहात्म्यवर्णनपूर्वकं स्तोत्रपूजाद्यनेकविधिविधानफल-
कथनम्... 98 1
2.2.m: 30. Description of the māhātmya of ritual ablution, gift-giving, and the like in the month of Jyeṣṭha; statement of the fruits of numerous rules for hymns of praise, worship, and the like, prefaced by a description of the māhātmya of the sacred fords, sacred fields, and abodes of the Mārkaṇḍeya-banyan, the Five Vāruṇīs, the banyan tree, Nārāyaṇa, the plow-bannered [Balarāma], the wooden bodies Viṣṇu, Balabhadra, and Subhadrā mounted on the three chariots, the gate to heaven, the four svastikas, the corners, the King of the Ocean, and so on... 98.1

2.2.s: 31 tataścendradyumnasaraḥsnānamāhātmyavarṇanapūrvakaṃ nṛsiṃhamaṃtroccāraṇena bahuphalaprāptikathanam, mañcasthitapuruṣottamadarśanamāhātmyam, jyeṣṭhamāse puruṣottamasnānamāhātmyam, puruṣottamastotrapaddhativarṇanam, puruṣottamadarśanena sveṣṭasarvaphalaprāptikathanam 101 1
2.2.d: 31 ततश्चेन्द्रद्युम्नसरःस्नानमाहात्म्यवर्णनपूर्वकं नृसिंहमंत्रोच्चारणेन बहुफलप्राप्तिकथनम्, मञ्चस्थितपुरुषोत्तमदर्शनमाहात्म्यम्, ज्येष्ठमासे पुरुषोत्तमस्नानमाहात्म्यम्, पुरुषोत्तमस्तोत्रपद्धतिवर्णनम्, पुरुषोत्तमदर्शनेन स्वेष्टसर्वफलप्राप्तिकथनम् 101 1
2.2.m: 31. And then, statement of the attainment of abundant fruit through chanting the Nṛsiṃha mantra, prefaced by a description of the māhātmya of ritual ablution in the pool of Indradyumna; the māhātmya of the darśana of Puruṣottama standing on the altar-dais; the māhātmya of ritual ablution for Puruṣottama in the month of Jyeṣṭha; description of the procedure for the hymn of praise to Puruṣottama; statement of the attainment of all desired fruits through the darśana of Puruṣottama... 101.1

2.2.s:
32 dakṣiṇāmūrtidarśanamāhātmyaphalavarṇanam, jyeṣṭhapañcakavratavarṇanam, mahājyaiṣṭhīdine jātasya puruṣottamadarśanasya phalamāhātmyavarṇanam, pañcadīpānprajvālya nṛsiṃhapūjanaṃ
vidheyamityādimāhātmyavarṇanam, jyeṣṭhapaurṇamāsyāṃ kṛtasyopoṣaṇasya kṛṣṇabalabha-
drasubhadrāpūjanasya ca phalakathanam-.. ... ... 103 1
2.2.d:
32 दक्षिणामूर्तिदर्शनमाहात्म्यफलवर्णनम्, ज्येष्ठपञ्चकव्रतवर्णनम्, महाज्यैष्ठीदिने जातस्य पुरुषोत्तमदर्शनस्य फलमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, पञ्चदीपान्प्रज्वाल्य नृसिंहपूजनं
विधेयमित्यादिमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, ज्येष्ठपौर्णमास्यां कृतस्योपोषणस्य कृष्णबलभ-
द्रसुभद्रापूजनस्य च फलकथनम्-.. ... ... 103 1
2.2.m: 32. Description of the māhātmya and fruits of the darśana of Dakṣiṇāmūrti; description of the vow of the five days of Jyeṣṭha; description of the fruits and māhātmya of the darśana of Puruṣottama occurring on the great Jyaiṣṭhī day; description of the māhātmya stating that worship of Nṛsiṃha must be performed after lighting five lamps; statement of the fruits of fasting and of worshipping Kṛṣṇa, Balabhadra, and Subhadrā on the full moon day of Jyeṣṭha... 103.1

2.2.s:
33 mahādevīmahotsabapradhānadektāpūjanasnānadānādividhimāhātmyavarṇanam, surathaṃ kṛtvā
yātrārthaṃ bhagavanmūrtiṃ sthāpayitvā tasya sīmollaṃghanādivarṇanam, rathasthaviṣṇudarśanama-
hāphalaprāptivarṇanam, mahādevīvrate puruṣottamabalabhadrasubhadrādarśanaphalavarṇanam, mahājyaiṣṭhyāṃ dārudehadarśanaphalam, sahasradīpaprajvalanamāhātmyam-.. 104 2

यात्रार्थं भगवन्मूर्तिं स्थापयित्वा तस्य सीमोल्लंघनादिवर्णनम्, रथस्थविष्णुदर्शनम-
हाफलप्राप्तिवर्णनम्, महादेवीव्रते पुरुषोत्तमबलभद्रसुभद्रादर्शनफलवर्णनम्, महाज्यैष्ठ्यां दारुदेहदर्शनफलम्, सहस्रदीपप्रज्वलनमाहात्म्यम्-.. 104 2
2.2.m: 33. Description of the rules and māhātmya of ritual ablution, gift-giving, and the like in the worship of the chief deity of the great festival of the Mahādevī; having constructed an excellent chariot, having installed the Lord’s image for the procession, description of his crossing the boundary and so forth; description of the attainment of the great fruit of seeing Viṣṇu mounted on the chariot; description of the fruit of the darśana of Puruṣottama, Balabhadra, and Subhadrā during the Mahādevī vow; the fruit of the darśana of the wooden body on the great Jyaiṣṭhī; the māhātmya of lighting a thousand lamps... 104.2

2.2.s:
34 aśvamedhāṃgasarastīrthamāhātmyavarṇanam, bindutīrthamāhātmyam, mahāvedyāṃ kṛtasya pitṛkarmaṇaḥ phalavarṇanam, indradyumnasaronṛsiṃhakṣetravanajāgaraṇatīrthahṛṣīkeśāditīrthasnāna-
dānādimāhātmyavarṇanam- ... .... .. 106 2
2.2.d:
34 अश्वमेधांगसरस्तीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, बिन्दुतीर्थमाहात्म्यम्, महावेद्यां कृतस्य पितृकर्मणः फलवर्णनम्, इन्द्रद्युम्नसरोनृसिंहक्षेत्रवनजागरणतीर्थहृषीकेशादितीर्थस्नान-
दानादिमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्- ... .... .. 106 2
2.2.m: 34. Description of the māhātmya of the sacred ford of the lake connected to the horse sacrifice; the māhātmya of the Bindu sacred ford; description of the fruit of ancestral rites performed on the great altar; description of the māhātmya of ritual ablution, gift-giving, and the like in the pool of Indradyumna, the Nṛsiṃha sacred field, the forest, the night-vigil sacred ford, Hṛṣīkeśa, and other sacred fords... 106.2
35. Account of the rites for protecting the chariot; description of the fruit of the darśana of Puruṣottama, Balabhadra, and Subhadrā standing upon it; account of the manner of praising them... 107.2

2.2.s:
36 śayanotsavavratavidhikathanam, āṣāḍhīmārabhya kārtikīparyantaṃ cāturmāsyapuṇyakāla-
varṇanam, nānāvidhapāpakṣālanārthaṃ cāturmāsye tīrthasnānapuruṣottamādikṣetradarśanaphalam, cāturmāsye grāhyāgrāhyavastuvicārakathanam, cāturmāsye dhāryaniyamānukathanam, etaccāturmāsyodbhavavratamāhātmyaśravaṇaphalam.. .-- 108 1
2.2.d:
36 शयनोत्सवव्रतविधिकथनम्, आषाढीमारभ्य कार्तिकीपर्यन्तं चातुर्मास्यपुण्यकाल-
वर्णनम्, नानाविधपापक्षालनार्थं चातुर्मास्ये तीर्थस्नानपुरुषोत्तमादिक्षेत्रदर्शनफलम्, चातुर्मास्ये ग्राह्याग्राह्यवस्तुविचारकथनम्, चातुर्मास्ये धार्यनियमानुकथनम्, एतच्चातुर्मास्योद्भवव्रतमाहात्म्यश्रवणफलम्.. .-- 108 1
2.2.m: 36. Account of the rules for the vow of the festival of sleep; description of the auspicious period of Cāturmāsya starting from the full moon day of Āṣāḍha and ending with the full moon day of Kārttika; the fruit of ritual ablution in sacred fords and the darśana of the sacred field of Puruṣottama and others in Cāturmāsya for cleansing various kinds of sin; account of the examination of permissible and forbidden substances in Cāturmāsya; account of the observances to be maintained in Cāturmāsya; the fruit of hearing the māhātmya of this vow arising in Cāturmāsya... 108.1

2.2.s:
37 karkasaṃkrāṃtyāṃ dakṣiṇāyanāraṃbhapuṇyakālaniyamakramavarṇanam, dakṣiṇāyane puruṣottama-
pūjanaphalam, puruṣottamasya daśadikṣu sthitānāṃ devānāṃ nāmanirdeśastaddarśanapūjana-
phalakathanaṃ ca, indradyumnena śatavarṣāṃte nṛharidarśanam, śvetarājenapuruṣottamanṛsiṃhayoḥ
pūjanaṃ stavanaṃ ca, bhagavatā rājñe varapradānam 109 1
2.2.d:
37 कर्कसंक्रांत्यां दक्षिणायनारंभपुण्यकालनियमक्रमवर्णनम्, दक्षिणायने पुरुषोत्तम-
पूजनफलम्, पुरुषोत्तमस्य दशदिक्षु स्थितानां देवानां नामनिर्देशस्तद्दर्शनपूजन-
फलकथनं च, इन्द्रद्युम्नेन शतवर्षांते नृहरिदर्शनम्, श्वेतराजेनपुरुषोत्तमनृसिंहयोः
पूजनं स्तवनं च, भगवता राज्ञे वरप्रदानम् 109 1
2.2.m: 37. Description of the sequence of observances for the auspicious period at the beginning of the southern transit of the sun at the Cancer equinox; the fruit of worshipping Puruṣottama during the southern transit of the sun; the mention of the names of the gods stationed in the ten directions around Puruṣottama, and the statement of the fruits of seeing and worshipping them; Indradyumna's darśana of Nṛhari at the end of a hundred years; the worship and praise of Puruṣottama and Nṛsiṃha by King Śveta; the Lord's bestowal of a boon upon the king... 109.1

2.2.s:
38 śvetarājñe varaṃ dattvā bhagavato'ntardhānam bhagavaducchiṣṭabhakṣaṇaphalakathanam, bhagava-
ttīrthaprāśananirmālyadhāraṇādiphalakathanam, kalikālanirṇayaḥ, kalau bhagavaccintanena phalaprāptivarṇanam, bhagavato dayādākṣiṇyādisvabhāvavarṇanam, kasyaciddvijasya
puruṣottamakṣetra āgamanam, dvijena saṃśayavatā bhagavaducchiṣṭamiti matvā bhagavanniveditamannaṃ naiva bhakṣitamatastasya dehapīḍāsaṃprāptikathanam, anyadvijānāṃ bhagavaducchiṣṭabhakṣaṇena devatulyakāntiprāptivṛttāntaḥ, naivedyaṃ tyaktavato dvijasyeśvaraprārthanāṃ kṛtvā saṃjātayā nṛsiṃhakṛpayā sauṃdaryaprāptikathanam, damanakadaityavināśasamaye sugaṃdhinirmitamālotpattikathanam, bhagavadbhaktapūjanapūrvakadevapūjanavidhivarṇanam, iṣṭaiḥ saha nṛsiṃhaprasādabhojanādiphalavarṇanam -. 110 1
2.2.d:
38 श्वेतराज्ञे वरं दत्त्वा भगवतोऽन्तर्धानम् भगवदुच्छिष्टभक्षणफलकथनम्, भगव-
त्तीर्थप्राशननिर्माल्यधारणादिफलकथनम्, कलिकालनिर्णयः, कलौ भगवच्चिन्तनेन फलप्राप्तिवर्णनम्, भगवतो दयादाक्षिण्यादिस्वभाववर्णनम्, कस्यचिद्द्विजस्य
पुरुषोत्तमक्षेत्र आगमनम्, द्विजेन संशयवता भगवदुच्छिष्टमिति मत्वा भगवन्निवेदितमन्नं नैव भक्षितमतस्तस्य देहपीडासंप्राप्तिकथनम्, अन्यद्विजानां भगवदुच्छिष्टभक्षणेन देवतुल्यकान्तिप्राप्तिवृत्तान्तः, नैवेद्यं त्यक्तवतो द्विजस्येश्वरप्रार्थनां कृत्वा संजातया नृसिंहकृपया सौंदर्यप्राप्तिकथनम्, दमनकदैत्यविनाशसमये सुगंधिनिर्मितमालोत्पत्तिकथनम्, भगवद्भक्तपूजनपूर्वकदेवपूजनविधिवर्णनम्, इष्टैः सह नृसिंहप्रसादभोजनादिफलवर्णनम् -. 110 1
2.2.m: 38. The Lord's disappearance after granting the boon to King Śveta; statement of the fruit of consuming the Lord’s leftover food; statement of the fruit of drinking the Lord’s water, wearing his consecrated flower-garlands, and so forth; determination of the Kali age; description of the attainment of fruits by meditating upon the Lord in the Kali age; description of the Lord's nature, such as compassion and benevolence; the arrival of a certain brahmin at the sacred field of Puruṣottama; account of the infliction of bodily affliction upon that doubting brahmin because he did not eat the food offered to the Lord, thinking it to be the Lord’s leftovers; the narrative of other brahmins attaining divine splendor by consuming the Lord’s leftovers; account of the attainment of beauty through the grace of Nṛsiṃha that arose when the brahmin who had rejected the food offering prayed to the Lord; account of the origin of the fragrant garland fashioned at the time of the destruction of the demon Damanaka; description of the rite of worshipping the deity preceded by the worship of the Lord’s devotee; description of the fruits of eating Nṛsiṃha's prasāda and so forth along with loved ones... 110.1

2.2.s:
39 dakṣiṇāmūrtidarśanena śayanotsavavratavidhānena ca sarvayātrāphalāvāptikathanam, bhaga-
vacchayanaparivartanakālakathanam, kaumudyākhyotthāpanamahotsavavidhikālakathanam,
tasminkāle bhagavatpūjāsāhityavarṇanam, pūjāphalakathanam, anayaiva pūjayā sārdha-
trikoṭitīrthābhiṣekaphalaprāptikathanam -. 112 2
2.2.d:
39 दक्षिणामूर्तिदर्शनेन शयनोत्सवव्रतविधानेन च सर्वयात्राफलावाप्तिकथनम्, भग-
वच्छयनपरिवर्तनकालकथनम्, कौमुद्याख्योत्थापनमहोत्सवविधिकालकथनम्,
तस्मिन्काले भगवत्पूजासाहित्यवर्णनम्, पूजाफलकथनम्, अनयैव पूजया सार्ध-
त्रिकोटितीर्थाभिषेकफलप्राप्तिकथनम् -. 112 2
2.2.m: 39. Statement of the attainment of the fruits of all pilgrimages through the darśana of Dakṣiṇāmūrti and the observance of the vow of the festival of sleep; account of the time of the Lord’s turning over in sleep; account of the time and rites for the great festival of awakening named Kaumudī; description of the articles of worship for the Lord at that time; statement of the fruit of worship; statement of the attainment of the fruit of ablution at three and a half million sacred fords through this very worship... 112.2
40. Account of the festival of covering on the sixth day of the bright fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa; statement of the fruit of the rites and observances of the vow of the festival of covering... 114.2
